# Reg, Onboarding and verification

# Business Registration, Sign-In & Verification

**PRD \- Business Registration, Sign-In & Verification**

# **1\. Registration**

Registration is a three-stage flow. Stage 1 (Account Setup) captures account credentials and personal data, then closes with an email verification screen. Stage 2 (Identity Verification) confirms mobile ownership and personal identity via Nafath. Stage 3 (Business Verification) confirms the business against the commercial registry and optionally collects bank account details. All three stages must be completed before platform access is granted.

## **1.1 Account Setup**

Account Setup has three screens. Screen 1 creates the account. Screen 2 collects personal and mobile data for later verification. Screen 3 instructs the user to verify their email before signing in to continue. No API calls fire during Account Setup.

### **Screen 1 \- Create Account**

| FR ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AS-1.1 | Screen collects three fields: Email Address, Password, and Confirm Password. No other fields are present. | All three fields visible and required. No additional fields on this screen. | Must Have |
| AS-1.2 | Email Address must be a valid email format and must not already be associated with an existing Qawafel account. | Standard email format validation applies. Duplicate email shows inline error: "An account with this email already exists. Sign in instead." | Must Have |
| AS-1.3 | Password must meet all five complexity rules: minimum 12 characters, at least one uppercase letter, at least one lowercase letter, at least one number, at least one special character. Password complexity is validated only when the user clicks Continue \- there is no live checklist. | Complexity rules validated on Continue click. If any rule is unmet, inline error lists the specific unmet rules. Continue does not fire while required fields are empty or format invalid. | Must Have |
| AS-1.4 | Confirm Password must exactly match the Password field. | Mismatch shown as an inline error on validation. Continue remains unavailable until both fields match and all complexity rules are met. | Must Have |
| AS-1.5 | Password show/hide toggle available on both password fields. | Eye icon on each field. Toggles between obscured and plain text. | Must Have |
| AS-1.6 | On successful submission, the account is created and an email verification link is automatically sent to the entered email address. | Account created on Continue success. Verification link sent immediately. User advances to Screen 2\. | Must Have |

# 

# Business Partner Management

 **PRD \- Business Partner Management**      

# **1\. Purpose & Scope**

This PRD defines the Business Partner Management experience on the Qawafel platform. It covers the manual addition of business partners, the Business Partners list view, the Trading Partner Record detail view, relationship management, and a complete use cases and error states reference for design and QA.

# **2\. Manual Business Partner Addition**

X Trading adds a business partner by entering the Business Partner's UNN. The platform runs a sequential lookup: internal checks first (own UNN, existing relationships, Qawafel Business Identity) in order, Saudi commercial registry API only when all internal checks find no match. UNN is the hard gate \- a business partner cannot be added without a valid UNN found in the Saudi commercial registry.

## **3.1 Entry Point**

| FR ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **FR-PA.1** | '+ Add Business Partner' button is shown in the Business Partners page header. Clicking it opens the UNN lookup. | Button visible in the page header at all times. UNN field is the only active input.  | Must Have  |

## **3.2 UNN Lookup**

The 'Check UNN' button is always active. Clicking it with an invalid UNN format shows an inline error without triggering a lookup. Clicking it with a valid UNN triggers the lookup. The lookup triggers only when X Trading clicks 'Check UNN' and never automatically. During the lookup, the button shows a spinner with the label 'Checking...', the UNN field becomes read-only, and a status text appears below the UNN field to inform X Trading that the check is in progress.

Lookup sequence: (1) Own UNN check: if the UNN matches X Trading's own business UNN, an error is shown immediately. No external check triggered. (2) Existing relationship check: if the UNN already has an active or inactive Trading Partner Relationship with X Trading, an inline message is shown. No external check triggered. (3) Qawafel Business Identity check: if the UNN belongs to a Verified Business Identity on Qawafel, the form fields become available with verified data. No Saudi commercial registry check. (4) Saudi commercial registry API: called only if none of the above match.

# **Business Registration, Onboarding, Sign-In & Access**

## **1\. Document Setup**

| Source product document | [Product PRD]() |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Status** | `Under discussion` |
| **Last updated** | `16-Jun-2026` |
| **Audience** | `Engineering, Product, Design` |
| **Owner** | `Engineering Team` |

## 

## **2\. Purpose**

This PRD defines the target business-facing registration, onboarding, sign-in, password recovery, and capability-gating model for Business Users on Qawafel.

This document is written from the resolved engineering model in the alignment document, not from the original screen-by-screen structure in the product PRD.

## **3\. Entities**

| Concept | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| User | The person who authenticates with the platform. In this PRD, the user becomes the canonical registered identity after completing user onboarding. |
| Business | The tenant business entity represented on the platform. |
| Business User | The canonical user's relationship to a business for business-surface access. |
| Business User:Owner | A `Business User` with the owner role. This notation is used throughout the PRD to distinguish the business-scoped role from the user entity. |
| Invited Business User | A user who is granted, or awaiting, business access through a `Business User:Owner` invitation. |
| Platform User | An internal platform-side user who performs business-verification review and approval actions. |

## **4\. Scope**

This PRD covers:

- guest registration with email and password signup  
- collection of user personal details during registration and onboarding continuation  
- email verification, mobile verification, and user KYC through Nafath  
- authenticated continuation of user onboarding until the user becomes a canonical registered `User`  
- onboarding of a first business by a completed user  
- onboarding of additional businesses by that same completed user  
- invitation of additional users to an existing business by a signed-in `Business User:Owner`  
- business KYB outcomes and capability gating  
- optional bank-account onboarding data and bank-verification gating  
- sign-in for existing users  
- password recovery  
- business-surface routing after authentication and onboarding checkpoints  
- in-session switching between businesses for a user linked to multiple businesses

This PRD does not cover:

- internal platform operations workflows in detail  
- `Platform User` verification tooling UX  
- authorized or delegated registrant flows  
- low-level government or bank integration contracts

## **5\. Assumptions**

The following assumptions are used to unblock this PRD and differ from, or extend beyond, the original product PRD:

- onboarding is split into user onboarding first and business onboarding second  
- primary sign-in is email and password only; sign-in OTP is not mandatory in this draft  
- personal details may be collected immediately after guest signup, before email verification completes  
- no OTP and no external verification checks are initiated when personal details are submitted during the guest portion of the flow  
- verified email is required before the user can rely on normal sign-in to continue onboarding after the signup-linked session ends  
- mobile uniqueness is treated as a verified-user policy in this draft rather than a guest-form-entry rule  
- Nafath verifies the user for KYC; it does not by itself complete business verification  
- successful email verification, mobile verification, and Nafath KYC establish the canonical registered `User`  
- a completed user can onboard one or more businesses without repeating user-level verification for each business  
- core business verification uses authoritative UNN-based business data during business onboarding after the user has completed user-level onboarding  
- the registrant must be the legal business owner for each business they onboard directly  
- when a user onboards a business, that user receives `Business User:Owner` access for that business only after the platform confirms the user's verified identity matches the legal owner of that business  
- business-user invitation by a signed-in `Bu siness User:Owner` is treated as part of the broader onboarding flow and is covered by this PRD  
- IBAN is in onboarding scope after business verification but is optional and non-blocking for business access  
- invited users must complete personal-details capture and mobile verification before their business access becomes active  
- whether invited users must also complete Nafath KYC before business access becomes active remains a product decision in this PRD  
- multi-business selection and switching UX are in scope for users linked to more than one business  
- no in-app business notifications are in scope; auth-required delivery such as mobile OTP and email verification links remain in scope  
- password recovery uses an email-link reset flow

## **6\. Journey Overview**

### 6.1 Verification checkpoints

| Checkpoint | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| Email verification | Confirms the user controls the registered email address and enables normal sign-in-based onboarding continuation. |
| Mobile verification | Confirms the user controls the registered mobile number. In this flow, it begins during forced onboarding continuation if the mobile is still unverified. |
| User KYC | Confirms the user's identity through Nafath and completes user-level onboarding. |
| Business KYB | Confirms business-level identity and eligibility. In this draft, core business identity verification is based on authoritative UNN-linked business data during business onboarding. |
| Bank verification | Confirms the submitted bank account for payout enablement as an optional post-business-verification checkpoint. |

### 6.2 Onboarding model

- Registration is the guest phase of the journey and begins with email and password signup.  
- User onboarding covers personal-details capture, email verification, mobile verification, and Nafath KYC.  
- Authentication belongs to the user.  
- Business-surface access belongs to the `Business User` relationship and the verification state of each business.  
- Email verification begins immediately after the user submits email and password during registration, but it does not block in-flow personal-details capture while the signup continuation path remains valid.  
- Personal-details submission during the guest phase must not itself start OTP delivery, Nafath verification, or business verification.  
- After successful email verification, mobile verification, and Nafath KYC, the platform treats the person as the canonical registered `User`.  
- A completed user can then onboard one or more businesses.  
- For each onboarded business, the onboarding user becomes `Business User:Owner` only after the platform confirms the user's verified identity matches the business's legal owner record.  
- UNN-based business verification must not begin during anonymous guest submission and must instead begin during business onboarding by a completed user.  
- Invitation extends access to an existing business through the `Business User` relationship and is not itself a business-creation flow.  
- Invited users must complete personal-details capture and mobile verification before business access becomes active.  
- If a user is linked to more than one business, the app must support switching the active business context from within the business surface.

### 6.3 User onboarding flow

![][image1]

1. A guest starts registration by submitting email and password.  
2. The platform immediately sends an email-verification link and presents the personal-details step.  
3. The guest may submit user-level personal details including National ID / Iqama, mobile number, and date of birth before email verification completes.  
4. Personal-details submission during this guest-stage flow does not start OTP delivery, Nafath verification, or business verification.  
5. Verified email is required before the user can rely on normal sign-in to resume onboarding after the signup-linked session ends.  
6. After sign-in, the platform must keep the user in onboarding until user-level onboarding is complete.  
7. If personal details were not previously captured, the user must complete them before moving forward.  
8. If the mobile number is still unverified, the platform begins OTP delivery and requires mobile confirmation at this stage.  
9. After mobile confirmation, the platform begins Nafath KYC.  
10. Successful Nafath completion establishes the canonical registered `User`.

Capability unlocked at this stage: `Can onboard a business`.

### 6.4 Business onboarding flow

![][image2]

1. A completed canonical `User` can start business onboarding for a first business or an additional business.  
2. The user submits business details for the target business.  
3. The platform begins UNN-based business verification for that business.  
4. The platform must confirm that the authenticated user's verified identity matches the legal owner of the business before owner access can be granted.  
5. On successful business verification and owner-identity match, the platform grants the `User` access to the verified `Business`.  
6. The user who onboarded the business receives `Business User:Owner` access for that business.  
7. Business-scoped app access opens for that business after verification succeeds and owner identity is confirmed.  
8. After business access opens, the platform may continue to optional IBAN capture, and the user may either provide bank details or navigate away.

Capability unlocked at this stage: `Business verified / app access opens`.

### 6.5 Business user invitation flow

1. A signed-in `Business User:Owner` starts an invite flow for an existing business.  
2. The `Business User:Owner` provides the email address of the user to invite.  
3. If the email matches an existing user account, the platform creates a pending business-access link for that `User` and sends an email informing them that access is waiting on required activation steps.  
4. If the email does not match an existing user account, the platform sends an invitation email with an account-creation link tied to the business invitation.  
5. The invited person must complete required personal details and mobile verification before the pending business access becomes active.  
6. If the invited person does not yet have an account, they must first create one through the invitation path and then complete the same required activation steps before business access becomes active.  
7. Whether invited users must also complete Nafath KYC before business access becomes active remains a product decision in this PRD.

### 6.6 Existing user sign-in journey

1. The user signs in with email and password.  
2. If user onboarding is incomplete, the platform keeps the user in onboarding continuation.  
3. If user onboarding is complete and the user has exactly one eligible business context, the platform takes the user directly to that business experience.  
4. If user onboarding is complete and the user has access to multiple businesses, the platform must let the user choose and switch business context from within the app.

### 6.7 Password recovery journey

1. The user requests password reset using their email address.  
2. The platform sends a reset link if the email corresponds to an eligible account.  
3. The user sets a new password through the reset link.  
4. Existing sessions are revoked after a successful password reset.

## **7\. Capability Tiers**

This section is the authoritative capability unlock model for this PRD pass.

| Capability stage | Trigger | Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| User capability \- Can onboard a business | The user completes email verification, mobile verification, and Nafath KYC. | The user becomes the canonical registered `User` and can onboard a first business or additional businesses. |
| Business User capability \- Business verified / app access opens | The canonical user submits business details for a specific business, automated UNN-based business verification succeeds for that business, and the platform confirms the user's verified identity matches the legal owner of that business. | Business-scoped app access opens for that business through the `Business User` relationship. The user who onboarded that business becomes `Business User:Owner` for that business. |
| Business capability \- IBAN checkpoint completed | The business has submitted IBAN details that satisfy the platform's required validation and verification checkpoint for payout-related readiness. | A distinct business capability stage tied to the verified IBAN checkpoint is recorded. The exact product capability unlocked by this stage remains an open product question in this PRD. |

IBAN remains an optional follow-on step after business verification and does not block business access.

## **8\. Implementation Tickets**

Requirement provenance legend for this section:

- `FR-P-*` requirements are derived from the source product PRD in `docs/prds/business_onboarding.md`, even where this engineering PRD has regrouped or renamed them.  
- `FR-E-*` requirements are introduced or materially extended in this engineering PRD to support the resolved engineering model.

### 8.1 T1: Registration Start

**Goal**

Allow a guest user to start registration with email and password and move immediately into the onboarding journey.

**Stories**

- As a guest user, I can start registration so I can begin onboarding.  
- As a registrant, I can provide my credentials so I can securely continue onboarding.  
- As a registrant, I receive an email-verification link after creating my credentials so I can verify my account without blocking my immediate onboarding progress.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Email-and-password signup starts the journey.  
- The platform sends a verification email immediately after signup.  
- The user can continue into the onboarding journey without waiting for email verification while the signup-linked session remains valid.  
- Invalid credentials at future sign-in remain generic and do not reveal account-existence details.

**Requirements**

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-P-001 | Registration start must collect an email address and password credentials. |
| FR-P-002 | Email must use standard email validation and must be unique at the `User` level. |
| FR-P-003 | Registration must capture a password and password confirmation. |
| FR-P-004 | Passwords must require at least 12 characters, one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character. |
| FR-P-005 | Confirm-password mismatch must be shown inline. |
| FR-P-006 | Password visibility toggles must be available on password fields. |
| FR-P-007 | After the user submits email and password during registration, the platform must send an email-verification link to the registered email address. |
| FR-P-008 | Email verification must not block continued progress through the signup-linked onboarding flow while the signup continuation path remains valid. |

### 

### 8.2 T2: Personal Details

**Goal**

Collect required user-level personal details as part of onboarding without prematurely starting later verification checkpoints.

**Stories**

- As a registrant, I can provide my personal details so my onboarding can continue.  
- As a registrant, I can submit personal details before email verification completes.

**Acceptance criteria**

- User-level personal details can be collected before email verification completes.  
- Personal-details submission does not start OTP delivery.  
- Personal-details submission does not start Nafath verification.  
- Personal-details submission does not start business verification.

**Requirements**

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-P-009 | User-level personal details in this journey must collect National ID / Iqama, Date of Birth, and mobile number. |
| FR-P-010 | National ID / Iqama must accept a 10-digit Saudi National ID starting with `1` or a 10-digit Iqama starting with `2`. |
| FR-P-011 | Date of birth must be captured as a valid `DD/MM/YYYY` date. |
| FR-P-012 | Mobile number must use Saudi format with a read-only `+966` prefix and a local number beginning with `5`. |
| FR-P-013 | Personal-details submission must not start OTP delivery, Nafath verification, or business verification. |
| FR-P-014 | Continue actions must remain gated by required-field validity. |
| FR-P-015 | Registration copy must include guidance that submitted details must match official documents exactly. |

### 

### 8.3 T3: Onboarding Continuation

**Goal**

Ensure incomplete users continue onboarding after sign-in until user-level onboarding is complete.

**Stories**

- As an existing user with incomplete onboarding, I am kept in onboarding until I finish the required user-level steps.  
- As an existing user, I can return after email verification and resume onboarding from the correct next step.

**Acceptance criteria**

- If user onboarding is incomplete, sign-in returns the user to onboarding continuation.  
- If personal details are still missing, the user must complete them before moving forward.

**Requirements**

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-E-001 | Verified email is required before the user can rely on normal sign-in to continue onboarding after the signup-linked session ends. |
| FR-E-002 | After successful email verification, the user must be able to use normal sign-in to resume onboarding and other eligible account flows. |
| FR-E-003 | If user onboarding is incomplete, sign-in must return the user to onboarding continuation rather than to a completed business experience. |
| FR-E-004 | If required personal details are still missing, the user must complete them before moving to later onboarding checkpoints. |

### 

### 8.4 T4: Mobile Verification

**Goal**

Confirm control of the registered mobile number during onboarding continuation.

**Stories**

- As a registrant, I can complete mobile verification so the platform can confirm I control the registered mobile number.

**Acceptance criteria**

- If the user's mobile number is still unverified during onboarding continuation, the platform begins OTP delivery.  
- Mobile confirmation is required before the user can move to Nafath KYC.  
- In-scope OTP flows follow the shared 6-digit, countdown, resend, and expiry contract.

**Requirements**

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-P-016 | Mobile verification flows that remain in scope must use a 6-digit OTP. |
| FR-P-017 | OTP entry screens must show a 3-minute countdown. |
| FR-P-018 | Resend must become available after 60 seconds and must be limited to 3 resend attempts per active code window. |
| FR-P-019 | Incorrect OTP entry must return an inline error and clear the field for re-entry. |
| FR-P-020 | Expired OTP must invalidate the current code and prompt regeneration or resend. |
| FR-P-021 | Mobile confirmation must be completed before the user can move to Nafath KYC. |

### 

### 8.5 T5: Nafath KYC

**Goal**

Complete user-level identity verification and establish the canonical registered `User`.

**Stories**

- As a registrant, I can complete Nafath verification so the platform can confirm my identity.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Nafath starts only after the required user-level prerequisites are complete.  
- Nafath exposes clear terminal states and deterministic next actions.  
- Successful completion of user onboarding unlocks the ability to onboard a first business or additional businesses.

**Requirements**

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-P-022 | Nafath user KYC must begin automatically when the user reaches the identity-verification checkpoint. |
| FR-P-023 | The Nafath screen must show the returned 2-digit number, a 3-minute countdown, and a CTA to open the Nafath app. |
| FR-P-024 | Nafath initiation failure must return an inline retry path. |
| FR-P-025 | Nafath success, rejection, and timeout states must produce deterministic next actions for the user. |
| FR-P-026 | Successful user KYC must establish the canonical registered `User`. |
| FR-P-027 | Successful user KYC must unlock the ability to onboard a first business or additional businesses. |

### 

### 8.6 T6: Business Onboarding

**Goal**

Allow a completed user to onboard a first business or additional businesses using the business verification flow.

**Stories**

- As a completed user, I can onboard my first business so I can gain business access.  
- As a completed user, I can onboard an additional business without repeating user-level verification.  
- As a registrant, I can submit my business data for review so the platform can determine which capabilities may unlock.

**Acceptance criteria**

- A completed user can submit business details for one or more businesses.  
- Each business goes through its own business verification flow.  
- User-level verification is not repeated for each new business.  
- Successful business verification and owner-identity match open business-scoped app access for that business.  
- Successful business verification and owner-identity match create the business-user role record required for that business.  
- The onboarding user receives `Business User:Owner` access for that business after owner identity is confirmed.

**Requirements**

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-E-005 | A completed user must be able to onboard a first business and additional businesses without repeating user-level verification. |
| FR-P-028 | Business onboarding must collect Unified National Number (UNN), VAT Registration Number, and optional Tax Identification Number (TIN). |
| FR-P-029 | UNN must accept a 10-digit number starting with `7`. |
| FR-P-030 | VAT Registration Number must accept a 15-digit number starting and ending with `3`. |
| FR-P-031 | TIN is optional in this journey and is stored as submitted if provided. |
| FR-P-032 | The business legal name in Arabic must be derived from authoritative business data and treated as the canonical legal name for the business. |
| FR-P-033 | UNN-based business verification must not begin during anonymous guest submission. |
| FR-E-006 | During business onboarding by a completed user, the platform must use the submitted UNN to review authoritative business identity data for business verification. This automated business-verification assumption is borrowed from `docs/prds/business_trading_partner.md` and is not fully specified in the source onboarding PRD. |
| FR-E-007 | Deferring UNN-based business verification until authenticated onboarding must be treated as an anti-abuse control to reduce random guest-form submissions against external business-data services and to tie lookup usage to an identified user session. |
| FR-E-008 | A business onboarding flow may only be initiated and completed by a user who is the legal owner of that business. |
| FR-E-009 | Before granting `Business User:Owner` access, the platform must confirm that the authenticated user's verified identity matches the legal owner information returned or referenced by the authoritative business data source. |
| FR-E-009a | On successful business verification and owner-identity confirmation, the platform must create the `Business User` relationship record for that `User` and `Business` in the system with the `Owner` role before business access is activated. |
| FR-E-010 | The onboarding user must receive `Business User:Owner` access for the onboarded business by default. |
| FR-E-011 | Authorized or delegated registrant flows are out of scope and must not be implicitly supported in product requirements or user-facing flow definitions. |
| FR-E-012 | Successful business verification and owner-identity confirmation must open business-scoped app access for that business. |
| FR-E-013 | The capability model for this journey must follow the three stages defined in Section 7 and must not collapse them into a single generic verified state. |
| FR-E-014 | User-facing status labels and implementation logic for business verification and access must reflect the stage-based capability model defined in Section 7\. |

### 

### 8.7 T7: Optional Bank Details

**Goal**

Allow bank details to be provided after business access opens without blocking immediate business access.

**Stories**

- As a registrant, I can optionally provide bank details during onboarding so later bank-dependent capabilities can be enabled without blocking my core access.

**Acceptance criteria**

- IBAN can be requested after business verification.  
- Bank details remain optional for immediate business access.  
- The user may provide bank details later if they navigate away.

**Requirements**

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-P-034 | After business access opens, onboarding must allow the user to enter Bank Name and IBAN. |
| FR-P-035 | Bank Name must be chosen from the supported bank list. |
| FR-P-036 | Saudi IBAN format must be validated as `SA` followed by 22 digits before bank verification can proceed. |
| FR-P-037 | If one of Bank Name or IBAN is provided, both must be completed before submission. |
| FR-P-038 | An explicit skip path must allow the user to continue without saving partial bank data. |
| FR-P-039 | Bank details are optional for immediate business access. |
| FR-E-015 | Completion of the IBAN checkpoint must be tracked as a distinct business capability stage separate from business access. |
| FR-E-016 | The IBAN checkpoint stage must not block the earlier business-access stage from remaining available. |

### 

### 8.8 T8: Business User Invitation

**Goal**

Allow `Business User:Owner` to invite other users to an existing business by email.

**Stories**

- As a `Business User:Owner`, I can invite another user to my business by email so they can gain access to the same business.  
- As an invited person who does not yet have an account, I can receive an invitation email with an account-creation link so I can create my user account and receive access to the business.  
- As an existing `User`, I can receive an invitation to an additional business and complete the required activation steps so I can access that business.

**Acceptance criteria**

- `Business User:Owner` can invite by email.  
- Existing users receive a pending business-access invitation and are informed by email.  
- New users receive an invitation email with an account-creation path.  
- Invited users must complete personal details and mobile verification before business access becomes active.  
- When an invite becomes active, the platform creates or activates the corresponding business-user access record in the system.  
- New users receive business access only after completing account creation and the required activation steps from the invitation flow.

**Requirements**

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-E-017 | A signed-in `Business User:Owner` must be able to invite additional users to the same business by providing an email address. |
| FR-E-018 | The invitation flow must operate at the business-access association level and must not treat the invite action as onboarding a separate business. |
| FR-E-019 | If the invited email already belongs to an existing `User`, the platform must create a pending access association for that user and send an email informing them of the required activation steps. |
| FR-E-020 | If the invited email does not yet belong to an existing `User`, the platform must send an invitation email containing a business-linked account-creation path. |
| FR-E-021 | Invited users must complete required personal-details capture and mobile verification before business access becomes active. |
| FR-E-022 | After a not-yet-registered invited person completes account creation through the invitation flow, the platform must keep business access pending until the required activation steps are complete. |
| FR-E-022a | When invited business access becomes active, the platform must create or activate the corresponding `Business User` relationship record for that `User` and `Business` in the system before the invited user can enter the business context. |
| FR-E-023 | Invitation emails must identify the inviting business context clearly enough for the recipient to understand which business access is being granted or requested. |
| FR-E-024 | This PRD defines invitation authority only for a signed-in `Business User:Owner`. Broader roles-and-permissions behavior for non-owner invite authority is out of scope. |

### 

### 8.9 T9: Sign-In

**Goal**

Provide a consistent sign-in experience for both incomplete users and users who already have business access.

**Stories**

- As an existing user, I can sign in with my email and password so I can access the correct next experience.  
- As an existing user, I can be taken to the correct next experience based on my onboarding and business-access state.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Email and password sign-in works without mandatory OTP.  
- Invalid credentials remain generic.  
- Incomplete users are kept in onboarding continuation.  
- Completed users with one eligible business are taken directly to that business experience.  
- Completed users with access to multiple businesses can switch active business context from within the app.

**Requirements**

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-P-040 | Sign-in must use email and password as the primary authentication flow. |
| FR-P-041 | Invalid credentials must return a generic error that does not reveal whether the email exists or the password is wrong. |
| FR-P-042 | Mandatory OTP is not part of the default sign-in flow in this PRD. |
| FR-P-043 | The next post-sign-in experience must depend on the user's onboarding state and eligible business context. |
| FR-P-044 | If the user has exactly one eligible business context, sign-in may route directly into that business context. |
| FR-P-045 | If the user has access to multiple businesses, the app must support switching the active business context from within the business surface. |
| FR-E-025 | Routing outcomes must reflect the stage-based capability model defined in Section 7\. |

### 

### 8.10 T10: Password Recovery

**Goal**

Allow users to securely recover access through an email-based password reset flow.

**Stories**

- As a user who forgot my password, I can request a reset securely so I can regain access to my account.  
- As a user resetting my password, I can set a compliant new password so my account remains secure.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Forgot-password begins with email-only request.  
- The request response uses account-safe messaging.  
- If eligible, the platform sends a reset-password link.  
- The reset flow allows the user to set a new compliant password.  
- Existing sessions are revoked after successful password reset.

**Requirements**

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-P-046 | Password recovery must begin with email entry only. |
| FR-P-047 | The reset request response must use account-existence-safe messaging. |
| FR-P-048 | If the account is eligible, the platform must send a reset-password link to the registered email address. |
| FR-P-049 | Password-reset screens must enforce the same password rules as registration. |
| FR-P-050 | A successful password reset must revoke existing user sessions. |
| FR-P-051 | Invalid or expired reset links must return the user to the forgot-password path with a clear error message. |

### 

### co8.11 Cross-Cutting Journey Communications

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-E-026 | No in-app business-state notifications are required for this journey. |
| FR-E-027 | Auth-required communications such as mobile OTP, email verification links, invitation emails, and reset delivery remain in scope where their related flows are in scope. |
| FR-E-028 | Completion acknowledgement may be shown in-product without requiring separate outbound business-state notifications. |

These recommendations are intentionally out of current implementation scope unless product explicitly pulls them into scope later.

| Recommendation ID | Recommendation | Why it may matter later | Current scope |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| PR-1 | Keep user KYC reusable across multiple businesses for the same user, with personal data such as date of birth owned at the user level rather than re-entered for each business onboarding flow. | Reduces repeated KYC and repeated entry for the same user across multiple businesses. | future enhancement |
| PR-2 | Consider a broader roles-and-permissions capability beyond basic owner-role identification once non-owner Business User actions need finer access control. | Prevents future permission drift as more business-scoped capabilities are added. | future enhancement |
| PR-3 | Document richer multi-business edge cases such as one verified business and one pending business or starting a second business while already active in another. | Helps future scope avoid implicit behavior and inconsistent routing beyond the in-scope switching baseline. | future enhancement |
| PR-4 | Allow authorized representatives of a business to register the business in a future enhancement, while providing both their own details and the owner details required for the business, with KYC flows defined for both users where policy requires it. | Expands onboarding beyond owner-only actor scope and avoids blocking legitimate delegated registration journeys. | future enhancement |

# Business Trading Partner Management

# **opBusiness Trading Partner Management** 

# **PRD Alignment document from Engineering Team**

## **1\. Document Setup**

| Title | `Business Trading Partner Management` |
| :---- | :---- |
| Companion concept note | [Business Trading Partner Concept Note](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1PFxKLHstI1tVcyJ-TA9aPOOnciwogCwgS25B7-7NNmY/edit?pli=1&tab=t.4am7vslx3884) |
| Related dependency document | [Business Registration, Onboarding, Sign-In & Access](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1PFxKLHstI1tVcyJ-TA9aPOOnciwogCwgS25B7-7NNmY/edit?pli=1&tab=t.t9mr6e8ul2b6) |
| Last updated | `2026-06-29` |
| Audience | `Engineering, Product, Design, QA` |

## **2\. Purpose**

This PRD defines the default business-surface trading partner experience for eligible `Business User`s on Apex.

It is the base engineering PRD for:

- resolving a target Business by `UNN`  
- creating or reusing one canonical `Business`  
- publishing authoritative business identity data returned by the `KYB API service`  
- creating and managing directional `Trading Partner Relationship`s  
- deriving reciprocal relationship state when both Businesses independently create their respective directional relationships through the standard `Add to network` flow without collapsing them into one shared record  
- managing relationship-local contact, address, notes and active or inactive state  
- presenting business profile, onboarding and discrepancy state  
- preserving continuity when a counterparty-added business later onboards directly

This PRD does not define transaction creation, transaction visibility, transaction sharing, historical transaction population or financial posting between Businesses. Those behaviours belong to a separate transaction-domain contract.

Creating, activating, inactivating or establishing the reverse direction of a `Trading Partner Relationship` must not, by itself, create, copy, backfill, hide, delete or otherwise alter transaction records.

The default authoritative `Add to network` path intentionally narrows the source Product PRD. It does not collect source-Business-authored Business Identity fields or create a source-authored `Business Profile Claim`. It publishes only approved authoritative identity returned by the KYB path and then permits relationship-local enrichment. Any source-authored Business identity submission belongs to the Extended PRD.

### 2.1 Requirement provenance

- `TP-P-*` requirements preserve or materially reframe the source Product PRD.  
- Companion product tickets and their acceptance criteria define the product-facing ticket slices for this initiative.  
- `TP-INV-*` requirements are domain invariants that every ticket must preserve.

## **3\. Scope And Functional Boundaries**

### 3.1 In scope

This PRD covers:

- `Add to network` eligibility for `BU:Owner` and `BU:Admin`  
- explicit `UNN` validation and internal resolution  
- self-add and duplicate-relationship prevention  
- reuse of an existing canonical `Business`  
- authoritative `KYB API service` lookup when no canonical `Business` exists  
- canonical `Business` creation from authoritative data  
- immediate publication of an authoritative `Business Identity` with profile status `verified`  
- initial onboarding status `pending_onboarding` for a counterparty-added business  
- outbound directional relationship creation  
- reciprocal relationship recognition when the target Business later adds the source Business through the same normal flow  
- Business network list, search and supported filters  
- trading partner detail composition  
- relationship-local contact, address and notes management  
- directional `active` and `inactive` state management  
- business profile status and business onboarding status presentation  
- discrepancy presentation, review and alignment to published truth on the business surface  
- direct onboarding continuity for an existing counterparty-added business  
- concurrency, uniqueness and idempotency requirements for canonical business and relationship creation

### 3.2 Out of scope

This PRD does not cover:

- user registration, sign-in, password recovery or user KYC  
- detailed direct business onboarding screens and verification mechanics  
- manual business-user fallback after a failed authoritative lookup  
- `Platform User` manual creation, correction or publication workflows  
- `Minimal Business`, unpublished profile and provisional publication rules  
- invoice import, bulk upload, enrichment or TIN-only matching  
- transaction creation, import, visibility, mirroring, sharing or historical population across Businesses  
- accounting, ledger posting, settlement, reconciliation or underwriting behaviour  
- notification delivery through inbox, email, push or SMS  
- exceptional identity merge, separation or relationship reassignment  
- low-level database schema, external-provider transport details or infrastructure topology  
- exact UI copy

### 3.3 Cross-document ownership

| Concern | Base Trading Partner PRD | Onboarding PRD |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Default `UNN` and authoritative KYB flow | Owns | Provides shared verification assumptions |
| Canonical `Business` reuse | Owns normal path | Reuses during direct onboarding |
| Manual fallback | Excludes | Excludes |
| Minimal Business | Excludes | Excludes |
| Provisional or unpublished publication | Presentation only | May consume |
| Outbound directional relationship | Owns | Excludes |
| Optional inbound-request workflow | Excludes | May consume after access opens if Product enables the extension |
| Reciprocal relationship | Owns derived reciprocal state when both directions exist | Excludes |
| Relationship-local edit | Owns | Excludes |
| Platform correction and exceptional removal | Excludes | Excludes |
| Direct onboarding linkage to existing Business | Defines continuity contract | Owns onboarding execution |
| Published identity replacement after claims review | Presentation contract only | Owns onboarding-originated submission and review contract |

## **4\. Domain Language And Truth Model**

### 4.1 Entities

| Concept | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| `User` | A person who authenticates with the platform. |
| `Business` | The canonical real-world business entity and business-surface tenant. Exact `UNN` is the primary identity anchor in this PRD. |
| `Business User` (`BU`) | The association granting a `User` access to a `Business`. |
| `BU:Admin` | A `Business User` allowed to manage trading partners for the business. |
| `BU:Owner` | A `Business User` with owner authority. `BU:Owner` may perform all trading-partner actions available to `BU:Admin`. |
| `Current Business` | The business context through which the signed-in user is acting. |
| `Business Identity` | The published counterparty-visible projection of a canonical `Business`. It is not the canonical business record itself. |
| `Business profile status` | The trust status of the published `Business Identity`. Values relevant to this PRD are `verified`, `provisional` and `unpublished`. The latter two are produced only by extended flows. |
| `Business onboarding status` | The owner-claim and access lifecycle of the canonical `Business`: `pending_onboarding` or `onboarded`. |
| `Trading Partner Relationship` | A directional association from a source `Business` to a target `Business`. It owns source-business-local relationship data and state. |
| `Reciprocal connection` | A derived view produced when both directional `Trading Partner Relationship`s exist. It is not a third shared relationship record. |
| `Business Profile Claim` | Append-only business-level evidence submitted by onboarding, extended, import or operational workflows. The default authoritative add path does not create a source-business-authored claim. |
| `Business Data Discrepancy` | A recorded conflict between a business-level claim and the currently published `Business Identity`. The workflow that creates the claim owns discrepancy production. When a previously unpublished or `provisional` Business later becomes published as `verified`, the publication-owning workflow must trigger retroactive discrepancy evaluation for existing directional relationships. This PRD owns business-surface presentation and alignment to published truth. |
| `KYB API service` | The authoritative business-verification service abstraction used to resolve a new `UNN`. A valid response may contain authoritative business data or a business-level error result. |

### 4.2 Truth views

| Truth view | Audience | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Published truth | Counterparties and normal Business-surface readers | The currently published `Business Identity`. |
| Business-owned working truth | The Business submitting, onboarding or correcting its own information | Pending `Business Profile Claim`s, onboarding submissions and correction state. |
| Relationship-local truth | Users acting through the source `Business` of a directional `Trading Partner Relationship` | Contact details, address, notes, tags and active or inactive state belonging only to that relationship. |
| Internal operational truth | Authorised Platform Users | Complete `Business`, claim, evidence, publication, discrepancy, review and correction history. |

### 

### 4.3 Status families

| Status family | Values | Owner |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Business profile status | `verified`, `provisional`, `unpublished` | Business publication workflow |
| Business onboarding status | `pending_onboarding`, `onboarded` | Onboarding workflow |
| Directional relationship state | `active`, `inactive` | Source business |
| Business discrepancy state | `open`, `resolved` | Business-surface action state derived from claim-producing workflows |
| Reciprocal state | Derived from both directional relationships | Read model, not persisted as a shared relationship |

Rules:

1. Business discrepancy state `resolved` means no further Business-surface action is required.  
2. `resolved` does not imply deletion, correction or invalidation of the originating evidence.  
3. Internal evidence disposition remains owned by the claim-producing workflow or operational workflow, not by the normal Business surface.

### 

### 4.4 Product-facing state interpretation

| Domain composition | Product-facing interpretation |
| :---- | :---- |
| `verified` \+ `pending_onboarding` | Authoritative Business identity exists but the owner has not completed onboarding. |
| `verified` \+ `onboarded` | Authoritative Business identity exists and Business access is active. |
| `provisional` \+ `pending_onboarding` | Extended-flow provisional identity exists with explicit provenance. |
| `unpublished` \+ `pending_onboarding` | Canonical Business exists but has no normal counterparty-visible profile. |

Product-facing labels must be mapped from the complete state composition. They must not be inferred from one status in isolation.

## **5\. Domain Invariants**

The following invariants apply to every flow and ticket in this PRD.

| ID | Invariant |
| :---- | :---- |
| `TP-INV-001` | An exact `UNN` resolves to at most one canonical `Business`. |
| `TP-INV-002` | A directional `Trading Partner Relationship` is unique for a `(source_business_id, target_business_id)` pair. |
| `TP-INV-003` | A `Business` cannot create a directional relationship to itself. |
| `TP-INV-004` | The two directions between a pair of businesses remain separate relationship records. |
| `TP-INV-005` | Reciprocal connection is derived from the existence and state of the two directional relationships. No shared reciprocal relationship row is created. |
| `TP-INV-006` | Relationship-local fields never modify the published `Business Identity`. |
| `TP-INV-007` | In the default authoritative path, adding a target Business does not create a source-business-authored `Business Profile Claim`. |
| `TP-INV-008` | Business-level claims are append-only and do not overwrite published truth directly. |
| `TP-INV-009` | Business profile status and business onboarding status remain separate dimensions. |
| `TP-INV-010` | A counterparty-added business created from authoritative data may be `verified` and `pending_onboarding` at the same time. |
| `TP-INV-011` | Later direct onboarding reuses the existing canonical `Business` for the same `UNN`. |
| `TP-INV-012` | Established relationships are not hard-deleted through the normal business surface. |
| `TP-INV-013` | Inactivating one directional relationship does not mutate the opposite-direction relationship. |
| `TP-INV-014` | A later reverse-direction add uses the same directional uniqueness, self-add and canonical Business invariants as the initial add. |
| `TP-INV-015` | Reciprocal state is derived automatically whenever the second directional relationship is created or either direction changes active state. No separate reciprocity action or shared reciprocal row exists. |
| `TP-INV-016` | Creating, activating, inactivating or establishing the reverse direction of a `Trading Partner Relationship` does not by itself create, copy, backfill, hide, delete or modify transaction records. |
| `TP-INV-017` | Concurrent attempts to create the same canonical Business or directional relationship resolve idempotently to one canonical record. |
| `TP-INV-018` | Published identity changes only through an authoritative update or approved publication workflow. |
| `TP-INV-019` | The default add flow never silently falls back to manual business identity entry. |
| `TP-INV-020` | Platform and business-surface actions that change durable state are auditable with actor, timestamp and outcome. |
| `TP-INV-021` | An inactive directional relationship is excluded from ordinary business-network browse and search. It may surface only through direct authorised access, an existing record or transaction context, or `Add to network` resolution for the same Business. |
| `TP-INV-022` | Reactivating a directional relationship updates the same row and does not create a second row or imply a reverse relationship. |
| `TP-INV-023` | When a previously unpublished or `provisional` Business becomes published as `verified`, the publication-owning workflow must trigger retroactive discrepancy evaluation across existing directional relationships pointing to that Business. This PRD consumes and presents the resulting discrepancy state. |
| `TP-INV-024` | Starting, resuming or correcting a Business onboarding application does not change Business onboarding status. The Business remains `pending_onboarding` until onboarding completes successfully. |
| `TP-INV-025` | Creating a directional `Trading Partner Relationship` does not notify the target Business, create a request or expose the source Business in the target Business's network. |
| `TP-INV-026` | A one-way directional relationship does not make the source Business automatically visible in the target Business's network or browse results. The target resolves the source only through an authorised independent lookup or another explicitly approved Product feature. |
| `TP-INV-027` | The default authoritative add flow does not collect source-Business-authored Business Identity values or create a source-authored Business Profile Claim. Source-authored identity submissions use the Extended PRD. |

## **6\. Field Ownership And Edit Rules**

| Field or state | Stored on | Editable in default business surface | Published to counterparties | Creates claim |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `UNN` | `Business` | No | Yes | No |
| Legal business name | `Business Identity` | No | Yes | No |
| Commercial name returned by KYB | `Business Identity` | No | Yes | No |
| VAT number returned by KYB | `Business Identity` | No | Yes | No |
| Business profile status | Publication state | No | Yes | No |
| Business onboarding status | `Business` lifecycle | No | Yes where relevant | No |
| Relationship email | `Trading Partner Relationship` | Yes | No | No |
| Relationship phone | `Trading Partner Relationship` | Yes | No | No |
| Relationship national address | `Trading Partner Relationship` | Yes | No | No |
| Relationship notes | `Trading Partner Relationship` | Yes | No | No |
| Directional active or inactive state | `Trading Partner Relationship` | `BU:Owner` or `BU:Admin` | No | No |
| Manual fallback identity values | `Business Profile Claim` | Extended flow only | Subject to publication rules | Yes |
| Onboarding identity values | `Business Profile Claim` | Onboarding flow only | Subject to publication rules | Yes |

## **7\. Access And Capability Model**

| ID | Capability | Preconditions | Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `CAP-TP-001` | View Business network | User has business-surface access to the `Current Business`. | User can view relationships permitted by their role. |
| `CAP-TP-002` | Create outbound relationship | User is `BU:Owner` or `BU:Admin` and the `Current Business` has reached `Business User capability - Business onboarded / app access opens`. | User can enter `Add to network`. |
| `CAP-TP-003` | Edit relationship-local data | User has edit rights for the `Current Business`. | User can edit relationship contact, address and notes. |
| `CAP-TP-004` | Change relationship state | User is `BU:Owner` or `BU:Admin`. | User can mark the directional relationship active or inactive. |

## **8\. State Models**

### 8.1 Business profile and onboarding composition

| Profile status | Onboarding status | Valid in this model | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `verified` | `pending_onboarding` | Yes | Authoritative profile is published but the owner has not started onboarding. |
| `verified` | `onboarded` | Yes | Authoritative profile is published and business access is active. |
| `provisional` | `pending_onboarding` | Extended flow only | A non-authoritative profile is published before owner onboarding. |
| `unpublished` | Any | Extended flow only | The canonical Business exists but has no counterparty-visible profile. |

### 8.2 Directional relationship state

| State | Allows | Blocks | Default network visibility | Reactivation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `active` | Supported new business activity and normal relationship management | Nothing beyond normal permissions and product rules | Visible | Not applicable |
| `inactive` | Historical access, direct detail access, existing-record context and management | Ordinary new activity through this relationship | Hidden from ordinary browse and search; available only through direct context, existing records, or `Add to network` resolution | Reactivates the same row |

### 

### 8.3 Reciprocal state derivation

| Source to target | Target to source | Derived connection meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Exists and active | Does not exist | One-way connection from the source Business |
| Exists and inactive | Does not exist | No ordinary business-surface reciprocal context |
| Exists and active | Exists and active | Mutual connection between both Businesses |
| Exists and active | Exists and inactive | Reverse relationship exists but is not part of the ordinary business-surface state |
| Exists and inactive | Exists and active | Reverse relationship exists but is not part of the ordinary business-surface state for the source Business |
| Exists and inactive | Exists and inactive | No ordinary business-surface reciprocal context |

Rules:

- Derived reciprocal state is recalculated when either directional relationship is created or changes active state.  
- Inactivating one direction does not change the opposite direction.  
- Reactivating one direction restores the derived state according to the matrix.  
- A second directional relationship, when later created by the other business, uses the same normal `Add to network` flow and invariants as the first direction.  
- Business-facing labels, if shown, should stay simple and should not expose internal inactive-only reciprocal variants.

## **9\. End-To-End Journeys**

### 9.1 Default `Add to network` journey

### ![][image3]

### 9.2 Internal resolution outcomes

| Outcome | Behaviour |
| :---- | :---- |
| Invalid `UNN` | Stay in flow. Show field error. Do not query internal storage or KYB. |
| Own `UNN` | Stay in flow. Show self-add error. Do not query internal storage or KYB. |
| Active relationship exists | Stay in flow. Show existing relationship and view action. |
| Inactive relationship exists | Navigate to existing relationship detail and show reactivation action. |
| Business exists without relationship | Stay in flow and present the existing Business with `Add to network`. |
| No Business exists | Call the `KYB API service`. |

### 

### 9.3 KYB result outcomes

| Outcome | Persistence | Navigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Valid authoritative business data | Create or resolve one canonical `Business`, publish verified `Business Identity`, set onboarding status to `pending_onboarding` if new | Navigate to target Business detail with `Add to network` |
| Valid business-level error | No Business or relationship created | Stay in add flow with inline error |
| Invalid response | No Business or relationship created | Stay in add flow with stop state |
| Service unavailable or timeout | No Business or relationship created | Stay in add flow with retry-later state |
| Concurrent Business creation by another request | Resolve to the canonical Business created by the winning request | Continue as successful existing Business resolution |

### 

### 9.4 Relationship creation and immediate outcomes

1. The source user confirms `Add to network` from a resolved target Business.  
2. The platform creates one active directional relationship from the `Current Business` to the target Business.  
3. At that moment the relationship is established and the source Business may use it for product actions that accept an active trading partner.  
4. The user may then optionally add relationship-local data already defined in this PRD: contact details, address and notes.  
5. Skipping that optional enrichment does not affect the established relationship.  
6. The new relationship is private to the source Business. It creates no target-side queue item, recommendation, notification or network-list entry.  
7. The target Business does not receive an automatic reverse relationship or recommendation from this base flow.  
8. If the target Business later wants a reciprocal connection, it must independently use the same normal `Add to network` flow.  
9. Transaction creation and visibility are outside this PRD. The relationship action emits no command to create, copy, backfill, hide, delete or modify transaction records.

### 9.5 Reciprocal relationship through later independent add

Rules:

1. The later reverse-direction add uses the same eligibility, validation, self-add and uniqueness rules as any other `Add to network` action.  
2. No request, recommendation or notification is created in the base flow.  
3. Reciprocal state is derived automatically once both directional relationships exist.  
4. No transaction backfill occurs when the second direction is added.

![][image4]

### 9.6 Network list and detail journey

- The default network list shows active directional relationships.  
- Ordinary browse and search operate only across active directional relationships.  
- Each row shows published business name, `UNN`, profile status, onboarding status, directional relationship state, reciprocal state and discrepancy indicator where applicable.  
- The detail view separates:  
  - published Business Identity  
  - profile and onboarding status  
  - relationship-local contact and address  
  - notes  
  - directional relationship state  
  - reciprocal state  
  - open discrepancy information  
- Published identity fields remain read-only in the default path.  
- Relationship-local sections may be edited without changing published truth.

### 9.7 Discrepancy journey

1. A claim-producing workflow creates a `Business Profile Claim`.  
2. That workflow compares the claim with the published `Business Identity`.  
3. If values conflict, it creates or updates a `Business Data Discrepancy`.  
4. When a previously unpublished or `provisional` Business later becomes published as `verified`, the publication-owning workflow must trigger retroactive discrepancy evaluation across existing directional relationships pointing to that Business.  
5. The Business network list and detail view show the discrepancy.  
6. The `Current Business` reviews the published and claimed values.  
7. The business resolves its Business-surface action by accepting the published identity for normal display.  
8. Where an equivalent editable relationship-local field exists, the user may update that field.  
9. The original claim, source evidence and audit history remain preserved.  
10. This PRD does not rewrite the originating `Business Profile Claim`, an invoice, a transaction `Source Observation` or any external source document.

## **10\. Use Cases And Error States**

| ID | Scenario | Expected behaviour |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `UC-001` | Eligible admin opens add flow | Flow opens with only `UNN` active. |
| `UC-002` | Ineligible user opens route directly | Access is blocked and user is returned to an appropriate business page. |
| `UC-003` | Invalid `UNN` format | Inline error. No internal or external lookup. |
| `UC-004` | User enters own `UNN` | Inline self-add error. |
| `UC-005` | Active relationship already exists | No new relationship. Show view action. |
| `UC-006` | Inactive relationship already exists | No new row. Navigate to detail with reactivation action. |
| `UC-007` | Existing Business without relationship | Present existing Business and allow relationship creation. |
| `UC-008` | New `UNN` returns authoritative data | Create canonical Business and verified published identity, then offer relationship creation. |
| `UC-009` | KYB returns valid business error | Stay in flow. Show returned business error. |
| `UC-010` | KYB times out or is unavailable | Stay in flow. Show retry-later state. No manual fallback in this PRD. |
| `UC-011` | User cancels after Business creation but before relationship creation | Business and published identity remain. No relationship is created. |
| `UC-012` | Relationship save fails | Stay on current state. Show error. No partial visible success. |
| `UC-013` | New relationship is created successfully | Relationship is established immediately. The user may optionally add relationship-local data, or skip and continue to the relationship detail. |
| `UC-014` | Two users create same Business concurrently | Both resolve to one canonical Business. |
| `UC-015` | Two users create same directional relationship concurrently | One relationship exists. Both callers receive deterministic success or existing-relationship outcome. |
| `UC-016` | Target business later adds the source Business through the same normal flow | A second directional relationship is created or reused, and reciprocal state is recalculated. |
| `UC-017` | One side of reciprocal pair becomes inactive | Ordinary business-surface reciprocal context is removed or simplified. Opposite relationship is unchanged. |
| `UC-018` | Both sides become inactive | No ordinary business-surface reciprocal context remains. |
| `UC-019` | User searches the ordinary network list | Results stay within the `Current Business` and the currently selected network filters. |
| `UC-020` | User edits relationship contact or address | Only relationship row changes. Published identity remains unchanged. |
| `UC-021` | User edits notes | Notes remain private to the `Current Business`. |
| `UC-022` | Conflicting claim is produced by another workflow | Base surface shows discrepancy but does not replace published identity. |
| `UC-023` | User resolves Business-surface discrepancy action by accepting published identity for normal display | Published identity remains authoritative, optional relationship-local fields may be updated, and the originating evidence remains preserved. |
| `UC-024` | Counterparty-added business starts onboarding | Existing Business is reused and onboarding claim is recorded on the same Business. |
| `UC-025` | Onboarding fails or requires correction | Existing published profile and relationships remain intact. |
| `UC-026` | Onboarding completes | Same Business becomes `onboarded`; `BU:Owner` is created or preserved. |
| `UC-027` | Legal name was changed through approved extended flow | Detail shows prior names as `Also known as` aliases where provided by published identity. |

### 11.2 Engineering-derived requirements and explicit Product reframing

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| `TP-E-001` | Inactive relationships are absent from ordinary browse and search and surface only through authorised direct context, existing-record context or `Add to network` resolution. |
| `TP-E-002` | When a previously unpublished or `provisional` Business becomes published as `verified`, the publication-owning workflow triggers retroactive discrepancy evaluation across applicable existing directional relationships. |
| `TP-E-003` | Approved prior legal names appear as read-only `Also known as` aliases when present. |
| `TP-E-004` | The default authoritative add path does not collect source-Business-authored Business Identity fields or create a source-authored Business Profile Claim. |
| `TP-E-005` | Notification delivery is excluded from this engineering release. Persistent Business-surface state remains in scope. |
| `TP-E-006` | Reciprocal state is a rebuildable derived projection from two directional relationships and is not a canonical shared relationship record. |
| `TP-E-007` | Relationship actions emit no command to create, copy, backfill, hide, delete or modify transaction records. |

### 11.3 Requirement authority

This PRD, its domain invariants, resolved decisions, and the companion ticket documents together define the requirement set for the base trading partner flow. Domain invariants apply to every ticket even when not repeated in its traceability section.

The source Product PRD previously described collecting additional Business Identity claim fields in the default add form and creating a Data Claim during save. This engineering PRD intentionally supersedes that behaviour for the default authoritative flow. Source-authored identity submissions are handled only through the Extended PRD.

## **12\. Resolved Decisions**

| ID | Decision |
| :---- | :---- |
| `DEC-001` | `Business Identity` means the published projection of a canonical `Business`, not a replacement canonical entity. |
| `DEC-002` | Exact `UNN` is the canonical identity anchor for this flow. |
| `DEC-003` | Authoritative KYB lookup is the only default no-match path. Manual fallback is excluded. |
| `DEC-004` | A valid authoritative result may create a verified Business before the owner onboards. |
| `DEC-005` | Business profile status and onboarding status are separate. |
| `DEC-006` | Relationships are directional and reciprocal state is derived. |
| `DEC-007` | The target does not receive an automatic reverse relationship from the base flow. A reciprocal connection exists only if the target later adds the source Business through the same normal flow. |
| `DEC-008` | Inactive relationships are hidden from ordinary browse and search and surface only through authorised direct context, existing-record context or `Add to network` resolution. |
| `DEC-009` | Inactivating one direction does not change the opposite relationship. |
| `DEC-010` | Optional inbound-request and request-driven reciprocal workflows, if enabled later, belong to the Extended PRD rather than this base PRD. |
| `DEC-011` | The default authoritative add path does not create a source-authored Business Profile Claim. |
| `DEC-012` | Claim-producing workflows own discrepancy production and internal evidence disposition. This PRD owns Business-surface presentation and action resolution. |
| `DEC-013` | This PRD does not define transaction creation, visibility, sharing, historical population or financial posting. Creating, activating, inactivating or reciprocating a Trading Partner Relationship produces no transaction-record mutation from this domain. |
| `DEC-014` | The base `Add to network` flow is private to the source Business. It creates no target-side request, recommendation, notification or network-list entry. |
| `DEC-015` | The default authoritative add flow does not collect or persist source-Business-authored Business Identity fields. It publishes approved authoritative identity and permits only relationship-local enrichment. Source-authored identity submission belongs to the Extended PRD. |
| `DEC-016` | Source-Business discrepancy and verification notifications described in the source Product PRD are deferred from this engineering release. Persistent Business-surface state remains required. |
| `DEC-017` | Reciprocal state may be materialised as a rebuildable read projection but the two directional relationships remain authoritative. |
| `DEC-018` | A Business may resolve its Business-surface discrepancy action by accepting published truth for normal display. This closes only the Business-facing action and does not delete, invalidate, correct or internally resolve the originating evidence. |
| `DEC-019` | The existing Business edit permission applies to all relationship-local fields in the base trading partner surface. |
| `DEC-020` | Internal reciprocal-state identifiers are engineering concerns only. Business-facing copy, if any, should use simple product wording and should not surface inactive-only reciprocal variants as distinct statuses. |

## **13\. Open Questions**

The following questions do not block the default flow tickets unless explicitly noted.

### `OQ-1`: User-facing reciprocal connection wording

- Should the business UI surface reciprocal context at all, or simply show the partner without an explicit one-way versus mutual indicator?  
- If reciprocal context is shown, Product and Design should choose appropriate labels.

**Answer: No need to surface reciprocal/mutual status in the Business Partner Management UI.**

## **2\. Tickets**

### Epic A: Add To Network

### T1: Add To Network Eligibility And Route Guard

**Goal**

Allow only eligible business actors to enter `Add to network`.

**User story**

As a `BU:Owner` or `BU:Admin`, I can access `Add to network` when my current business has active business access.

**Actor and preconditions**

- Actor: `BU:Owner` or `BU:Admin`  
- `Current Business` has reached `Business User capability - Business onboarded / app access opens`

**Trigger**

- User selects `Add to network`  
- User navigates directly to the route

**In scope**

- Entry-point visibility  
- Server-side and route-level access control  
- Initial page state  
- Blocked-route handling

**Out of scope**

- `UNN` validation  
- Business resolution  
- KYB lookup  
- Persistence

**Primary flow**

1. Evaluate role and business capability.  
2. Show entry point only when eligible.  
3. Open add flow with only `UNN` active.  
4. Do not trigger lookup automatically.

**Failure flows**

- Ineligible user does not see the entry point.  
- Direct route access is blocked and redirected to an appropriate business page.

**User-visible outcome**

Eligible user sees the initial add flow. Ineligible user cannot enter.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given an eligible `BU:Owner`, when the user selects `Add to network`, then the add page opens with only the `UNN` field active.  
- Given an eligible `BU:Admin`, the same behaviour applies.  
- Given an ineligible `BU`, the entry point is absent.  
- Given an ineligible direct route attempt, access is denied after server-side authorisation and the user is redirected.  
- Changing client-side state cannot bypass authorisation.

**Traceability**

- `TP-P-001`  
- `TP-P-002`

---

### T2: UNN Validation And Internal Business Resolution

**Goal**

Resolve all internal outcomes before any authoritative external lookup.

**User story**

As an eligible business administrator, I can check a target `UNN` and receive the correct existing-business outcome.

**Actor and preconditions**

- Eligible actor is inside the add flow  
- Flow is in initial or reset state

**Trigger**

User enters a `UNN` and explicitly selects check.

**In scope**

- Format validation  
- Existing canonical Business lookup  
- Self-add detection  
- Existing active relationship detection  
- Existing inactive relationship detection  
- Existing Business without relationship  
- Reset after `UNN` edit

**Out of scope**

- KYB lookup  
- New Business creation  
- Relationship mutation

**Primary flow**

1. Validate ten digits beginning with `7`.  
2. Resolve canonical Business by exact `UNN`.  
3. If found, evaluate self-add.  
4. If not self, evaluate directional relationship existence and state.  
5. Return the matching UI outcome.

**Alternate and failure flows**

- Invalid format stops before storage lookup.  
- Active relationship returns existing relationship.  
- Inactive relationship routes to detail.  
- Existing Business without relationship returns add action.  
- Editing a resolved `UNN` resets the flow.

**User-visible outcome**

One clear result with no external lookup for existing Businesses.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Invalid format triggers no Business lookup and no KYB call.  
- Own `UNN` cannot progress.  
- Existing active relationship does not create another relationship.  
- Existing inactive relationship navigates to the existing detail page.  
- Existing Business without relationship is shown with `Add to network`.  
- Editing the resolved `UNN` removes prior result state.  
- Resolution is scoped to the `Current Business` for relationship checks.

**Traceability**

- `TP-P-003`  
- `TP-P-004`

### T3: Authoritative KYB Lookup And Result Classification

**Goal**

Call the authoritative KYB service only when internal resolution has no Business and classify its outcome clearly.

**Outcome**

The Business domain can distinguish authoritative business data, valid business errors and technical failures without silently entering a manual flow.

**Actor and preconditions**

- Eligible actor has submitted a valid `UNN`  
- T2 returned no canonical Business

**Trigger**

Internal resolution reaches the no-Business branch.

**In scope**

- KYB request  
- Request progress state  
- Result classification  
- Retry-later state  
- Business-level error presentation

**Out of scope**

- Canonical Business persistence  
- Manual fallback  
- Relationship creation

**Primary flow**

1. Send the valid `UNN` to the `KYB API service`.  
2. Make the `UNN` read-only while the request is active.  
3. Classify the response:  
   - authoritative business data  
   - valid business-level error  
   - invalid response  
   - timeout or unavailable service  
4. Return a clear outcome to the add flow.

**Failure flows**

- Valid business error remains inline.  
- Invalid response and service failure expose retry-later or stop state.  
- No manual fields become available.

**User-visible outcome**

The user remains in the add flow unless authoritative data is successfully returned.

**Acceptance criteria**

- KYB is called only after T2 returns no Business.  
- A valid business error is not classified as a transport failure.  
- A timeout is not classified as a business-level rejection.  
- Repeated retry does not create Business records.  
- The default flow never exposes manual identity fields after a failure.  
- A successful authoritative result allows the user to continue with the resolved business.

**Traceability**

- Applicable domain invariants and this ticket's acceptance criteria.
