# 🚨 Draft Business Logic Decisions Record

**Document 0 \- Business Logic Decisions Record**

Shared Foundation for Business Registration, Trading Partner Management & Admin Verification PRDs

**Version 2.0  |  Status: Locked \- Source of truth for all downstream PRDs**

# **1\. Purpose & How to Use This Document**

This document is the authoritative record of every business logic decision covering trading partner management, transaction permissions, verification access tiers, data merging, owner and admin structure, and ZATCA as a data source. It exists so that each downstream PRD can stay focused on requirements without re-explaining the business logic that drives them.

Engineering teams should read this document once before reading any of the three companion PRDs. When a PRD states a rule \- 'payment links are blocked at Tier 1' or 'merge triggers only on exact CR match' \- the reasoning is here, not in the PRD itself.

This document is not a requirements document. It contains no functional requirements, acceptance criteria, or implementation detail. Those live in the PRDs. This document contains only decisions, their rationale, and the constraints they impose.

| Document | Title & Scope |
| :---- | :---- |
| **PRD 1** | Business Registration & Onboarding \- covers sign-up, onboarding wizard, ownership invitation, multi-business login, progressive tier unlocking, dashboard states, and re-submission flow. |
| **PRD 2** | Trading Partner Management \- covers Path A (manual CR-first entry), Path B (ZATCA invoice import), Path C (contact enrichment via API and bulk upload), badge model, merge logic, trading partner profile fields, and UX journeys for all paths. |
| **PRD 3** | Admin Verification Interface \- covers the verification queue, field-level review, partial section approval unlocking tiers, MoC cross-reference step, and ownership invitation monitoring. |

# **2\. Data Model & Terminology Definitions**

This section establishes the canonical definitions for every entity and concept referenced across the Foundation PRDs. These definitions must be used consistently by Product, Design, and Engineering. Where a term below replaces a prior term used in earlier documentation, the replacement is binding.

## **2.1 Core Entity Definitions**

| Concept | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Business** | The canonical real-world entity \- any company operating in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Identified uniquely by CRN (Commercial Registration Number) or UNN (Unified National Number), enforced as unique identifiers at the database level. The Business entity exists the moment its CR/UNN appears on the platform \- whether through self-registration or through another business adding it as a trading partner. Registration status is a property of the Business, not a different entity type. |
| **Trading Partner Record** | A record in a specific business's directory representing a trading relationship. This is a relational data structure scoped to the creating business \- it is not the Business entity itself. Each registered business maintains its own set of Trading Partner Records. A Trading Partner Record references the canonical Business entity and reflects that entity's current badge state. Local attributes on the record (internal notes, custom labels) are private to the creating business and do not affect the canonical Business. |
| **Business Network** | A business's own scoped collection of Trading Partner Records. Built through Path A (manual addition), Path B (ZATCA invoice import), or Path C (bulk upload or API). Every registered business on the platform has their own Business Network. An Unregistered Business in one merchant's network is a canonical Business record linked to that merchant through a Trading Partner Record. |
| **Business Directory** “Q4 deferred feature” | A platform-wide searchable listing of all registered and verified businesses on APEX. It allows a business to search for and discover other platform businesses by trade name without needing to know their CR number. When a match is found, that Business can be added directly to the searching business's network. The Business Directory is the discovery layer that feeds into the Business Network. |
| **Badge** | A signal that reflects a Business's registration and verification state on the platform. The badge is a property of the Business entity \- not of the Trading Partner Record. The Trading Partner Record references and displays the badge of the Business it points to. When a Business's verification state changes, the badge updates once at the Business level and is automatically reflected across every Trading Partner Record on the platform that references that Business. |

## **2.2 Business Registration States**

Every Business on the platform exists in one of three internal states. These states drive badge assignment and platform behavior.

| Internal State | Description | External Badge | Platform Behavior |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Not Registered** | The Business exists in the real world. It has been added to one or more businesses' networks via Path A, Path B, or Path C. It has no APEX account. | Unverified | Can be traded with at Tier 2+. Excluded from financing eligibility. |
| **Registered \- Pending** | The Business has created an APEX account and submitted for review. It has not yet reached Tier 1\. The Business has joined the platform and is actively seeking verification. | Unverified | Same permissions as Not Registered externally. Internally tracked as distinct state. |
| **Platform Verified** | The Business has self-registered and reached Tier 1 (Core Business Identification confirmed by admin). This is the trigger point at which Trading Partner Records in other businesses' networks update to reflect Platform Verified. | Platform Verified | Full trust signal. Eligible as trading partner for financing submissions when counterpart is Tier 2+. |

The external badge is intentionally two-state. Both Not Registered and Registered-Pending are visible to other businesses as Unverified. The internal three-state distinction is tracked at the platform level and informs ops workflows and future product features.

# **3\. Decisions**

## **3.1 Admin Verification & Progressive Access**

| Topic | Decision | Detail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Tier model** | **Three tiers, independently unlocked** | Tier 1: Core Business Identification confirmed. Tier 2: full verification including owner identity. Tier 3: bank account verified. Admin unlocks each tier independently through section-level CTA confirmation. Not all-or-nothing. |
| **Tier 1 unlock** | **Core Business Identification section CTA** | Admin approves all actionable fields in the Core Business Identification section and clicks the section-level CTA ('Approve Core Business Identification → Unlock Business Access'). The Business immediately becomes Platform Verified to other businesses and gains Tier 1 capabilities even while the rest of the review is ongoing. |
| **Tier 2 unlock** | **Beneficial Owners section CTA** | Admin approves all actionable fields in the Beneficial Owners section and clicks the section-level CTA. Core Business Identification (Tier 1\) must already be complete. Owner identity is part of Tier 2 \- not a separate gate above it. |
| **Tier 3 unlock** | **Bank Account section CTA** | Admin approves the IBAN field and clicks the section-level CTA. Tier 3 unlocks. Settlement payouts become available. Nothing else gates on bank verification. |
| **Taxable Business declaration** | **Toggle at onboarding, visible in admin review** | During onboarding the business sees a Taxable Business toggle. Toggle is On by default (taxable \- normal state). Switching it Off triggers a warning: 'Declaring your business as non-taxable means VAT invoicing and ZATCA submission will not be available on APEX. This declaration cannot be changed without contacting support.' The business must confirm to proceed. When Off, VAT Registration Number and VAT Certificate upload are hidden from the onboarding form and from the admin review. TIN remains visible and required for all businesses regardless of toggle state. The admin sees a read-only label: Non-taxable business (self-declared) alongside the TIN field for review. |
| **Buyer financing gate** | **Parked \- ARB dependency** | Whether owner verification or any specific tier is required for buyer financing with ARB is a banking partner requirement question, not a platform decision. Flagged as open pending ARB eligibility criteria. |
| **IBAN validation gate** | **Invalid \= hard gate; Valid \= advisory** | System performs mathematical IBAN validation (format and checksum) before the admin reviews the field. If the system result is Invalid, the admin Approve action is disabled \- the IBAN cannot be approved in an Invalid state. If the system result is Valid, the result is advisory: the admin uses it alongside the declared bank name to confirm that the bank derived from the IBAN matches the business's declared bank. A Valid system result does not compel approval \- admin retains judgment on bank name match. |
| **Section-level CTA mechanics** | **Explicit confirmation per section** | Each of the three review sections has its own section-level CTA that is activated after all actionable fields in that section are individually approved. The section CTA ('Approve \[Section Name\] → Unlock \[Tier\] Access') is the explicit trigger for the corresponding tier unlock. Tier unlocks are not automatic on individual field approval \- they require the section-level CTA to be clicked. A 'Send Section for Correction' CTA is the rejection path at section level. |

## **3.2 ZATCA as a Verification Source of Truth**

| Topic | Decision | Detail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **ZATCA buyer validation** | **Format only \- not existence** | ZATCA Phase 2 validates buyer TIN format only. It does not verify that the buyer's TIN or CR belongs to a real registered entity. ZATCA verifies the seller (enrolled in Fatoora). The buyer is a passive recipient. Confirmed against ZATCA Phase 2 specification. |
| **Path B status** | **Record creation and enrichment only** | Path B survives as a mechanism for creating and enriching Trading Partner Records from invoice data. Confidence level is explicitly format-validated, not existence-validated. Path B data does not change the Business badge. |
| **ZATCA badge impact** | **None \- Unverified badge always** | Trading Partner Records created or enriched purely through Path B carry the Unverified badge regardless of invoice volume or data consistency. Badge only changes to Platform Verified on self-registration and Tier 1 completion. |
| **Internal quality labels** | **Four levels within Unverified** | Manually Entered (Path A). ZATCA Referenced Single Seller (Path B, one enrolled seller). ZATCA Referenced Multiple Sellers (Path B, two or more distinct enrolled sellers). Business Supplied (Path C creation mode). Never surfaced externally. Feed matching confidence scoring and future financing eligibility logic. |
| **CR validation** | **Explicit admin step** | Admin cross-referencing submitted CR against the MoC public portal is an explicit step in the admin verification review. This confirms CR existence and active status. Wathq API integration is a future enhancement. |
| **ZATCA buyer fields** | **Partial \- no contact details** | ZATCA invoice XML carries: buyer legal name (Arabic and/or English), VAT Registration Number or (TIN) where present, national address fields. Sometimes CR number in the additional ID field \- not always populated. It never carries email or phone number. Path B records always have a contact detail gap. |

## **3.3 Business Addition & Minimum Data**

| Topic | Decision | Detail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Creation paths** | **Path A, Path B, and Path C** | **Path A**: CR/UNN required. Legal business name (Arabic) required. All other fields optional at creation. **Path B**: Automatic extraction from ZATCA invoice import. No record created without a CR or TIN anchor. **Path C**: Sellers supply buyer business identity and contact data via API or bulk CSV upload. Platform handles record creation and enrichment automatically. |
| **Path C \- enrichment rule** | **Gap-fill for enrichment events; full overwrite on merge** | For Path C enrichment events (adding to an existing record), contact fields (email, phone) follow the gap-fill rule: Path C adds contact fields where absent and does not overwrite existing values. For the merge trigger event (Business self-registers and reaches Tier 1), the full overwrite rule applies to all fields including contact fields. See Section 8 for complete merge rules. |
| **Search by Business name** | **Deferred to Q4** | Search by trade name to find Businesses already on the platform is a Q4 enhancement, naturally delivered alongside the Business Directory. Not a launch requirement. |
| **Merge trigger** | **Silent, automatic, exact CR match only** | When a Business self-registers and reaches Tier 1 (Core Business Identification confirmed by admin), the platform performs an exact CR/UNN match across all Trading Partner Records platform-wide. Matching records are merged silently. No notification to either party. No admin involvement in the merge. See Section 8 for full merge behavior. |
| **Merge timing** | **After Tier 1 only** | Merge does not trigger on provisional self-registration. Merge triggers only after admin confirms the Core Business Identification section and the Business reaches Tier 1\. Provisional records remain as-is until then. |
| **Merge scope** | **Full overwrite \- all fields** | Verified self-registered data overwrites all Trading Partner Record fields \- including identity fields and contact fields. Contact fields are platform-owned on merge. The protection against incorrect merges is the exact CR/UNN match requirement. See Section 8 for survivor rules and merchant-owned field exceptions. |
| **Badge states** | **Two external states** | **Unverified**: the Business has no self-registered platform account with a matching CR, or has registered but not yet reached Tier 1\. **Platform Verified**: the Business self-registered and reached Tier 1\. Badge is a property of the Business entity. Badge updates on merge trigger are reflected automatically across all Trading Partner Records that reference that Business. |
| **Historical snapshots** | **Immutable** | Historical invoice snapshots are never updated by any merge or profile change. They remain as created at invoice issuance time. |
| **Duplicate CR registration** | **Defined handling** | If a CR is submitted at registration that already belongs to an active registered Business, the second registration is blocked with a message directing the person to request access from the business administrator. If the CR belongs to a Business that is registered but pending verification, the second registration is blocked and routed to ops as a duplicate registration case for manual resolution. |

## **3.4 Transaction Permissions**

| Topic | Decision | Detail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Permission axis** | **Verification status** | Transaction permissions are driven by the verification status (tier) of the registered business. Taxability drives document compliance rules (ZATCA submission, invoice type) separately. These are not the same axis and must not be conflated in access logic. |
| **Unverified business** | **No outbound financial actions** | A business below Tier 2 cannot generate payment links, issue invoices, or make financing requests. Invoice import and Trading Partner Record creation can happen in the background. No outbound financial action until Tier 2\. |
| **Unverified Business (trading partner)** | **Transactions permitted, financing excluded** | A Tier 2+ business can invoice and generate payment links against an Unverified Business (CR known). The trading partner is flagged as Unverified on all documents. That invoice is excluded from financing eligibility regardless of the business's tier. |
| **Non-taxable businesses** | **Full permissions once verified** | Non-taxable businesses receive full Tier 2 permissions once admin-verified. ZATCA submission is blocked and clearly communicated. Financing eligibility is subject to ARB partner criteria \- not a platform decision. |
| **Financing check timing** | **Parked** | Whether financing eligibility is checked at invoice time or at financing submission time is deferred to the financing topic discussion. |

## **3.5 Business Data Merging & Pre-onboarding Transactions**

| Topic | Decision | Detail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Newly registered business view** | **Clean slate with opt-in** | A Business that self-registers sees no pre-existing transactions recorded by other businesses against them. They arrive on a clean slate. At first login, an opt-in prompt is shown offering to surface transactions where the Business was directly a party \- specifically transactions where they were the buyer on another platform business's payment link or invoice. The opt-in scope is strictly limited to transactions they were a party to \- not another business's private records about them. If opted in, these transactions appear in historical view labelled as pre-registration activity. |
| **Own imported documents** | **Visible** | The newly registered business can see their own imported documents \- invoices they generated and imported via API or bulk upload. These are their records, not another party's attribution. |
| **Pre-onboarding disputes** | **No dispute mechanism** | APEX has no standing to adjudicate transactions it did not facilitate. No dispute mechanism exists for pre-platform transactions. |
| **Identifier hierarchy** | **CR/UNN primary; TIN secondary (ops only)** | CR/UNN is the definitive anchor for all auto-merge logic. TIN is the secondary identifier. A TIN match without a corresponding CR/UNN match does not trigger an auto-merge \- it surfaces a possible duplicate case to ops for manual review. At Tier 1, the verified CR/UNN triggers merge against CR-anchored records; the verified TIN then cross-references TIN-only records and resolves them through the same event. There is no third tier of identifier below TIN for merge purposes. |
| **Merge control** | **Automatic \- not admin-controlled** | The merge is automatic on exact CR/UNN match. The protection against incorrect merges is the exact match requirement, not human intervention. Ops tooling for TIN-matched possible duplicates is defined in the Ops Process Requirements section. |
| **Orphaned records** | **Ops backlog** | Trading Partner Records with no CR/UNN match after a Business self-registers are surfaced to admin as a data hygiene view. Admin can manually investigate and trigger a match. Future capability, not a launch requirement. |

## **3.6 Business Owner vs. User Verification**

| Topic | Decision | Detail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **First registrant role declaration** | **Captured at registration** | The onboarding form asks the registrant to declare their role upfront: either 'I am the company owner' or 'I am authorized to register this business'. This declaration drives role assignment and downstream flows. |
| **Path A \- Owner registers directly** | **Owner role assigned immediately** | When the registrant declares they are the company owner, the Owner role is assigned to them upon registration. No invitation flow is triggered. |
| **Path B \- Authorized person registers** | **Admin role assigned; Owner invited separately** | When the registrant declares they are authorized but not the owner, they receive the Admin role. The Admin then sends an ownership invitation to the legal owner's email. The legal owner accepts, creates or connects their APEX account, and the Owner role is assigned to them. |
| **Ownership invitation \- new user** | **Simplified account creation** | When the invited owner has no existing APEX account, they see a simplified account creation screen \- email (pre-filled from the invitation address, locked) and password only. No full sign-up flow and no onboarding wizard. The business already exists and the owner is claiming their role only. On account creation, the owner lands directly on the business dashboard with the Owner role assigned. The invitation link is tied to the specific email it was sent to \- attempts to register under a different email are rejected. |
| **Ownership invitation scope** | **Path B only** | The ownership invitation flow applies exclusively to Path B. It does not exist in Path A, where the owner has already self-identified and been assigned the Owner role directly. |
| **Tier 2 dependency on ownership** | **None** | Tier 2 unlocks on verification regardless of path or whether the ownership invitation has been accepted. Admin role is sufficient for all Tier 2 commercial operations. |
| **Financing gate** | **Authorized signatory \- not Owner role** | Financing requires a designated authorized signatory with verified identity. This is independent of path or Owner role status. |
| **Ownership-exclusive actions** | **Unavailable until Owner role is active** | Ownership transfer and account deletion require the Owner role. In Path A this is available immediately. In Path B these actions are unavailable until the invitation is accepted. |
| **Beneficial owner fields \- Path A** | **Collapse into registrant** | When the registrant is the owner, their registration details serve as the beneficial owner record. No separate beneficial owner capture is required. |
| **Beneficial owner fields \- Path B** | **Always captured separately** | When the registrant is not the owner, the onboarding form captures the legal owner's details as required fields. The admin verification team verifies these as part of standard review. |
| **Subsequent users** | **No independent verification** | Invited users do not need independent identity verification once the business is verified and they are invited through the Owner or Admin account. |

# **4\. Transaction Permissions Matrix**

The matrix below defines what is permitted based on the verification tier of the registered business and the badge status of the trading partner. This is the authoritative reference for access logic across all platform features.

| Registered business | Trading partner status | Permitted actions |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Unverified (any tier below Tier 2\) | Any | Invoice import and Trading Partner Record creation in background only. No payment link generation. No financing requests. No outbound financial actions. |
| Tier 1 \- CR confirmed | Any | Platform login. View imported invoices. Add businesses to network. Appear as Platform Verified to other businesses. Cannot generate payment links or transact financially. |
| Tier 2 \- Fully verified | Platform Verified (CR confirmed) | Full commercial operations: invoicing, payment links, ZATCA submission, credit notes, receiving payments, invoice financing. Eligible for financing submissions. |
| Tier 2 \- Fully verified | Unverified Business (CR known) | Invoicing and payment links permitted. Trading partner flagged as Unverified on all documents. Excluded from financing eligibility regardless of invoice count. |
| Tier 2 \- Fully verified (non-taxable) | Any | Same as Tier 2 verified. ZATCA submission blocked and communicated clearly. Financing eligibility subject to ARB partner criteria \- not a platform decision. |
| Tier 2 or Tier 3 | Any | Settlement payout to bank account: requires Tier 3 (bank account verified). All other Tier 2 operations proceed regardless of bank verification status. |

Taxability affects document compliance rules (ZATCA submission type, invoice format) not transaction permissions. A non-taxable business at Tier 2 has the same transaction permissions as a taxable business at Tier 2 \- ZATCA submission is simply blocked and communicated.

# **5\. Progressive Access Matrix**

The matrix below defines which platform capabilities unlock at each verification tier, and which admin action triggers each unlock. Admin approves sections independently \- tier unlocks happen on section-level CTA confirmation, not only at full review completion.

| Platform capability | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 | Admin action to unlock |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Log in and view platform | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Approve Core Business Identification section |
| Appear as Platform Verified to other businesses | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Approve Core Business Identification section |
| Add businesses to network (Path A, B, or C) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Approve Core Business Identification section |
| Import invoices (API / bulk / OCR) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Approve Core Business Identification section |
| View imported invoices | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Approve Core Business Identification section |
| Issue invoices | \- | ✓ | ✓ | Approve Beneficial Owners section |
| ZATCA submission (taxable only) | \- | ✓ | ✓ | Approve Beneficial Owners section |
| Credit notes | \- | ✓ | ✓ | Approve Beneficial Owners section |
| Generate payment links | \- | ✓ | ✓ | Approve Beneficial Owners section |
| Receive payments (into settlement layer) | \- | ✓ | ✓ | Approve Beneficial Owners section |
| Invoice financing submission | \- | ✓ | ✓ | Approve Beneficial Owners section |
| Buyer financing (ARB) | \- | ? | ? | ARB criteria \- parked |
| Settlement payout to bank account | \- | \- | ✓ | Approve Bank Account section |
| Ownership transfer / account deletion | \- | \-\* | \-\* | Owner role must be assigned via accepted invitation |

\* Ownership transfer and account deletion are Owner role exclusive. These actions are unavailable until the ownership invitation is accepted and the Owner role is assigned \- regardless of verification tier.

# **6\. Business Badge & Confidence Label Model**

Two external badge states are shown to businesses on the platform. Four internal quality labels exist \- three within the Unverified state and one for Business Supplied records \- never surfaced externally, used for matching confidence scoring and future financing eligibility logic. The badge is a property of the Business entity and is referenced by Trading Partner Records.

| Badge (external) | Internal quality label | Source / trigger | Permissions & restrictions |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Unverified | Manually Entered | Path A \- CR entered by seller manually | Usable for invoicing and payment links. Flagged on all documents. Excluded from financing eligibility. Lowest confidence. |
| Unverified | ZATCA Referenced \- Single Seller | Path B \- CR/TIN appeared on ZATCA-cleared invoice from one enrolled seller | Same as Manually Entered. Higher internal confidence \- format validated by ZATCA, economic incentive for seller to enter correct data. |
| Unverified | ZATCA Referenced \- Multiple Sellers | Path B \- same CR/TIN on cleared invoices from two or more distinct enrolled sellers | Same external permissions. Highest confidence within Unverified tier. Feeds financing eligibility scoring when financing topic is resolved. |
| Unverified | Business Supplied | Path C creation mode \- record created via API or bulk CSV upload by seller | Same as Manually Entered. Label distinguishes records created at scale via API or CSV from one-by-one manual entries. |
| **Platform Verified** | **Self-registered** | Business self-registered and reached Tier 1 (CR confirmed by admin). Exact CR/UNN match triggered silent merge. | Full trust signal. Trading Partner Records updated with verified data and aliases stored. Eligible as trading partner for financing submissions if registered business is also Tier 2+. |

# **7\. Field-Level Verification Matrix**

The matrix below defines every field presented to the admin in the verification review, the action available on each field, which tier that field's approval contributes to unlocking, and the verification method the admin uses.

| Field | Admin action | Tier unlocked | Verification method |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Section 1 \- Core Business Identification  (full section approval unlocks Tier 1\)** |  |  |  |
| CR/UNN Number | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | Cross-check against uploaded CR certificate. Admin must also cross-reference against MoC public portal to confirm CR is active and registered. MoC confirmation checkbox required before approval can be saved. |
| Legal Business Name (Arabic) | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | Must match exactly as it appears on the CR certificate. |
| Upload CR Certificate | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | Admin opens document and confirms legal name and CR number match submission. Document must be unexpired. |
| Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | Verified via ZATCA portal. 10-digit number. Always present and required for all businesses regardless of taxability declaration. Verified via ZATCA portal. 10-digit number. |
| VAT Registration Number | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | Verified via ZATCA portal. 15-digit number starting and ending with 3\. Only shown if business declared VAT-registered. Hidden for non-taxable businesses. |
| Upload VAT Certificate | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | Admin opens document and confirms VAT number matches submission. Only shown if business is VAT-registered. |
| Non-taxable declaration | Display only | \- | Read-only label shown when business switched the Taxable Business toggle Off at onboarding: 'Non-taxable business (self-declared)'. TIN and VAT fields are absent from the admin review for these businesses. Admin takes no action \- section completes without those fields. |
| Registered Address (National Address) | Display only | \- | Not verified by admin. Shown for reference only. |
| **Section 2 \- Beneficial Owners  (full section approval completes Tier 2\)** |  |  |  |
| Full Name | Approve / Reject | Tier 2 | Cross-check against uploaded owner ID document. Name must match exactly. |
| National ID (Saudi) or Iqama (resident) | Approve / Reject | Tier 2 | Cross-check against uploaded ID document. Number must match. |
| Upload ID Copy (National ID, Passport, or Iqama) | Approve / Reject | Tier 2 | Admin opens document and confirms it is clear, valid, unexpired, and matches name and ID number submitted. |
| **Section 3 \- Bank Account Details  (IBAN approval unlocks Tier 3\)** |  |  |  |
| IBAN | Approve / Reject | Tier 3 | System performs mathematical IBAN validation (format and checksum). Result shown to admin before decision. If result is Invalid, Approve action is disabled \- admin can only reject. If result is Valid, admin cross-references bank name derived from IBAN against the business's declared bank name before approving. Valid result is advisory, not a compelled approval. |
| Bank Name | Display only | \- | Auto-derived from IBAN. No independent action required. |
| Account Holder Name | Display only | \- | Shown for reference alongside IBAN. |
| Bank Account Number | Display only | \- | Shown for reference. |

Approving all actionable fields in Section 1 and clicking the section CTA unlocks Tier 1\. For non-taxable businesses, TIN and VAT fields are absent \- the section is complete without them. Approving all actionable fields in Section 2 and clicking the section CTA completes Tier 2\. Section 3 IBAN approval and section CTA independently unlocks Tier 3\.

# **8\. Merge Behavior & Record Consolidation**

This section defines the complete set of rules governing how the platform handles Business record merging and deduplication. These rules apply when a Business self-registers and reaches Tier 1, when duplicate records are identified, and when ops intervenes to correct records. All merge decisions below are authoritative and binding on PRD 2 and PRD 3\.

## **8.1 Merge Trigger & Scope**

| Topic | Decision | Detail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Primary merge trigger** | **Tier 1 unlock \- exact CR/UNN match** | When a Business reaches Tier 1, the platform runs an exact CR/UNN match across all Trading Partner Records platform-wide simultaneously. Only exact CR/UNN matches trigger an auto-merge. A single-digit transposition prevents an incorrect merge. |
| **Secondary match \- TIN** | **Ops review only, no auto-merge** | When a TIN match is found without a corresponding CR/UNN match, the platform does not auto-merge. It surfaces a possible duplicate case to the ops queue for manual review and resolution. At Tier 1, the now-verified CR/UNN may cross-reference TIN-only records and resolve them through the same event if the TIN is confirmed. |
| **Full overwrite scope** | **All fields \- identity and contact** | Verified self-registered data overwrites all Trading Partner Record fields: CR/UNN, legal name, TIN, VAT Registration Number, national address, email, and phone. Contact fields are platform-owned on the merge event. This differs from Path C enrichment events, which are gap-fill only. |
| **Alias preservation** | **Previous names stored at merge** | Prior names from pre-merge records are stored as searchable aliases on the Business record at merge time. The verified legal Arabic name is canonical and displayed as primary. Aliases are visible in the Business profile as 'Also known as' \- read-only, not editable. Alias names are included in search results. |
| **Merge atomicity** | **Complete or not at all** | The merge must complete fully or not at all. A partial merge state must not be visible to any user or business. If the merge fails mid-process it rolls back entirely. |
| **Background processing** | **Non-blocking** | The merge job runs in the background. Invoice import completion must not be delayed by trading partner processing. |

## **8.2 Duplicate & Deduplication Rules**

| Scenario | Decision | Rules & Detail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Same CR/UNN, different trade names** | **CR/UNN is definitive; verified legal name is canonical** | Exact CR/UNN match declares the same Business regardless of name variation. Names differ in practice for legitimate reasons. The verified legal Arabic name from the Business's onboarding data becomes canonical. Prior names are stored as aliases. Aliases remain searchable but are not displayed as primary. |
| **Same Business \- two records with different anchors** | **TIN match surfaces to ops; resolved at Tier 1** | If Record A was created with CR/UNN and Record B with TIN only (no shared anchor), the auto-merge cannot fire. The TIN match is surfaced to ops as a possible duplicate. When the Business self-registers and reaches Tier 1, the verified CR/UNN merges Record A; the verified TIN then cross-references and resolves Record B through the same Tier 1 event. |
| **Duplicate records already referenced by transactions** | **Re-point to survivor; immutable audit trail** | Historical transactions are re-pointed to the survivor Business record so the seller sees a clean unified history. The system preserves an immutable audit trail: original record linkage, merge timestamp, and initiating trigger. A 'merged record' indicator is shown on affected historical documents so the seller understands why the name changed. |
| **Self-registration after multiple partial records** | **Platform-wide simultaneous merge** | When a Business reaches Tier 1, the merge fires simultaneously across all merchants' Trading Partner Records that match the CR/UNN. One canonical Business entity is updated platform-wide. Each merchant retains their own Trading Partner Record, now linked to the verified canonical entity with Platform Verified badge and verified data. |
| **Conflicting seller-supplied vs. verified data** | **Platform-owned fields overwritten; merchant-owned fields preserved** | Platform-owned fields (CR/UNN, legal name, TIN, VAT Registration Number, national address, email, phone) are overwritten by verified data on merge — across all businesses' records. No platform-owned field is editable by any business after the merge event or at any other time. Pre-merge aliases are never overwritten and remain private to each business |
| **Merge reversibility** | **Not reversible; ops corrective action path** | A merge cannot be auto-reversed. If a merge proves incorrect, ops performs a corrective action: record separation, transaction reassignment to the correct Business record, and creation of a new Trading Partner Record where needed. The merge log provides all evidence necessary for correction. |

## **8.3 Merge Audit & Ops Visibility**

| Topic | Decision | Detail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Merge log** | **Stored permanently; ops-visible** | For every merge event, the platform stores: matched fields and their values at time of merge, source precedence applied, timestamp of merge, initiating trigger (Tier 1 approval event), and which records were consolidated. The merge log is accessible to Super Admin and Operations roles only. |
| **Business-visible indicator** | **Merged record indicator on affected documents** | Sellers see a 'merged record' indicator on historical documents that were affected by a merge. No detailed log is shown to merchants \- only the indicator and the updated Business name. |
| **Possible duplicate queue** | **TIN-matched cases surfaced to ops** | When TIN match exists without CR/UNN confirmation, a possible duplicate case is created in the ops queue. Ops reviews the case, contacts parties if necessary, confirms the legitimate entity, and either confirms or dismisses the duplicate. |

# **9\. Tier Drop Behavior (Edge Cases)**

When the admin rejects a field in a section that was previously fully approved, the Business drops below the tier associated with that section. This section defines the cascading effects of a tier drop.

| Topic | Decision | Detail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Badge on tier drop** | **Reverts platform-wide immediately** | When a Business drops below Tier 1 due to a Section 1 field rejection, its badge reverts from Platform Verified to Unverified across all Trading Partner Records platform-wide immediately. The badge is a property of the Business entity \- the reversion is automatic and reflected everywhere simultaneously. |
| **Active payment links on tier drop** | **Existing links honoured; new operations blocked** | Payment links already generated under Tier 2 remain valid and honoured \- they reflect the tier state at creation. From the moment of tier drop, new Tier 2 operations are blocked: no new payment links, no new invoices, no new ZATCA submissions, until the tier is restored through re-approval. |
| **Historical documents on tier drop** | **Immutable** | Historical invoices and documents issued under the dropped tier are never retroactively affected by the tier change. They always reflect the state at creation time. |
| **Section-specific tier preservation** | **Tier 1 preserved when only Section 2 fields rejected** | If a business is at Tier 2 and a Section 2 field is rejected, the business drops below Tier 2 but retains Tier 1\. Tier 1 is only revoked if Section 1 fields are rejected. Tier 1 capabilities (view, add to network, appear as Platform Verified) remain active during a Section 2 Action Required state. |
| **Bank account update \- Tier 3** | **Settlement frozen during re-verification** | When a Tier 3 business updates their bank account details, Tier 3 is immediately suspended. Settlement payouts are frozen \- no payouts to old or new IBAN during the review period. The bank account update is flagged as urgent in the admin queue. Tier 3 reinstates immediately upon admin approval of the new IBAN. The business is notified at submission that settlement will freeze until the new IBAN is approved. |

# **10\. Ops Process Requirements**

The following cases require defined operational processes to be specified in PRD 3 (Admin Verification Interface). Each case represents a scenario where the platform surfaces a case to the Qawafel Operations team requiring human judgment and action.

| Case | Name | Trigger | Ops Action Required |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **TIN-matched possible duplicate review** | TIN match found without CR/UNN confirmation | Ops reviews possible duplicate case. Investigates both records. Contacts parties if necessary. Confirms legitimate entity and either resolves the duplicate or dismisses the case. |
| **2** | **Corrective merge action** | Auto-merge later proves incorrect | Ops separates records, reassigns historical transactions to the correct Business record, and creates a new Trading Partner Record where needed. Merge log used as evidence source. |
| **3** | **Duplicate CR registration** | CR belongs to Business registered but pending verification and second registration attempt received | Ops contacts both parties to confirm the legitimate representative. Resolves which registration is the valid one and closes the duplicate. |
| **4** | **Non-taxable status reversal** | Business contacts support to reverse non-taxable declaration (e.g. crossed SAR 375,000 VAT threshold) | Ops receives support ticket. Updates Taxable Business toggle from Off to On. Fields added: VAT Registration Number and VAT Certificate upload. TIN is already on record \- it is required at registration for all businesses regardless of taxability. Triggers field-level admin review for newly added fields only. Tier 1 remains active throughout. Historical non-taxable invoices remain immutable. |
| **5** | **Bank account update post-Tier 3** | Tier 3 business submits a new IBAN | Case flagged as urgent in admin queue. Ops prioritizes review to minimize settlement freeze window. Admin reviews new IBAN using the same mathematical validation and bank name cross-reference as initial verification. Tier 3 reinstates on approval. |
| **6** | **Merge log review** | Audit, compliance, or dispute investigation | Super Admin and Operations can access the full merge evidence trail for any Business record at any time: matched fields, source precedence, timestamp, and initiating trigger. |

# **11\. Parked & Open Items**

The following items are parked. They are not open questions \- they are known future decisions that depend on external inputs or later-phase work.

| Item | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Financing eligibility check timing** | Whether financing eligibility is re-checked at invoice time or at financing submission time. Deferred. |
| **Buyer financing \- ARB criteria** | Whether owner verification or a specific tier is required for buyer financing with ARB. This is an ARB banking partner requirement, not a platform decision. Flagged as open pending ARB eligibility specification. |
| **Business Directory search** | Search businesses by trade name without knowing the CR. Deferred to Q4 as a natural output of the Business Directory module. |
| **Orphaned Trading Partner Record hygiene** | Admin tooling to surface and manually resolve Trading Partner Records that could not be auto-matched on a Business's self-registration. Future ops capability, not a launch requirement. |
| **Wathq integration** | Automated real-time CR and National ID validation via Wathq API. Deferred \- admin manual review is the sole verification path until Wathq is live. |
| **Relationship-level contact fields** | Relationship-level contact fields \- a future enhancement that introduces a separate merchant-owned contact layer per Trading Partner Record, distinct from the platform-owned contact fields. This layer would allow sellers to maintain a direct day-to-day contact (e.g. procurement manager's email) that is not subject to merge overwrite. Merchant-owned fields beyond this (internal notes, custom labels) are out of scope entirely for the current version and will be revisited in a future phase. |

# 🔌 Draft Business Registration & Onboarding

**PRD 1 \- Business Registration & Onboarding**

Sign-Up, Onboarding Wizard, Ownership Invitation, Multi-Business Login & Progressive Access

**Version 2.0  |  Status: Draft \- Internal EPD Review**

Depends on: Document 0 \- Business Logic Decisions Record  |  Companion: PRD 2 (Trading Partner Management), PRD 3 (Admin Verification)

# **1\. Purpose & Scope**

This PRD defines the complete business registration and onboarding experience on the APEX platform. It covers sign-up, the onboarding wizard, the ownership invitation mechanic, multi-business login and in-session switching, the progressive tier unlocking model as admin sections are approved, dashboard states per tier, the re-submission flow when the admin rejects fields, account settings, and account lifecycle policies.

|  |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **In scope** | Sign-up (email \+ password). Onboarding wizard: Step 1 Account Creator Details, Step 2 Core Business Identification, Step 3 Beneficial Owners, Step 4 Bank Account Details. Taxable Business toggle. VAT-registered declaration. Section-by-section submission. Ownership invitation flow (conditional on role declared in Step 1). Save & Continue Later with dashboard resume banner. Multi-business login, entity selection, and in-session context switching. Dashboard states per verification tier. Re-submission flow after admin rejection. Some account settings including business notification email. Account lifecycle and inactivity expiry policy. Tier unlock notifications. |
| **Out of scope** | OAuth sign-up (Google / Microsoft) \- deferred. OTP email verification at sign-up \- deferred. Forgot password / password reset \- deferred. Plan selection and payment integration \- deferred. ZATCA integration during onboarding \- deferred. Wathq real-time CR validation \- deferred. |
| **Depends on** | Document 0 for all business logic. PRD 3 (Admin Verification) for the admin-side section approvals that trigger tier unlocks referenced in this PRD. |

# **2\. User Types**

| First Registrant | The person who creates the business account on APEX. Receives the Admin or Owner role depending on their role declaration in Step 1\. Declares their role in Step 1 of the onboarding wizard: either as the company owner or as an authorised registrant. Their Full Name, Work Email, Mobile Number, and Designation are captured in Step 1\. No restriction on who registers. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Legal Owner / Authorised Representative** | The individual named on the Commercial Registration as the legal representative. Their identity details are captured in Step 3 (Beneficial Owners). If the first registrant declared themselves as the company owner in Step 1, their Step 1 data pre-fills Step 3 fields and no ownership invitation is sent. If the first registrant declared themselves as an authorised registrant, an ownership invitation is shown in Step 3 and sent to the legal owner, who accepts and holds the Owner role. |
| **Multi-Business User** | A user who is a member of more than one business on APEX. At login they see a business selection screen and choose which business context to enter. Once inside the platform, they can switch between businesses using the in-session business switcher in the navigation bar \- no logout required. The business selection screen used at login and the in-session switcher share the same interface and logic. |

# **3\. Sign-Up**

Sign-up is the first step. A person creates their APEX user account with email and password. There is no verification step, no OTP, and no social login in this phase. On successful registration the user proceeds immediately to the onboarding wizard.

| FR ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **FR-1.1** | Sign-up screen accepts email address and password only. | User submits email \+ password and account is created. System redirects to onboarding wizard immediately. | Must Have |
| **FR-1.2** | Email address must be unique across all APEX accounts. | Duplicate email returns inline error: 'An account with this email already exists. Log in instead.' | Must Have |
| **FR-1.3** | Password minimum complexity: at least 12 characters, 1 uppercase letter, 1 lowercase letter, 1 special character, 1 number. A live validation checklist is shown as the user types \- each rule turns green when met. | Live checklist updates silently on each keystroke. All five rules must be met before the form can be submitted. Submit button disabled until all rules satisfied. | Must Have |
| **FR-1.4** | No OTP, no email verification, no SSO buttons in this phase. | Sign-up screen contains none of these elements. | Must Have |
| **FR-1.5** | On successful sign-up the user is directed to the onboarding wizard Step 1 (Account Creator Details) with no intermediate screen. | Onboarding wizard Step 1 loads immediately after account creation. | Must Have |
| **FR-1.6** | At registration, the platform checks whether the business's CR/UNN submitted in Step 2 already belongs to an active registered business or a pending registration on APEX. | If CR/UNN belongs to an active registered business: registration step blocks with message: 'This business is already registered on APEX. If you are a member of this business, please request access from your account administrator.' If CR/UNN belongs to a pending registration: second registration is blocked and the case is routed to the Qawafel Operations team as a duplicate registration case for manual resolution. | Must Have |

# **4\. Onboarding Wizard**

The onboarding wizard collects all information required for admin verification. It is divided into four steps. Step 1 (Account Creator Details) and Step 2 (Core Business Identification) are mandatory and cannot be skipped. Steps 3 and 4 can be saved and completed later. Each section can be submitted independently for admin review as soon as its required fields are complete \- full completion of all four steps is not required before section-level submission begins.

## **4.1 Wizard Structure & Navigation**

| FR ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **FR-2.1** | The wizard has four steps: Account Creator Details (Step 1), Core Business Identification (Step 2), Beneficial Owners (Step 3), Bank Account Details (Step 4). A progress indicator shows completion status per step. | Progress indicator shows four steps. Each step shows Completed, Current, or Incomplete state. | Must Have |
| **FR-2.2** | Steps 1 and 2 cannot be skipped. Step 1 requires role selection and all required fields before proceeding. Step 2 requires all required fields before proceeding to Step 3\. | No Skip button on Steps 1 or 2\. | Must Have |
| **FR-2.3** | Steps 3 and 4 can be partially completed and saved for later via Save & Continue Later. When the user saves mid-wizard and navigates away, a resume banner appears on the Dashboard showing the step they left on with a direct Resume Now link. | Partial progress persists. On return wizard opens at the saved step with all previously entered data pre-filled. Dashboard shows resume banner with step reference. Banner disappears on submission. | Must Have |
| **FR-2.4** | All form fields auto-save on blur using local storage \- no server call per field interaction. Save & Continue Later triggers an explicit server-side save, persisting all current field values to the server. Server-side persistence guarantees cross-device and cross-browser continuation. If the user closes the browser without clicking Save & Continue Later, local storage preserves progress for same-device same-browser return only. The resume dashboard banner appears only after a server-side save event. | Blur auto-save uses local storage. Save & Continue Later persists to server. Cross-device continuation supported when server-side save has been triggered. Resume banner visible only after server-side save. | Must Have |

# **7\. Dashboard States per Verification Tier**

The dashboard experience changes as the business progresses through verification tiers. Each tier has a defined banner, access level, and primary CTA. Tiers are unlocked progressively as the admin approves individual sections and clicks the section-level CTA \- not all-or-nothing. See Document 0 Section 5 (Progressive Access Matrix) for the full capability list per tier.

## **7.1 First Login Behaviour**

On the first login of a newly self-registered business, before the dashboard tier state renders, the platform shows a one-time opt-in prompt offering to surface transactions where the business was a direct party prior to registration \- specifically transactions where they appeared as buyer on another platform business's payment link or invoice. The prompt is shown once. The business can accept or dismiss. Full behaviour including opt-in scope, the pre-registration activity view, and the account settings toggle is defined in PRD 2 FR-D.9 and FR-D.11

| Status | Banner message | Platform access | Primary CTA |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Pending Verification (submitted, awaiting review) | Your account is under review. Estimated review time: 24–48 hours. You can explore the platform in the meantime. | Platform navigation visible but all transactional features locked. | Explore Platform |
| Tier 1 \- Core Business Identification Confirmed (mid-review) | Your business identity has been confirmed. You can now add businesses to your network and create or import invoices. Full access unlocks once your complete review is approved. | Login, view, add businesses to network, create/import invoices, appear as Platform Verified to others. | Explore Platform |
| Action Required (fields rejected) | Action needed \- some information requires correction. Please review and resubmit. \[Fix Issues Now\] | Same as pre-submission. Fix Issues Now CTA opens the re-submission wizard. | Fix Issues Now |
| Tier 2 \- Verified, Bank account pending  | Your account is verified. Your bank account details are pending verification. Settlement payouts will be available once verified | Full commercial access: invoicing, payment links, payments, ZATCA submission (taxable businesses), invoice financing.  Settlement payouts not yet available. | Explore Platform |
| Tier 3 \- Fully Active, Bank account Verified  | Full access, no restrictions. | All platform capabilities including settlement payouts. | Banner dismiss |

Tier banners are shown on the dashboard page. The Action Required banner is not dismissible. When all tiers are approved, a dismiss CTA appears to remove the banner or automatically dismiss the banner.

# **10\. Account Lifecycle & Inactivity Policy**

The platform enforces an inactivity policy to prevent abandoned registrations from holding CR numbers indefinitely. CR uniqueness is enforced at the database level \- an abandoned registration that holds a CR number permanently could block legitimate future registrations for that business. The inactivity rules apply universally regardless of prior tier status \- a business that was previously verified and dropped below Tier 1 due to a rejection follows the same thresholds as a business that never submitted.

| FR ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **FR-AL.1** | Accounts created but never submitted for review are subject to inactivity expiry. A warning email is sent after 30 days of inactivity. If no action is taken within 60 days of account creation, the registration expires. | Warning email sent at 30-day inactivity mark. Expiry occurs at 60 days of inactivity if no action taken after warning. Warning email directs the user to resume their onboarding. | Must Have |
| **FR-AL.2** | Accounts in 'Action Required' state with no re-submission activity are subject to a shorter inactivity threshold regardless of prior verification tier. A warning email is sent after 14 days of inactivity. If no re-submission is made within 30 days of the rejection, the registration expires. CR/UNN released, email freed, record soft-deleted | Warning email sent at 14-day inactivity mark. Expiry occurs at 30 days if no re-submission after warning. | Must Have |
| **FR-AL.3** | On expiry: the registration record is soft-deleted, the CR/UNN number is released and becomes available for a new registration attempt, and the email address is freed for re-use. | Registration record soft-deleted on expiry. CR/UNN number released and available immediately for a new registration. Email address freed. Soft-deleted record preserved internally for audit purposes \- not permanently purged. | Must Have |
| **FR-AL.4** | Warning emails are sent to the registrant's work email and include a clear call to action to resume onboarding or re-submit corrections. | Warning email includes direct link to resume or resubmit. Email content follows notification definitions in Section 11\. | Must Have |

# 🤝 Draft Trading Partner Management

**PRD 2 \- Trading Partner Management**

Path A (Manual), Path B (ZATCA Invoice Import), Path C (CSV/API), Badge Model, Merge Logic & UX Journeys

**Version 2.0  |  Status: Draft \- Internal EPD Review**

Depends on: Document 0 \- Business Logic Decisions Record  |  Companion: PRD 1 (Registration), PRD 3 (Admin Verification)

# **1\. Purpose & Scope**

This PRD defines the trading partner management system on the APEX platform \- how registered businesses add and manage their trading partners. APEX models two distinct concepts: the Business (the canonical real-world entity, identified by CR/UNN) and the Trading Partner Record (a relationship-scoped data structure in a business's network, referencing the canonical Business). This PRD covers three business addition paths: manual CR entry (Path A), automatic extraction from invoice import (Path B), and contact via API or bulk upload (Path C). It also covers the badge model, the automatic merge logic when a Business self-registers, the Business profile field set, and the UX journeys for all paths including payment link sharing and buyer financing invitation.

|  |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **In scope** | Path A: manual business addition with CR/UNN as anchor, legal business name (Arabic) required. Path B: automatic Trading Partner Record creation from ZATCA invoice import. Path C: contact via API import or bulk CSV upload. Business profile field set. Badge model (Unverified / Platform Verified). Internal quality labels (four values). Automatic merge on self-registration including aliases and audit trail. Concurrent registration scenarios. Clean slate with opt-in for pre-registration history. Business Network directory. UX journeys for all paths including payment link sharing with missing contact fields and buyer financing invitation. |
| **Out of scope** | Search businesses by trade name \- deferred to Q4 Business Directory. Admin tooling for orphaned Trading Partner Records \- future ops capability. Business-initiated dispute mechanism \- not in scope per Document 0\. |
| **Depends on** | Document 0 for all business logic. PRD 1 for the business verification tiers that determine which business addition actions are available. PRD 3 for admin section approval that triggers Platform Verified badge on Business merge. |

# **2\. Business Data Model**

The Trading Partner Record represents a trading relationship between a registered business and another Business in their network. It is scoped per business \- each registered business maintains its own Business Network (their set of Trading Partner Records). Records are created via Path A or populated via Path B. Contact details are enriched via any path including Path C. The badge displayed on a Trading Partner Record is a property of the referenced Business entity \- not of the record itself. When the Business's verification state changes, the badge updates automatically across all Trading Partner Records that reference it.

## **2.1 Business Profile Fields**

| Field | Type | Required at creation | Notes | Editable by Business |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| CR/UNN number | Number | Yes | Primary matching key. Required at creation for Path A. Extracted from invoice additional ID field for Path B where present. | No (read-only always) |
| Legal business name (Arabic) | Text | Yes | Required at creation for Path A. Extracted from ZATCA invoice buyer name for Path B. | No (read-only always) |
| Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) | Number | Optional | Secondary matching key. 10-digit number. Extracted from ZATCA invoice buyer TIN for Path B. Always present for all businesses regardless of taxability. | No (read-only always) |
| VAT Registration Number | Number | Optional | 15-digit number starting and ending with 3\. Only present for VAT-registered businesses. Present when the Taxable Business toggle is On. Not present for non-taxable businesses. Distinct from TIN \- not the same field. Extracted from ZATCA invoice where present. | No (read-only always) |
| Email address | Email | Optional | Required to share payment links via email and to send buyer financing invitations. Never extracted from ZATCA invoice \- must come via Path A manual entry or Path C. Prompted at share or invite time if absent. Platform-owned on merge event \- overwritten by verified Business data. | No (read-only always)  |
| Phone number | Phone | Optional | Required to share payment links via WhatsApp. Never extracted from ZATCA invoice. Prompted at share time if absent. Platform-owned on merge event \- overwritten by verified Business data. | No (read-only always)  |
| National address | Text | Optional | Extracted from ZATCA invoice buyer address fields for Path B. Overwritten by verified data on merge. | No (read-only always) |
| Aliases | Text array | \- | Platform-managed. Populated at merge time with prior names from pre-merge records. Read-only. Visible in Business profile as 'Also known as'. Included in search results but not displayed as primary name. | No (platform-managed always) |
| Badge status | System | \- | Platform-managed. Property of the Business entity, surfaced through the Trading Partner Record. Two states: Unverified (default) and Platform Verified (set when the referenced Business reaches Tier 1). | No (platform-managed always) |
| Internal quality label | System | \- | Platform-managed. Four values: Manually Entered, ZATCA Referenced Single Seller, ZATCA Referenced Multiple Sellers, Business Supplied. Never shown externally. | No (platform-managed always) |
| Source | System | \- | Platform-managed. Values: Path A / Path B / Path C. Audit use. | N/A |
| Linked platform account | System | \- | Platform-managed. Populated on self-registration and exact CR/UNN match at Tier 1\. | N/A |

No (read-only always) in the Editable by Business column means existing field values cannot be overwritten by any business action. Empty fields can still be populated through gap-fill mechanisms: Path B enrichment, Path C enrichment, and for email and phone specifically, at payment link share time or financing invitation time

# **3\. Path A \- Manual Business Addition**

Path A is the flow when a registered business manually adds a trading partner to their Business Network. The CR/UNN number is the required anchor identifier. Legal business name in Arabic is required as the display name. All other fields are optional at creation.

Path A is only available to businesses at Tier 1 or above. A business below Tier 1 cannot add trading partners.

# **4\. Path B \- Invoice Import Business Extraction (not a user action)**

Path B creates or enriches Trading Partner Records automatically from imported invoices. When an invoice is imported the platform extracts buyer identity fields and either creates a new Trading Partner Record or enriches an existing one.

ZATCA Phase 2 validates buyer TIN format only \- not existence. Path B data is format-validated, not existence-validated. Path B records carry the Unverified badge regardless of invoice volume. See Document 0 for the confirmed technical finding.

## **4.1 Fields Extracted from ZATCA Invoice XML** **(Partially Linked to Path C \- API Import section 5.3)**

| Extraction status | Fields |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Always extracted** | Legal business name (Arabic), TIN where present, national address fields (building number, street, district, city). |
| **Conditionally extracted** | CR/UNN number \- extracted when present in the invoice additional ID field. Not always populated by the seller's system. VAT Registration Number \- extracted when present. |
| **Never extracted** | Email address and phone number. These fields are not part of the ZATCA XML standard for the buyer. Path B records always have a contact detail gap. Path C exists specifically to fill this gap. |

If no match a new Trading Partner Record is created. | Must Have |
| **FR-B.2** | If an exact CR/UNN match is found the platform enriches the existing record with any new fields extracted from the invoice. Path B only fills gaps \- it does not overwrite existing field values. | Enrichment adds fields not previously present. If the record already has a legal name and the invoice carries a different one, the existing name is preserved. | Must Have |
| **FR-B.3** | If no match is found a new Trading Partner Record is created with extracted fields, Unverified badge, and internal quality label set to ZATCA Referenced Single Seller. | New record created with all extractable fields populated. Badge: Unverified. Internal label: ZATCA Referenced Single Seller. | Must Have |
| **FR-B.4** | If a subsequent invoice from a different enrolled seller carries the same CR/UNN or TIN and matches the same Trading Partner Record the internal quality label upgrades to ZATCA Referenced Multiple Sellers. | Second distinct seller's invoice matching same record triggers internal label upgrade. Badge remains Unverified. | Must Have |
| **FR-B.5** | Path B record creation and enrichment happens asynchronously in the background without requiring any user action. Invoice import completion must not be delayed by trading partner processing. | Invoice import triggers processing in the background. Business Network updates without user interaction. Invoice import response does not wait for processing to complete. | Must Have |
| **FR-B.6** | If a Path B extracted CR/UNN matches a currently registered and Tier 1+ platform Business, the Trading Partner Record is immediately assigned Platform Verified badge and the linked platform account field is populated. | CR/UNN match against a registered Tier 1+ Business immediately sets badge to Platform Verified and links the account. | Must Have |

# **5\. Path C \- Contact Import & Business Record Creation via API or Bulk Upload**

Path C is a dual-purpose mechanism. It allows registered businesses to create new Trading Partner Records and to enrich existing ones with contact details that ZATCA invoices can never carry. Path C operates in two modes: creation mode and enrichment mode. Creation mode applies when a submitted CR/UNN number has no existing Trading Partner Record in the seller's network. Enrichment mode applies when a matching record already exists \- contact fields are gap-filled without overwriting existing values.

## **5.1 Why Path C Exists**

Registered businesses accumulate buyer relationships outside APEX \- through prior trading, offline agreements, or systems not connected to the platform. Path A allows manual entry of these businesses one at a time, but this is impractical at volume. Path C provides a scalable equivalent: sellers can supply a structured file or API payload containing buyer business identity and contact data, and the platform handles record creation and enrichment automatically.

For trading partners that already exist via Path B (extracted from ZATCA invoice imports), Path C fills the gap left by ZATCA's structural inability to carry contact fields. Without contact data, buyer financing invitations cannot be sent. Path C resolves this without requiring the seller to edit records one by one.

## **5.2 Merge Logic for Path C Records**

Path C enrichment events (adding contact fields to an existing record) follow the gap-fill rule: contact fields are added where absent and existing values are never overwritten by a Path C submission. This gap-fill rule applies to Path C enrichment and Path B enrichment events only.

When a Business self-registers and reaches Tier 1, the merge event follows the full overwrite rule: verified self-registered data overwrites all Trading Partner Record fields \- including identity fields (CR/UNN, legal name, TIN, VAT Registration Number, national address) and contact fields (email, phone). The gap-fill protection does not apply to the merge trigger event. See Document 0 Section 8 for complete merge behavior.

# **7\. Automatic Merge on Self-Registration**

When a Business self-registers on APEX and reaches Tier 1 (Core Business Identification section fully approved by admin and section CTA clicked), the platform automatically matches their CR/UNN against all existing Trading Partner Records platform-wide. Matching records are merged silently with no notification to either party.

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

| **FR-D.2** | For each Trading Partner Record where the CR/UNN matches exactly, the platform performs a full overwrite of all record fields with the self-registered Business's verified data. Full overwrite includes identity fields (CR/UNN, legal name, TIN, VAT Registration Number, national address) and contact fields (email, phone). Only exact CR/UNN matches trigger a merge. | Merge updates all fields including contact fields with verified data. One-digit CR/UNN transpositions do not merge. Contact fields are overwritten by verified Business contact data. | Must Have |
| **FR-D.3** | Prior names from pre-merge records are stored as searchable aliases on the Business record at merge time. The verified legal Arabic name is canonical and displayed as primary. Aliases are visible in the business profile as 'Also known as' \- read-only, not editable. Alias names are included in directory search results. | Aliases field populated at merge with prior names. Verified legal name shown as primary. 'Also known as' section visible in business profile. Aliases searchable in Business Network search. | Must Have |
| **FR-D.4** | Historical transactions referenced by Trading Partner Records involved in the merge are re-pointed to the survivor Business record so the seller sees a clean unified history. A 'merged record' indicator is shown on affected historical documents. | Transaction history unified under survivor record post-merge. 'Merged record' indicator visible on affected historical invoices and payment links. The merged record indicator includes a **Contact Support** link. Clicking it opens a Zendesk support ticket pre-populated with the business name, record ID, and merge timestamp. | Must Have |
| **FR-D.5** | After merge the Trading Partner Record badge changes to Platform Verified  | Badge updates immediately post-merge.  | Must Have |
| **FR-D.6** | The merge is silent. No notification is sent to the business that owns the Trading Partner Record or to the newly registered Business. | No email, no in-app notification, no banner triggered by the merge event. | Must Have |
| **FR-D.7** | An immutable audit trail is stored for every merge event: matched fields and their values at time of merge, source precedence, timestamp, initiating trigger, and which records were consolidated. Audit trail is accessible to Super Admin and Operations roles only. | Merge audit log created for every merge event. Log accessible via internal admin tooling. Never visible to business users beyond the merged record indicator. | Must Have |
| **FR-D.8** | Historical invoice snapshots are never updated by the merge. # **8\. Concurrent Registration Scenarios**

The following scenarios define platform behavior when a Business is in various registration states at the time another business attempts to add it to their network, or when a Business registers while Trading Partner Records already exist for it.

|  | Scenario | Defined Behavior |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **Business ABC is pending verification; Business XYZ tries to add ABC via Path A** | System recognises the CR as belonging to a registered-but-pending Business. Message shown: 'This business is registered on APEX and is pending verification.' Pre-populates CR/UNN and legal name from submitted onboarding data only \- no verified data yet. Record created with Unverified badge. When ABC later reaches Tier 1, merge fires and upgrades the record. |
| **2** | **Business ABC is Tier 1+; Business XYZ tries to add ABC via Path A** | System detects Tier 1+ match. Pre-populates verified fields. Message shown: 'This business is registered on APEX. Their verified details have been pre-filled.' Record created with Platform Verified badge immediately. |
| **3** | **XYZ manually added ABC via Path A; ABC then registers and reaches Tier 1** | No impact on ABC's registration flow. When ABC reaches Tier 1, merge fires automatically against XYZ's existing Trading Partner Record and upgrades it. |
| **4** | **XYZ ZATCA-imported ABC via Path B; ABC then registers and reaches Tier 1** | Same as Scenario 3\. ABC registers normally. Tier 1 merge fires and upgrades the Path B record. |
| **5** | **Multiple businesses manually added ABC; ABC then registers** | Platform-wide simultaneous merge fires across all Trading Partner Records with exact CR/UNN match at Tier 1\. Each business's record is upgraded independently. |
| **6** | **Multiple businesses ZATCA-imported ABC; ABC then registers** | Same as Scenario 5\. Platform-wide simultaneous merge across all Path B records. |
