# 🌐 Draft Admin Verification Interface

**PRD 3 \- Admin Verification Interface**

Verification Queue, Section-Level Approval, Tier Unlocking, Field-Level Review, Submission History & Ops Process Requirements

**Version 2.0  |  Status: Draft \- Internal EPD Review**

Depends on: Document 0 \- Business Logic Decisions Record  |  Companion: PRD 1 (Registration), PRD 2 (Trading Partner Management)

# **1\. Purpose & Scope**

This PRD defines the admin verification interface \- the tools Qawafel Operations staff use to review business submissions, approve or reject individual fields, confirm tier unlocks through section-level CTAs, and manage operational cases including merge duplicates, inactive accounts, bank account updates, and non-taxable status reversals.

The verification model is progressive, not all-or-nothing. Admin reviews fields within each section independently. When all actionable fields in a section are approved, the admin clicks the section-level CTA to confirm the section and trigger the corresponding tier unlock. Tier unlocks are not automatic on field approval \- they require the explicit section-level CTA. Each tier unlock is immediate \- the business gains the corresponding capabilities while the rest of the review is still in progress.

All business logic decisions are in Document 0\. This PRD contains admin interface requirements and acceptance criteria only.

|  |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **In scope** | Pending verification queue with tier-aware status and queue ordering. Field-level approve/reject with section-level CTA for independent tier unlocking. Non-taxable declaration handling. CR cross-reference step. IBAN mathematical validation display with hard gate for Invalid results. Submission history and re-submission comparison view. Ownership invitation monitoring. All-businesses directory with role-based access controls. Disputes tab with ops case management: TIN-matched duplicates, corrective merge actions, duplicate CR registrations, non-taxable status reversals, and merge log review. Bank account update post-Tier 3 handling in Pending Queue. Tier drop cascading effects. |
| **Out of scope** | Wathq API integration \- deferred. Admin dashboard analytics \- deferred. Bulk actions across multiple businesses \- deferred. Business impersonation \- Roles & Permissions PRD. Admin-initiated business creation \- future capability. Automated document quality checks \- deferred. |
| **Admin roles with access** | Operations: full access \- primary role for verification and disputes. Super Admin: full access including merge log. Support: view-only \- can see records and history, cannot approve, reject, or change status. Finance/Settlement: bank details and settlement-relevant fields. Risk & Compliance: risk flags and compliance-relevant fields. |

# **2\. Business Status Model (Admin View)**

| Status | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Pending Verification** | Business submitted for review. No tier unlocked. Admin review not yet started or in progress. Admin can begin reviewing fields and unlock tiers as sections are approved via section-level CTAs. |
| **Tier 1 Active (mid-review)** | Admin approved all actionable fields in Section 1 and clicked the 'Approve Core Business Identification → Unlock Business Access' CTA. Business has Tier 1 capabilities and appears as Platform Verified to other businesses. Section 2 and/or Section 3 review still pending. |
| **Tier 2 Active (mid-review)** | Admin approved all of Section 1 and Section 2 and clicked both section-level CTAs. Business has full commercial capabilities. Section 3 (Bank) review may still be pending. |
| **Action Required** | Admin clicked 'Send Section for Correction'. One or more fields rejected. Business notified. Tier drop effects apply as defined below. |
| **Active (Tier 2 or Tier 3\)** | All required sections fully approved via section CTAs. Business has full access. Business exits the queue. |

## **2.1 Tier Drop Behavior on Rejection**

Tier drops have cascading effects that must be handled explicitly by the platform.

| Scenario | Cascading Effects |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Section 1 field rejected \- Tier 1 drop** | Business drops below Tier 1\. Badge reverts from Platform Verified to Unverified platform-wide across all Trading Partner Records immediately. Active payment links already generated remain valid and honoured. New Tier 1 and Tier 2 operations blocked from moment of tier drop. Historical documents are immutable. |
| **Section 2 field rejected \- Tier 2 drop** | Business drops below Tier 2 but retains Tier 1\. Tier 1 capabilities (view, add to network, appear as Platform Verified) remain active. Payment links already generated under Tier 2 remain valid and honoured. New Tier 2 operations (payment links, invoices, ZATCA submission) blocked until Section 2 corrections are re-approved. Tier 1 badge is preserved. |
| **Section 3 field rejected \- Tier 3 suspended** | Settlement payouts suspended until bank account is re-verified. Tier 2 operations unaffected. Business retains full commercial capabilities. |
| **Bank account update post-Tier 3** | When a Tier 3 business submits a new IBAN, Tier 3 is immediately suspended. Settlement payouts frozen \- no payouts to old or new IBAN during review. Case flagged as urgent in Pending Queue. Tier 3 reinstated on IBAN approval. Business notified of settlement freeze at submission. |

# **3\. Pending Verification Queue**

The Pending Queue is the primary working view for the Operations team. It shows all businesses with status Pending Verification or Action Required. Active businesses do not appear in the queue. Bank account update post-Tier 3 cases are surfaced here as urgent \- they are tied directly to the verification tier and must be actioned with minimum delay to lift the settlement freeze.

## **3.1 Queue Columns**

Business legal name (Arabic)

CR/UNN number

Submission date and time

Attempt number \- 1st, 2nd, 3rd… (re-submissions clearly badged)

Current tier status \- Unstarted, Tier 1 Active, Tier 2 Active, Action Required

Ownership invitation status \- Self-declared Owner / Accepted / Pending (with days elapsed since sent) / Not sent

Non-taxable indicator \- flagged where the business declared non-taxable at onboarding

Urgency flag \- flagged for bank account update cases requiring expedited review

Review CTA \- opens the business detail and review view

## **3.2 Queue Ordering**

Urgent cases (bank account update post-Tier 3\) appear first. Re-submissions (attempt number \>= 2\) appear next regardless of submission time. New first-time submissions follow in FIFO order by submission timestamp.

## **3.3 Queue Functional Requirements**

| FR ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **FR-Q.1** | Queue shows only businesses with status Pending Verification or Action Required. Active businesses are absent from the queue unless a re-submission is pending. | Active businesses absent from queue unless a re-submission is pending. | Must Have |
| **FR-Q.2** | Queue sorted: urgent cases first, then re-submissions, then FIFO by submission timestamp. | Bank account update cases shown first. Re-submitted business at T+10 appears above first-time submission at T+1 within the same priority tier. | Must Have |
| **FR-Q.3** | Re-submission rows carry a visible attempt number badge. | Attempt number visible on queue row. First-time submissions carry no badge. | Must Have |
| **FR-Q.4** | Non-taxable indicator shown on queue rows where the business declared non-taxable. | Non-taxable indicator visible on relevant queue rows. | Must Have |
| **FR-Q.5** | Ownership invitation status column shows one of four states: Self-declared Owner (registrant declared company ownership \- no invitation sent), Accepted, Pending with days elapsed since sent, Not sent. | Self-declared Owner shown where registrant declared company ownership. Accepted shown in green. Pending shown with elapsed days. Not sent shown where no invitation has been issued. | Must Have |
| **FR-Q.6** | Queue shows a running total count of pending submissions at the top. | Counter updates in real time as reviews are completed. | Should Have |
| **FR-Q.7** | Bank account update cases are flagged as urgent with a distinct visual indicator. These cases are prioritised at the top of the queue to minimise the settlement freeze window for the affected business. | Urgent flag visible on queue row. Urgent cases appear above re-submissions in queue ordering. | Must Have |

# **4\. Business Review View**

The review view is the admin's workspace for a single business submission. It presents all submitted fields organised into three sections \- each with individual field-level actions and a section-level CTA that confirms section completion and triggers the tier unlock.

For non-taxable businesses, TIN and VAT fields are absent from the Section 1 review \- not present at all, not shown as empty. The admin sees a Non-taxable business (self-declared) label and proceeds to approve the remaining Section 1 fields. The section-level CTA activates when all present actionable fields are approved.

When all fields in a section are approved, the section-level CTA becomes the most prominent element on screen. A prompt is shown: 'All fields approved \- click to unlock Tier X.' This ensures the admin cannot miss the confirmation step.

## **4.1 Review View Layout**

Business summary card \- read-only header: legal name (Arabic), email, CR/UNN, attempt number, current tier status, non-taxable indicator (if applicable), ownership invitation status.

Tier indicator \- shows which tiers are unlocked (Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3\) with clear visual state for each.

Tab 1: Core Business Identification \- all fields from onboarding Step 2\. Full section approval and section CTA click unlocks Tier 1\.

Tab 2 and Tab 3 render in a locked state until their prerequisite tier is confirmed

Tab 2: Beneficial Owners \- all fields from onboarding Step 3\. Full section approval and section CTA click completes Tier 2\.

Tab 3: Bank Account Details \- IBAN and derived bank fields. IBAN approval and section CTA click unlocks Tier 3\.

Submission history panel \- collapsible, shows all previous submissions with outcomes.

Section-level CTAs at the bottom of each tab: 'Approve \[Section Name\] → Unlock \[Tier\] Access' (active when all actionable fields in the tab are approved) and 'Send Section for Correction' (active when at least one field is rejected).

## **4.2 Field-Level Review \- Action Matrix**

The table below is the authoritative reference for every field in the review view, the admin action available, which tier the approval contributes to, and the verification method.

| Field | Admin action | Tier unlocked | Verification method |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Tab 1 \- Core Business Identification  (section CTA click unlocks Tier 1\)** |  |  |  |
| CR/UNN Number | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | Cross-check against uploaded CR certificate. Admin MUST also cross-reference the CR number against the MoC public portal to confirm the CR is active and registered. This field requires a MoC confirmation checkbox before approval can be saved. |
| Legal Business Name (Arabic) | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | Must match exactly as it appears on the CR certificate. |
| Upload CR Certificate | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | Admin opens document viewer. Confirms legal name and CR number match submission. Document must be unexpired. |
| Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | Verified via ZATCA portal. 10-digit number. Always present and required for all businesses regardless of taxability declaration. |
| VAT Registration Number | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | 15-digit number starting and ending with 3\. Only shown when the Taxable Business toggle is On. Not shown for non-taxable businesses. |
| Upload VAT Certificate | Approve / Reject | Tier 1 | Admin opens document viewer. Confirms VAT number matches submission. Only shown when the Taxable Business toggle is On. |
| Non-taxable declaration | Display only | \- | Shown as a read-only label: 'Non-taxable business (self-declared)' when the business switched the Taxable Business toggle Off at onboarding. VAT Registration Number and VAT Certificate upload are absent from the review for these businesses. TIN remains present and must be approved. Admin approves TIN and clicks the section CTA to complete Tier 1\. |
| Registered Address (National Address) | Display only | \- | Not verified by admin. Shown for reference only. |
| **Tab 2 \- Beneficial Owners  (section CTA click completes Tier 2\)** |  |  |  |
| Full Name | Approve / Reject | Tier 2 | Cross-check against uploaded owner ID document. Name must match exactly. When registrant declared company ownership in Step 1, this field is pre-filled from Step 1 Account Creator Details. |
| National ID (Saudi) or Iqama Number (resident) | Approve / Reject | Tier 2 | Cross-check against uploaded ID document. Number must match. |
| Upload ID Copy (National ID, Passport, or Iqama) | Approve / Reject | Tier 2 | Admin opens document viewer. Confirms document is clear, valid, unexpired, and matches name and ID number submitted. |
| Ownership status | Display only | \- | Read-only label: 'Self-declared owner' (registrant declared company ownership) or 'Ownership via invitation' with invitation status (Pending / Accepted). |
| **Tab 3 \- Bank Account Details  (section CTA click unlocks Tier 3\)** |  |  |  |
| IBAN | Approve / Reject | Tier 3 | System performs mathematical IBAN validation (format and checksum) before the review view renders. Admin sees validation result (Valid / Invalid) next to the IBAN field. If result is Invalid, the Approve action is disabled \- admin can only reject. If result is Valid, admin cross-references the bank name derived from the IBAN against the business's declared bank name before approving. Valid result is advisory \- not a compelled approval. |
| Bank Name | Display only | \- | Auto-derived from IBAN. No independent admin action required. |
| Account Holder Name | Display only | \- | Shown for reference alongside IBAN. |
| Bank Account Number | Display only | \- | Shown for reference. |

Non-taxable businesses: VAT Registration Number and VAT Certificate upload are completely absent from the Section 1 review view \- not shown as empty or greyed out. TIN is present and must be approved. The Non-taxable declaration label is displayed alongside TIN. The admin approves all Section 1 fields including TIN and clicks the section CTA. Tier 1 unlocks normally.

# **5\. Ownership Invitation Monitoring**

The admin interface surfaces ownership invitation status for each business. This is informational for all admin roles \- no admin role can resend, cancel, or modify an ownership invitation from the admin interface. That action belongs to the merchant's Admin role in business settings. Four states are possible: Self-declared Owner, Accepted, Pending, Not sent.

| FR ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **FR-O.1** | The review view and the all-businesses directory both show ownership invitation status per business: Self-declared Owner (registrant declared company ownership \- no invitation sent), Accepted, Pending (with days elapsed), or Not sent. | Ownership invitation status visible in both the review view and all-businesses directory for all admin roles. Read-only for all roles \- no action available. | Must Have |
| **FR-O.2** | The pending verification queue shows a flag on businesses where the ownership invitation has been outstanding for more than 7 days. Informational only \- does not affect queue ordering. | Queue row shows an indicator for invitations older than 7 days. | Should Have |
| **FR-O.3** | All admin roles can view ownership invitation status in read-only mode. No admin role has action buttons available on ownership invitation status. | Ownership invitation status visible to all admin roles in read-only view. No action buttons available for any role. | Must Have |

# **6\. All-Businesses Directory**

The all-businesses directory shows the complete canonical business registry used for look-up, audit, and operational support. It includes two types of records: registered businesses (businesses that have completed sign-up on APEX) and unregistered Business records (Trading Partner Records added by registered businesses via any path with no corresponding APEX account). Both types are shown together in a single unified directory view.

The all-businesses directory is an intentional exception to the per-business data isolation rule in PRD 2\. It is a defined operational surface. Access to seller-supplied contact data within this directory is governed by the role-based access controls below. Admin visibility into seller-supplied contact data is justified under legitimate interest in platform operations and compliance obligations (PDPL-relevant surface).

| FR ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **FR-D.1** | The directory shows all registered businesses. Registered business records display: Business legal name (Arabic), CR/UNN, Tier, Record type (REG), Verification status, Registrant email, Owner email, Owner invite status, Registration date, and View action. | All columns visible per registered business row. Record type indicator REG distinguishes registered businesses. | Must Have |
| **FR-D.2** | The directory also shows all unregistered Business records from across the platform. Unregistered Business records display: legal business name, CR/UNN number, badge status (Platform Verified / Unverified), record type (BP), and record source (Manual / ZATCA Import / Bulk Upload). | Unregistered Business records appear alongside registered businesses. Each unique CR/UNN appears once. Distinguished by a BP record type indicator. Both REG and BP type indicators explained in a visible legend. | Must Have |
| **FR-D.3** | The directory is filterable by record type (registered / unregistered), tier status, and badge status. Searchable by business name (Arabic) or CR/UNN number. | Filters and search apply in real time. All filter combinations supported. | Must Have |
| **FR-D.4** | Clicking View on a registered business opens the business profile. For an active business this is read-only mode. Clicking View on an unregistered Business record opens a profile panel showing all available fields, source, and badge status. | View opens the business profile. Unregistered Business profile panel accessible for all records. | Must Have |
| **FR-D.5** | Access to fields in the all-businesses directory is role-dependent: Super Admin and Operations have full record visibility including seller-supplied contact data (email, phone). Support can see business identity fields only (legal name, CR/UNN, tier status) \- no seller-supplied contact details. Finance/Settlement can see bank details and settlement-relevant fields only. Risk & Compliance can see risk flags and compliance-relevant fields only. | Role-based field visibility enforced in the directory. Support role cannot see email or phone fields on any record. Finance/Settlement and Risk & Compliance see only their role-relevant fields. Super Admin and Operations see all fields. | Must Have |

# **7\. Ops Process Requirements**

This section defines the operational cases that the Qawafel Operations team manages on the APEX admin interface. Cases are surfaced across two locations: the Pending Queue (for bank account updates that are directly tied to verification tier) and the Disputes tab (for all other cases requiring investigation and resolution).

## **7.1 Admin Interface Navigation**

The admin interface has three tabs:

| Tab | Purpose & Cases |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Pending Queue** | Primary working view for verification review. Contains all businesses with status Pending Verification or Action Required. Also surfaces bank account update post-Tier 3 cases as urgent flagged rows \- these are tier-dependent and must be actioned immediately to lift the settlement freeze. |
| **All Businesses** | Complete canonical business registry. Shows all registered and unregistered Business records. Used for look-up, audit, profile review, and merge log access. Role-based field visibility enforced. |
| **Disputes** | Dedicated tab for operational cases that require investigation and resolution: TIN-matched possible duplicates, corrective merge actions, duplicate CR registrations, non-taxable status reversals, and merge log reviews. Cases in this tab are not directly linked to the verification queue. |

## **7.2 Disputes Tab \- Case Lifecycle**

Every case in the Disputes tab follows a defined status lifecycle. Operations is the final decision maker on all cases \- no escalation path is defined for this phase.

| Status | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Open** | Case created by the platform trigger. Not yet actioned by Operations. Visible in Disputes tab with Open indicator. |
| **In Progress** | Operations has started working the case \- contacted parties, reviewed records, or initiated a resolution action. Case is actively being handled. |
| **Resolved** | Case closed with a defined outcome. Operations confirmed the action taken. Case moves to resolved history. Audit note required. |
| **Dismissed** | Case closed with no action required \- for example a TIN match was investigated and confirmed as two distinct businesses. Dismissal reason required. |

SLA: 24 hours from case creation for all Disputes tab cases. Bank account update cases in the Pending Queue have no fixed SLA \- priority queue position is the mechanism to minimise the settlement freeze window.

## **7.3 Case Definitions & Resolution Flows**

The following cases are surfaced in the Disputes tab unless noted otherwise. Each case definition includes the platform trigger, what Operations sees, the step-by-step resolution flow, and the available outcomes.

**Case 1 \- TIN-Matched Possible Duplicate Review**

Location: Disputes tab

| Case 1 \- TIN-Matched Possible Duplicate Review |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Trigger** | TIN match identified between two Trading Partner Records without a corresponding CR/UNN confirmation. Platform cannot auto-merge. |
| **What ops sees** | Side-by-side comparison panel showing both records: record IDs, matched TIN value, all available fields for each record, record sources (Path A / B / C), creation dates, and owning businesses. |
| **Resolution steps** | **1\.**  Open the case from the Disputes tab. **2\.**  Review the side-by-side field comparison. Check whether both records refer to the same real-world business. **3\.**  If additional information is needed, contact the businesses that own the records using the contact details in the record. **4\.**  Confirm whether the records are the same entity or two distinct businesses. **5\.**  Select the appropriate outcome and add a mandatory audit note before closing. |
| **Outcomes** | Confirm as duplicate \- platform merges the records and links them to the canonical Business entity. Dismiss as distinct entities \- records remain separate, possible duplicate flag cleared. Both outcomes logged permanently in the case audit trail. |
| **SLA** | 24 hours from case creation. |

**Case 2 \- Corrective Merge Action**

Location: Disputes tab

| Case 2 \- Corrective Merge Action |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Trigger** | A business reports an incorrect merge via the Contact Support link on the merged record indicator in their documents. The support ticket is routed from Zendesk to the Disputes tab as a Corrective Merge Action case. Cases can also be initiated manually by Operations during a merge log audit.  |
| **What ops sees** | Merge log for the affected Business record showing: matched fields and values at time of merge, source precedence, timestamp, initiating trigger, and which records were consolidated. |
| **Resolution steps** | **1\.**  Open the case from the Disputes tab. **2\.**  Review the merge log to understand what was merged and why. **3\.**  Identify the correct records that should exist separately. **4\.**  Use the record separation action: select the records to separate. **5\.**  Review the affected historical transactions and confirm reassignment to the correct Business record. **6\.**  Create a new Trading Partner Record where needed for the separated entity. **7\.**  Add a mandatory audit note documenting the reason for the corrective action and the outcome. **8\.**  Close the case as Resolved. |
| **Outcomes** | Resolved \- records separated, transactions reassigned, new Trading Partner Record created if needed. Corrective action itself cannot be undone without initiating another corrective action case. All steps logged in the merge audit trail. |
| **SLA** | 24 hours from case creation. |

**Case 3 \- Duplicate CR Registration**

Location: Disputes tab

| Case 3 \- Duplicate CR Registration |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Trigger** | A CR/UNN submitted at registration belongs to a business already registered but pending verification. A second registration attempt has been made for the same CR/UNN. |
| **What ops sees** | Both registration records side by side: submission timestamps, registrant names, registrant emails, step completion status for each, and contact details for both parties. |
| **Resolution steps** | **1\.**  Open the case from the Disputes tab. **2\.**  Review both registration records. Identify which represents the legitimate representative of the business. **3\.**  Contact both parties using the registrant contact details shown. **4\.**  Confirm the legitimate representative through direct communication. **5\.**  Approve the valid registration and close the duplicate. If the duplicate is the more complete submission, coordinate with the legitimate party to resubmit under the approved account. **6\.**  Add a mandatory audit note documenting which registration was confirmed as legitimate and why. **7\.**  Close the case as Resolved. |
| **Outcomes** | Resolved \- one registration approved, duplicate closed. If neither party can be confirmed, escalate to Super Admin and document the hold in the audit note. |
| **SLA** | 24 hours from case creation. |

**Case 4 \- Non-Taxable Status Reversal**

Location: Disputes tab \- triggered by support ticket from Zendesk

| Case 4 \- Non-Taxable Status Reversal |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Trigger** | A business has contacted support requesting reversal of their non-taxable declaration \- for example because they have crossed the SAR 375,000 VAT registration threshold. Support ticket routed from Zendesk. |
| **What ops sees** | Business profile with current non-taxable declaration status, support ticket summary from Zendesk, and the fields that will be revealed on toggle switch: TIN, VAT Registration Number, and VAT Certificate upload. |
| **Resolution steps** | **1\.**  Open the case from the Disputes tab. **2\.**  Review the support ticket to confirm the reversal request is legitimate and the reason is valid. **3\.**  Switch the Taxable Business toggle from Off to On in the admin interface. **4\.**  The following fields are now revealed and required: VAT Registration Number (15 digits, starts and ends with 3\) and VAT Certificate upload. TIN is already on record from registration and does not need to be re-submitted. **5\.**  Trigger field-level admin review for the newly added fields only. Tier 1 remains active throughout \- do not suspend access. **6\.**  Notify the business that their taxable status has been updated and that they must now submit their VAT Registration Number and VAT Certificate for review. **7\.**  Historical non-taxable invoices are not affected \- they remain immutable. **8\.**  Add an audit note and close the case as Resolved. |
| **Outcomes** | Resolved \- toggle switched, fields revealed, review triggered, business notified. Historical invoices unaffected. |
| **SLA** | 24 hours from case creation. |

**Case 5 \- Merge Log Review**

Location: All Businesses directory \- accessible from the business profile

| Case 5 \- Merge Log Review |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Trigger** | Audit, compliance, dispute resolution, or investigation requires review of a merge event for a specific Business record. |
| **What ops sees** | Full merge evidence trail for the selected Business record: matched fields and their values at time of merge, source precedence applied, timestamp of merge, initiating trigger (Tier 1 approval event), and which records were consolidated. |
| **Resolution steps** | **1\.**  Navigate to the All Businesses directory tab. **2\.**  Search for the Business record under investigation. **3\.**  Open the business profile and access the Merge Log section. **4\.**  Review the merge evidence trail. **5\.**  If the merge is confirmed as incorrect, initiate a Corrective Merge Action case (Case 2). **6\.**  If the review is for audit or compliance purposes only, no further action is required. |
| **Outcomes** | No case status required \- merge log review is a read-only audit action. If a corrective merge action is needed, a separate Case 2 is initiated. |
| **SLA** | 24 hours from case creation. |

## **7.4 Ops Process \- Functional Requirements**

| FR ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **OP-1** | TIN-matched possible duplicate review: when the platform identifies a TIN match without a corresponding CR/UNN confirmation, a possible duplicate case is created in the Disputes tab. | Possible duplicate case appears in Disputes tab with: both record IDs, matched TIN value, record sources, creation dates, and a side-by-side field comparison view. Operations can: Confirm as duplicate, Dismiss as distinct entities, or mark In Progress while contacting parties. Audit note required to close. | Must Have |
| **OP-2** | Corrective merge action: when an auto-merge proves incorrect, Operations must be able to initiate a corrective action to separate records and reassign transactions. | Corrective merge action available in Disputes tab. Action: select records to separate, review affected transactions, confirm reassignment, and add an audit note. All steps logged in merge audit trail. Corrective action cannot be undone without another corrective action case. | Must Have |
| **OP-3** | Duplicate CR registration: when a CR/UNN submitted at registration belongs to a business already registered but pending verification, the case is routed to the Disputes tab. | Duplicate CR case appears in Disputes tab with both registration records, submission timestamps, and registrant details. Operations contacts both parties, confirms legitimate representative, and resolves. Outcome options: approve one, close the duplicate; or place on hold pending further investigation. | Must Have |
| **OP-4** | Non-taxable status reversal: when a business contacts support to reverse their non-taxable declaration, the support ticket is routed from Zendesk and appears as a case in the Disputes tab. | Case appears in Disputes tab with business profile and Zendesk ticket summary. Ops switches Taxable Business toggle from Off to On, reveals VAT Registration Number and VAT Certificate upload fields, triggers field-level admin review for the newly revealed fields only. TIN already exists on the record and does not require re-review. Tier 1 remains active. Historical non-taxable invoices immutable. Business notified. | Must Have |
| **OP-5** | Bank account update post-Tier 3: when a Tier 3 business submits a new IBAN, the case is flagged as urgent in the Pending Queue and the settlement freeze begins immediately. | Urgent flag on Pending Queue row. Admin reviews new IBAN using mathematical validation and bank name cross-reference. If Invalid, Approve disabled. Settlement freeze shown on business dashboard. Tier 3 reinstated immediately on IBAN approval. Business notified. | Must Have |
| **OP-6** | Merge log review: Operations and Super Admin can access the complete merge audit trail for any Business record at any time from the All Businesses directory. | Merge log accessible from business profile in All Businesses directory. Log shows: matched fields, source precedence, timestamp, initiating trigger, and consolidated records. Read-only \- no edit actions. Available to Operations and Super Admin only. | Must Have |

# **1\. Purpose & Scope**

This PRD defines the role, permission, and access architecture for the APEX platform. It covers two domains: business user roles governing how merchant staff operate their accounts, and Qawafel internal admin roles governing how Qawafel Operations staff manage the platform.

This document is structured in two explicit layers:

| Layer 1 \- Locked | Role model, data architecture, and permission surface for all features with locked PRDs. Authoritative. Engineering builds from this layer now. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Layer 2 \- Deferred** | Role and permission definitions for surfaces without locked PRDs. Named explicitly. No placeholders or TBD entries. Updated when the corresponding PRD is locked. |

| *The Role PRD is a living document. Each time a new feature PRD is locked, the corresponding permission surface is added to Layer 1 and removed from Layer 2\. Version history tracks each update.* |
| :---- |

# **2\. Core Architectural Decisions**

## **2.1 One Unified Permission Engine**

Business users and Qawafel internal staff operate within the same permission model and share a single audit trail. Qawafel is itself a registered business on the platform and its staff are members of that business, with admin capabilities scoped to the platform-operator context.

One login entry point serves both merchant users and platform staff. The platform determines at login whether the authenticated user belongs to the Qawafel platform-operator business and routes them to the appropriate interface accordingly.

## **2.2 Data Model \- Build for Phase 2 from Day One**

The permission model must be designed from day one to support Phase 2 (merchant-defined custom roles) without requiring a structural rebuild. Phase 1 ships with fixed role names. Phase 2 adds the ability for merchants to define custom roles — this must be achievable as a product capability unlock, not a re-architecture.

| *Role capabilities must never be hardcoded against role names. A user's accessible actions must reflect the current state of their role's permissions at the time of any request, not at the time of login.* |
| :---- |

## **2.3 Authorized Signatory \- Orthogonal to Role**

The Authorized Signatory designation is independent of role. Any user of any role can be designated as an Authorized Signatory. The designation unlocks high-stakes financial actions regardless of the user's base role.

Two rules are permanently immutable:

* The Owner's Authorized Signatory status is set permanently at the point the Owner role is assigned. It cannot be removed by any user, system process, or admin action.

* This must be enforced as a hard platform constraint — not only a UI guard. Any attempt to remove it through any means must be rejected.

## **2.4 Single Owner per Business**

One Owner role exists per merchant at any time. The Owner is the designated legal representative nominated during registration — not automatically assigned based on CR presence. Multiple legal representatives named on a CR are accommodated through the Admin role combined with the Authorized Signatory designation, which grants equivalent operational and financial authority.

## **2.5 Role Model Phase Evolution**

| Phase | Who defines roles | Who configures permissions | Trigger to advance |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Phase 1** | Platform \- fixed role names (Owner, Admin). Finance role defined but deferred. | Merchant \- can configure which permissions each platform-defined role holds. Cannot add or rename roles. | Ships with general availability. |
| **Phase 2** | Merchant \- can create custom role names in addition to platform-defined roles. | Merchant \- full configuration per role including custom roles. Platform roles remain as templates. | Triggered by sustained merchant feedback or enterprise segment requirement. |

| *Phase 2 requires no data migration. The schema supports custom roles from day one. Phase 2 is a UI unlock, not a schema change.* |
| :---- |

# **3\. Role Assignment at Registration**

Role assignment is determined by the declaration the first registrant makes in Step 1 (Account Creator Details) of the onboarding wizard. Two paths are possible.

| Step 1 Declaration | Role Assigned | Owner Invitation | Pre-Owner Window |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| "I am the company owner" | Owner \- self-assigned at submission | None. Owner role is self-declared. | Not applicable. Owner role is immediately active. |
| "I am authorised to register this business" | Admin \- assigned at submission | Ownership invitation sent or skipped in Step 3\. Owner role unassigned until invitation is accepted. | Admin operates the full platform. Ownership transfer and account deletion CTAs are hidden until Owner role is assigned. |

| *The pre-Owner window requires no special 'acting Owner' state in the permission engine. The Admin role carries full operational authority. The two Owner-exclusive actions (ownership transfer, account deletion) are enforced by hiding the CTAs in the UI and by a permission check at the API layer that verifies an active Owner membership record exists before permitting those actions.* |
| :---- |

# **4\. Business User Roles \- Layer 1**

## **4.1 Role Definitions**

| Role | Description | Key Constraints |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Owner** | The legal representative of the business. Holds all permissions including the two exclusive actions: ownership transfer and account deletion. Created via self-declaration at registration or by accepting an ownership invitation. | One Owner per merchant at any time. Always an Authorized Signatory — this designation cannot be removed. Ownership transfer is self-service with no Qawafel approval required. |
| **Admin** | The operational manager. Holds all permissions except ownership transfer and account deletion. Manages users, roles, and platform configuration on behalf of the merchant. Can operate the full platform during the pre-Owner window. | Multiple Admins allowed. Can be designated as Authorized Signatory by the Owner or another Admin. Cannot transfer ownership or delete the merchant account. |
| *Finance role \- explicitly deferred to Layer 2\. The Finance role will be defined once PRDs 4–7 (Payments, Settlement, Financing) are locked. The schema must support a third role from day one. See Section 9\.* |  |  |

## **4.2 Ownership Transfer**

The Owner can transfer ownership to any active member of the merchant account. Transfer is immediate and self-service — no Qawafel admin involvement is required. On transfer:

* The previous Owner's membership is downgraded to Admin role.

* The new Owner's membership is upgraded to Owner role.

* The new Owner inherits the Authorized Signatory designation automatically.

* All other memberships are unaffected.

| *If the Owner's account is deactivated without a prior ownership transfer, the merchant account enters a suspended state. Recovery requires Qawafel Operations to reassign ownership to a verified active member.* |
| :---- |

## **4.3 Admin-to-Admin Deactivation Rules**

The following rules govern deactivation between users of equal or overlapping roles:

| Scenario | Rule |
| :---- | :---- |
| Owner deactivates an Admin | Always permitted. |
| Admin deactivates another Admin (no Authorized Signatory) | Permitted. |
| Admin deactivates another Admin who holds the Authorized Signatory designation | Not permitted. Only the Owner can deactivate an Admin who holds the Authorized Signatory designation. |
| Admin deactivates themselves | Not permitted. Self-deactivation is blocked for all roles. |
| Any user deactivates the Owner | Not permitted through self-service. Owner deactivation requires Qawafel Operations involvement. |

# **6\. Functional Requirements \- Business User Role Engine**

| FR ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **FR-RP.1** | Role capabilities must be resolved at the time of every request. No role capability may be fixed at login time. | A user's accessible actions change immediately when their role or permission configuration is updated — no re-login required. | Must Have |
| **FR-RP.2** | Permissions must be enforced as a hard platform constraint, not only through UI visibility. A user without a given permission must be blocked regardless of how the request is made. | Direct requests that bypass the UI are blocked for unauthorised actions with an appropriate rejection response. | Must Have |
| **FR-RP.3** | The Owner's Authorized Signatory designation is permanently set at role assignment and cannot be modified by any user or system process. | Attempting to remove the Authorized Signatory designation from an Owner returns an error. No UI control to remove it is shown. | Must Have |
| **FR-RP.4** | Ownership transfer and account deletion must be unconditionally blocked when no active Owner exists on the merchant account, regardless of the requesting user's role. | When no active Owner exists, both actions are rejected. The UI hides them and any direct attempt is also rejected. | Must Have |
| **FR-RP.5** | Every permission-gated action must produce an audit log entry recording: the user, the business context, the action, the timestamp, and the outcome (success or denied). Authorized Signatory actions must additionally record whether the Authorized Signatory designation was active at the time. | Audit log entries are present for every permission-gated action, including denied attempts. Denied entries include the denial reason. | Must Have |
| **FR-RP.6** | The Authorized Signatory designation must be verified at the time of action execution. If the designation has been removed since the user's session began, the action must be blocked. | Removing a user's Authorized Signatory designation takes effect immediately. Any subsequent attempt in the same session to perform a designation-required action is blocked. | Must Have |
| **FR-RP.7** | Platform-operator capabilities (approve KYB, configure global settings) must be definitively restricted to the Qawafel platform-operator context and must not be assignable to any merchant role. | Attempting to assign a platform-operator capability to a merchant role returns a validation error. | Must Have |
| **FR-RP.8** | Every request must be scoped to the user's active business context. Data from other businesses must never be accessible through session manipulation or otherwise. | Attempting to access data belonging to a different business returns a rejection response. | Must Have |
| **FR-RP.9** | An Admin must not be able to deactivate another Admin who holds the Authorized Signatory designation. Only the Owner can deactivate an Authorized Signatory Admin. | Attempting to deactivate an Authorized Signatory Admin from an Admin account returns a rejection. The action succeeds only when initiated by an Owner. | Must Have |
| **FR-RP.10** | An Admin must not be able to remove the Authorized Signatory designation from another Admin who currently holds it. Only the Owner can remove it. | Attempting to remove another Admin's Authorized Signatory designation from an Admin account returns a rejection. | Must Have |

# **7\. Tier-Drop & Permission Continuity**

Tier-drop events originate in PRD 3 (Admin Verification). This section defines the permission and continuity effects from the Roles perspective.

## **7.1 Tier 1 Drop — Section 1 Field Rejected**

| Effect | Specification |
| :---- | :---- |
| Badge | Platform Verified badge reverts to Unverified across all Trading Partner Records in all sellers' networks immediately. |
| New operations | All Tier 1-gated operations are blocked from the moment of tier drop until re-approval. |
| In-flight operations | No in-flight operations exist that are solely Tier 1-gated and time-sensitive. Adding to Business Networks and viewing invoices are read-type actions; no continuity exception is required. |
| Historical documents | Immutable. All documents issued under any tier always reflect the verified state at creation time. |

## **7.2 Tier 2 Drop — Section 2 Field Rejected**

| Effect | Specification |
| :---- | :---- |
| Tier 1 status | Preserved. Platform Verified badge is retained. |
| New Tier 2 operations | Blocked immediately: issuing invoices, generating payment links, ZATCA submission, invoice financing. |
| Active payment links already generated under Tier 2 | Remain valid and are honoured to completion. A payment link in flight is not cancelled by a tier drop. |
| Historical documents | Immutable. Invoices and payment links issued under Tier 2 always reflect the state at creation time. |

## **7.3 Tier 3 Drop — Section 3 Field Rejected or Bank Account Updated**

| Effect | Specification |
| :---- | :---- |
| Tier 1 and Tier 2 status | Preserved. All commercial operations remain available. |
| Settlement payouts | Suspended immediately. Payouts continue to neither the old nor the new IBAN during the review period. |
| Historical documents | Immutable. |
| Re-instatement | Tier 3 reinstates immediately upon admin approval of the submitted IBAN. |

# **8\. Qawafel Internal Admin Roles**

Qawafel internal staff access the platform as members of the Qawafel business, which carries platform-operator status. Admin roles are scoped to the Qawafel business context. Platform-operator capabilities exist only within this context and cannot be assigned to any merchant role.

| Role | Description | Key Constraints |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Super Admin** | Full access to all platform capabilities \- business and admin. Reserved for Qawafel engineering leads and senior operations. | Restricted to two or fewer active accounts at any time. Every action is logged with elevated audit priority. |
| **Operations** | Primary role for merchant onboarding and verification lifecycle. Full access to KYB queue, field-level review, tier unlocking, merchant status transitions, and payment method configuration. | Cannot approve payouts, access platform-wide settlement records, or impersonate merchants. |
| **Support** | Handles merchant support cases. Can view merchant data and impersonate merchants in view-only mode for troubleshooting. Can view and resolve support tickets. | Impersonation is view-only and fully audited. Cannot modify merchant data, approve KYB, or access financial records. |
| **Finance / Settlement** | Manages platform-level settlements, payout approvals, fee configuration, and financial reconciliation. | Cannot approve KYB, impersonate merchants, or modify merchant profiles. Financial data access is read-only except for payout approval and fee configuration. |
| **Risk & Compliance** | Monitors transaction data for suspicious activity, manages PDPL data requests, and produces regulatory exports. Can flag transactions and accounts for review. | Cannot approve KYB, impersonate merchants, or process payouts. Data access is read-only. All exports are logged. |

## **9.1 Impersonation Rules**

Impersonation is a Support-only capability, also available to Super Admin. The following rules apply unconditionally:

* Impersonation is view-only. The impersonating user cannot submit forms, approve actions, generate payment links, or take any action that modifies merchant data.

* Every impersonation session is logged atomically: impersonating user identity, target merchant, session start time, session end time, and pages visited. If the session log write fails, the impersonation session must not be permitted to start.

* The merchant cannot detect or prevent an impersonation session. No notification is sent to the merchant.

* Impersonation session logs are accessible only to Super Admin and Risk & Compliance.

* Maximum impersonation session duration to be defined by Engineering in consultation with the Product team before the feature is built.

Finance is the third platform-defined role and will be populated when PRD 5 (Settlement & Take Rate) and PRD 6 (Payment Methods) are locked. |
| Settlement & Take Rate | PRD 5 | View settlement records, download reports, request payout (Authorized Signatory required), view fee breakdown. Finance role permissions across this surface. |
| Payment Methods & Balance Visibility | PRD 6 | Configure payment methods, view balances, manage virtual IBANs. Role permissions across Owner, Admin, Finance. |
| Buyer Financing (BNPL / ARB) | PRD 7 | Apply for financing facility, view financing status, approve drawdown (Authorized Signatory required). Finance role permissions. |

| API key / service account permissions | API PRD | Machine-to-machine access controls are a separate concern from human user roles. |

# **11\. Non-Functional Requirements**

| Permission enforcement | A user without a given permission must be blocked from performing the associated action regardless of how the request arrives. UI-only enforcement is not sufficient. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Role resolution** | A user's accessible actions must reflect the current state of their permissions at the time of any request. A change to permissions takes effect immediately — no re-login required. |
| **Audit trail** | Every permission-gated action must be recorded with sufficient detail to reconstruct: who performed it, in what business context, what the action was, when it occurred, and whether it succeeded or was denied. Authorized Signatory actions must additionally record whether the designation was active at execution time. |
| **Session scoping** | Every request must be scoped to the user's active business context. Data from other businesses must be inaccessible regardless of how the request is constructed. |
| **Platform-operator containment** | Platform-operator capabilities must be definitively restricted to the Qawafel platform-operator context. They must not be configurable on any merchant role. |
| **Impersonation audit atomicity** | An impersonation session must not be permitted to start unless its opening log entry has been successfully written. Partial session logging is not acceptable. |
| **Owner Authorized Signatory immutability** | The Owner's Authorized Signatory designation must be permanently enforced as a hard constraint at every layer. No path — including direct technical access — should be able to remove it. |

# **12\. Out of Scope**

* Phase 2 custom role creation UI \- schema supports it from day one. UI is a later phase triggered by merchant demand.

* Branch scoping \- no branch concept exists in any current PRD. Will be defined when a branch management PRD is written.

* Multi-merchant permission inheritance \- whether an Owner of Merchant A who is also an Admin of Merchant B can perform cross-merchant actions is out of scope.

* API key / service account permissions \- machine-to-machine access controls are a separate concern.

* PDPL subject access request workflow \- the compliance workflow is a separate PRD concern. Risk & Compliance role access is defined here.

* Role-based notification routing \- which role receives which notification type is a notification system PRD concern.
