*Foundation PRD Review | QAWAFEL APEX PLATFORM | Based on Foundation PRDs v1.1*

# **Foundation PRDs \- Locked Decisions Summary**

This document summarises every decision locked during the Foundation PRD review cycle. These decisions are now encoded in the v2.0 document set and are the authoritative source for all EPD build work. Nothing in this summary supersedes the PRDs \- refer to the source documents for full acceptance criteria and functional requirements.

# **1\. Terminology & Data Model**

These decisions establish the canonical language and entity model the entire platform must use.

| Terminology Replacements (applies across all Foundation PRDs) |
| :---- |
| **'Counterparty Management' → 'Trading Partner Management'** The PRD 2 title and all references to counterparty management as a product domain are replaced. The word 'counterparty' no longer appears in the product. |
| **'Counterparty record' → 'Trading Partner Record' (relationship) or 'Business' (entity)** These are two distinct concepts and must not be conflated. A Business is the canonical real-world entity. A Trading Partner Record is a relational data structure in a seller's directory that references that Business. |
| **'Counterparty directory' → 'Business Network'** Each registered business has their own Business Network \- their private set of Trading Partner Records. |
| **'Network directory' → 'Business Directory'** The platform-wide searchable listing of registered businesses. A Q4 deferred feature. |
| **'Non-taxable toggle' → 'Taxable Business toggle'** Toggle is On by default (taxable \- the normal case). Switching Off is the non-taxable declaration. This is a UI and logic inversion from the prior naming. |
| **Add Counterparty → Add Business** All CTAs, labels, and flows use 'Add Business'. |

| Data Model \- Two Distinct Concepts |
| :---- |
| **Business (canonical entity)** Identified by CRN or UNN. Exists the moment its CR appears on the platform \- through self-registration or through another business adding it. Three internal states: Not Registered, Registered-Pending, Platform Verified. The badge is a property of the Business, not of the Trading Partner Record. |
| **Trading Partner Record (relationship)** Scoped to the creating business \- lives in their Business Network. References the canonical Business. Private local attributes (notes, labels) never overwritten by platform events. |
| **Badge is a property of Business** When a Business's verification state changes, the badge updates once at Business level and is automatically reflected across every Trading Partner Record across all sellers that reference that Business. |
| **External badge is intentionally two-state** Both Not Registered and Registered-Pending show as Unverified externally. The internal three-state distinction is for platform tracking only. |

# **2\. Registration & Onboarding**

These decisions affect the sign-up, onboarding wizard, and account management experience.

| Freelancer Scope |
| :---- |
| **Freelancer removed from APEX entirely** APEX is a B2B platform serving businesses only. All Freelance Certificate references, freelancer-specific form paths, and freelancer field logic are removed from every PRD and every feature. The business type selection (Business vs Freelancer) is removed from Step 2\. |

| Taxable Business Toggle & VAT Declaration |
| :---- |
| **Toggle is On by default; Off is the exceptional declaration** The Taxable Business toggle in onboarding Step 2 is On (taxable) by default. Switching Off triggers a warning and requires confirmation. Warning: 'Declaring your business as non-taxable means VAT invoicing and ZATCA submission will not be available on APEX. This cannot be changed without contacting support.' |
| **VAT Registered checkbox \- separate from taxability** When the toggle is On (taxable business), a 'VAT Registered?' checkbox is shown. Checking it reveals two additional fields: VAT Registration Number (15-digit, starts and ends with 3\) and VAT Certificate upload. These are separate from TIN. A taxable business that is not yet VAT-registered leaves the checkbox unchecked \- no VAT fields needed. |
| **TIN and VAT Registration Number are two distinct fields** TIN is 10 digits. VAT Registration Number is 15 digits starting and ending with 3\. They are not the same field, not derived from one another, and must not be conflated in any form, admin review, or database field. |

| Section-by-Section Submission |
| :---- |
| **Each section can be submitted independently as soon as its required fields are complete** Full completion of all four onboarding steps is not required before admin review can begin. A business can submit Section 1 (Core Business Identification) alone and receive Tier 1 while still completing Section 2 and Section 3\. |

| Auto-Save Semantics |
| :---- |
| **Blur auto-save \= local storage only; Save & Continue Later \= server-side** Auto-save on field blur uses local storage \- no server call per keystroke. Save & Continue Later triggers an explicit server-side save. Cross-device continuation is only guaranteed after a server-side save. The resume banner on the dashboard appears only after a server-side save. |

| In-Session Business Switching |
| :---- |
| **No logout required to switch between businesses** Multi-business users can switch context from the navigation bar using the in-session business switcher. The same business selection screen used at login is surfaced in-session. No logout required. |

| Ownership Invitation \- New User Flow |
| :---- |
| **Simplified account creation only \- no full sign-up** When an invited owner has no existing APEX account, they see a simplified creation screen: email (pre-filled from invitation, locked) and password only. No onboarding wizard. No business data to enter \- the business already exists. On account creation, the Owner role is assigned and the owner lands directly on the business dashboard. |
| **Invitation is tied to the specific invited email** Attempting to register under a different email address is rejected. The invitation cannot be claimed by a different address. |

| Duplicate CR Registration |
| :---- |
| **Active registered CR: blocked, directed to contact admin** If a CR belongs to an already active registered business, the second registration attempt is blocked with: 'This business is already registered on APEX. If you are a member of this business, please request access from your account administrator.' |
| **Pending registration CR: blocked, routed to ops** If a CR belongs to a business that is registered but pending verification, the second attempt is blocked and the case is routed to Qawafel Operations for manual resolution. |

| Business Notification Email |
| :---- |
| **No separate business email at onboarding \- added post-registration by Owner** To reduce onboarding friction, no dedicated business notification email is collected during sign-up. Until set, all notifications go to the account creator's work email. The Owner can set and update the business notification email from account settings at any time after registration. |

| Account Lifecycle & Inactivity Expiry |
| :---- |
| **Never submitted: 30-day warning, 60-day expiry** Accounts created but never submitted for review receive a warning email at 30 days of inactivity. If no action is taken, the registration expires at 60 days. |
| **Action Required with no re-submission: 14-day warning, 30-day expiry** Accounts in Action Required state with no re-submission activity receive a warning at 14 days. Expiry at 30 days if no re-submission. |
| **On expiry: soft-delete, CR/UNN released, email freed** The registration record is soft-deleted (preserved internally for audit). The CR/UNN is released and immediately available for a new registration attempt. The email address is freed for re-use. |

# **3\. Trading Partner Management**

These decisions affect Path A, Path B, Path C, badge behavior, and the quality label model.

| Path A \- Manual Business Addition |
| :---- |
| **CR/UNN is the only required anchor \- no Freelance Certificate** Path A requires CR/UNN number and legal business name (Arabic). Freelance Certificate is removed as a valid anchor entirely. |
| **Pending Business pre-population** When adding a business via Path A and the CR/UNN matches a registered-but-pending Business, the platform pre-populates only CR/UNN and legal name (no verified data yet) and shows: 'This business is registered on APEX and is pending verification.' Record is created with Unverified badge. |
| **Tier 1+ match: Platform Verified badge immediately** When adding via Path A and the CR/UNN matches a Tier 1+ registered Business, the record is immediately created with Platform Verified badge and verified data pre-filled. No need to wait for a merge event. |

| Internal Quality Labels \- Four Values |
| :---- |
| **Business Supplied added as the fourth label** Path C creation mode records are assigned the Business Supplied internal quality label. The four labels are: Manually Entered (Path A), ZATCA Referenced Single Seller (Path B, one seller), ZATCA Referenced Multiple Sellers (Path B, two+ sellers), Business Supplied (Path C creation). |
| **Path C enrichment does not change the quality label of an existing record** Only the creation event sets the label. Enrichment events leave the existing label unchanged. |

| Path C Merge Logic \- Gap-Fill for Enrichment, Full Overwrite on Merge |
| :---- |
| **Gap-fill applies to enrichment events (Path C, Path B)** When Path C adds contact fields to an existing record, it follows gap-fill: adds where absent, does not overwrite existing values. |
| **Full overwrite applies to the merge trigger event** When a Business reaches Tier 1 and the merge fires, all Trading Partner Record fields are overwritten \- including contact fields (email, phone). Contact fields are platform-owned at the merge event. The gap-fill protection does not apply to the merge trigger. |

# **4\. Merge & Deduplication**

These decisions define what happens when a Business self-registers and matches existing Trading Partner Records in other sellers' networks.

| Core Merge Rules |
| :---- |
| **Exact CR/UNN match only \- auto-merge** The auto-merge fires on exact CR/UNN match only. A single-digit transposition prevents an incorrect merge. |
| **TIN match without CR/UNN match \- ops review, no auto-merge** A TIN match without a corresponding CR/UNN confirmation surfaces a possible duplicate case to the Qawafel Operations queue for manual review. No automatic merge fires on TIN match alone. |
| **Platform-wide simultaneous merge** When a Business reaches Tier 1, the merge fires simultaneously across all sellers' Trading Partner Records that match the CR/UNN. Every seller sees their record upgraded at the same time. |
| **Full overwrite on merge \- all fields including contact** Verified self-registered data overwrites all Trading Partner Record fields: identity fields, national address, and contact fields (email, phone). Contact fields are platform-owned on merge. |
| **Aliases stored at merge \- prior names searchable** Names from pre-merge records are stored as aliases on the Business record. The verified legal Arabic name is canonical and shown as primary. Aliases appear in the business profile as 'Also known as' \- read-only, searchable. |
| **Historical transactions re-pointed to survivor record** Historical transactions are re-pointed to the survivor Business record for a clean unified history. A 'merged record' indicator appears on affected historical documents. Immutable audit trail stored permanently. |
| **Merge is not reversible \- ops corrective action path only** A merge cannot be auto-reversed. Incorrect merges require Operations to perform a corrective action: record separation, transaction reassignment, and creation of a new Trading Partner Record where needed. |

| Clean Slate with Opt-In for Pre-Registration History |
| :---- |
| **Default: newly registered Business sees no pre-existing transactions** A Business that self-registers arrives on a clean slate \- no transactions recorded by other businesses against them are visible by default. |
| **Opt-in at first login: limited pre-registration activity view** At first login, an opt-in prompt offers to surface transactions where the Business was directly a party (e.g. they were the buyer on another seller's payment link or invoice). Scope is strictly limited to transactions they were directly involved in. If opted in, these appear in a read-only view labelled as pre-registration activity. |

| Same CR/UNN, Different Trade Names |
| :---- |
| **CR/UNN is definitive \- verified legal name is canonical** If records exist under different trade names but the same CR/UNN, they refer to the same Business. The verified legal Arabic name from the Business's onboarding data becomes the canonical primary name. All prior names are stored as aliases. |

# **5\. Admin Verification & Tier Mechanics**

These decisions affect how the admin reviews submissions and how tier unlocks are triggered.

| Section-Level CTA \- No Automatic Tier Unlock |
| :---- |
| **Tier unlocks require an explicit section CTA click, not just field approval** Approving all fields in a section is not sufficient to unlock the tier. The admin must click the section-level CTA after all section fields are approved. The three CTAs are: 'Approve Core Business Identification → Unlock Business Access' (Tier 1), 'Approve Beneficial Owners → Unlock Full Commercial Access' (Tier 2), 'Approve Bank Account → Enable Settlement Payouts' (Tier 3). |
| **'Send Section for Correction' is the rejection path at section level** When one or more fields are rejected, the admin clicks 'Send Section for Correction' \- not a global rejection. Each section has its own correction flow. |

| IBAN Validation \- Hard Gate vs Advisory |
| :---- |
| **Invalid IBAN \= hard gate: Approve action disabled** When the system's mathematical IBAN validation result is Invalid, the Approve action is disabled. The admin can only reject. An Invalid IBAN cannot be approved under any circumstance. |
| **Valid IBAN \= advisory: admin must still cross-reference bank name** A Valid result is advisory. The admin must cross-reference the bank derived from the IBAN against the declared bank name before approving. A Valid result does not compel approval \- the admin retains judgment. |

| Admin Directory \- Role-Based Access Controls |
| :---- |
| **The all-businesses directory is an intentional exception to data isolation** The admin directory gives Qawafel Operations visibility into seller-supplied contact data across the platform. This is justified under legitimate interest in platform operations (PDPL-relevant). |
| **Role-based field visibility** Super Admin and Operations: full visibility including seller contact data. Support: identity fields only (legal name, CR/UNN, tier) \- no email or phone. Finance/Settlement: bank and settlement fields only. Risk & Compliance: risk and compliance fields only. |

# **6\. Tier Drop & Business Continuity**

These decisions define what happens when a field is rejected on a previously approved section.

| Tier Drop Cascading Effects |
| :---- |
| **Section 1 rejection: badge reverts platform-wide immediately** When a Section 1 field is rejected and the business drops below Tier 1, the Platform Verified badge reverts to Unverified across all Trading Partner Records in all sellers' networks instantly. |
| **Active payment links remain honoured; new operations blocked** Payment links already generated under the dropped tier remain valid and are honoured. From the moment of tier drop, new operations at that tier level are blocked until the tier is restored through re-approval. |
| **Section 2 rejection: Tier 1 preserved** Rejecting a Section 2 field drops the business below Tier 2 but Tier 1 is preserved. The Platform Verified badge is retained. Tier 2 operations (payment links, invoices, ZATCA submission) are blocked until Section 2 corrections are re-approved. |
| **Historical documents are always immutable** Invoices and payment links issued under any tier are never retroactively affected by a tier change. They always reflect the state at creation time. |

| Bank Account Update Post-Tier 3 |
| :---- |
| **Settlement is frozen immediately on new IBAN submission \- not continued to old IBAN** When a Tier 3 business submits a new IBAN, Tier 3 is immediately suspended and settlement payouts are frozen. Payouts continue to neither the old nor the new IBAN during the review period. This decision was made because the business may no longer have access to the old account. |
| **Flagged as urgent in admin queue \- expedited review** Bank account update cases are prioritised at the top of the admin queue above re-submissions. Tier 3 reinstates immediately on admin approval of the new IBAN. |

# **7\. Defined Ops Process Cases**

Six operational scenarios now have defined processes \- these are no longer open questions.

|  | Case | Defined Process |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **TIN-matched possible duplicate** | TIN match without CR/UNN confirmation surfaces a possible duplicate to the ops queue. Ops reviews, investigates, and either confirms the merge or dismisses. |
| **2** | **Corrective merge action** | If an auto-merge proves incorrect, ops separates records, reassigns transactions to the correct Business record, and creates a new Trading Partner Record where needed. Merge log used as evidence source. |
| **3** | **Duplicate CR registration** | When a CR belongs to a pending registration and a second attempt is made, ops contacts both parties, confirms the legitimate representative, and resolves which registration is valid. |
| **4** | **Non-taxable status reversal** | Business contacts support. Ops switches the Taxable Business toggle from Off to On, adds TIN, VAT Registration Number, and VAT Certificate fields, and triggers field-level review for the new fields only. Tier 1 remains active throughout. Historical non-taxable invoices are immutable. |
| **5** | **Bank account update post-Tier 3** | Flagged as urgent. Settlement frozen. Ops prioritises review. Admin applies same IBAN validation and bank name cross-reference. Tier 3 reinstates on approval. |
| **6** | **Merge log review** | Super Admin and Operations can access the full merge evidence trail at any time: matched fields, source precedence, timestamp, and initiating trigger. Available for audit, compliance, and dispute resolution. |

# Business and Trading Partner \- Concept Note

# **Business and Trading Partner \- Concept Note (Engineering team)**

## **Purpose**

This document proposes a concrete direction for how APEX should model Businesses, Trading Partner relationships, source of truth, verification and merge management.

The current Foundation PRDs distinguish canonical `Business` from `Trading Partner Record` at the terminology level. This note goes further: it proposes making the source-of-truth model explicit and replacing the current copy-and-overwrite merge behavior with a claims-and-publication model.

It addresses recurring ambiguity in these areas:

- What is the canonical Business record?  
- What belongs to the business-to-business relationship?  
- What happens when two businesses add the same business (counterparty) with different data but the same CRN?  
- What should counterparties see before and after verification?  
- What does "merge" actually mean in Trading Partner management?  
- How do rejection, expiry, TIN-only matching and corrective operations behave without destroying history?  
- How do admin review, field-level decisions, tier events and ops corrections work without destroying history?

---

## **Section 1 \- Product Team**

### 1\. Problem Statement

The current PRD set already distinguishes some of these concepts at the terminology level, but several lifecycle, merge and publication flows still mix three different concerns:

- the real-world Business  
- the business-to-business relationship  
- the data submitted about that Business by different sources over time

That causes confusion in flows such as:

- two businesses adding the same counterparty with different names  
- a business self-registering after other businesses already added it  
- a pending or rejected submission changing what counterparties see  
- a registration expiring while the business is still referenced by other businesses  
- TIN-only imports creating duplicates or near-duplicates  
- "merge" being described as both identity linkage and destructive data overwrite

This creates unresolved questions around source of truth, ownership of data, edit rights and rollback behavior.

### 2\. Recommended Product Direction

Adopt this model:

1. One canonical `Business Identity` per exact `CR/UNN` (`crn_unn`).  
2. One `Trading Partner Relationship` per business-to-business relationship.  
3. Every source of business data creates a `claim`, not a destructive overwrite.  
4. The platform publishes one current Business profile view from those claims.  
5. Verification upgrades the published view. It does not erase history.  
6. Registration application lifecycle must be separate from Business identity lifecycle.

In one sentence:

> APEX should be identity-canonical early, but truth-canonical only after verification.

### 3\. The Conceptual Model

#### *3.1 The three layers*

| Layer | What it represents | Examples |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Business Identity | The real-world company | Al Noor Trading LLC with `CR/UNN` `1010101010` |
| Trading Partner Relationship | Relationship-scoped link to that business | Desert Pearl Retail trades with Al Noor Trading LLC; Cedar Horizon Foods also trades with Al Noor Trading LLC |
| Data Claims | Statements made about the Business by different sources | Trading-partner-entered name, ZATCA import values, self-registration submission, admin-approved values |

#### *3.2 The key rule*

> `CR/UNN` creates identity. Everything else is a claim.

That means:

- exact `CR/UNN` match means the platform is talking about the same Business Identity  
- different names on the same `CR/UNN` are not separate businesses; they are competing claims about one business  
- `TIN` helps matching, but should not outrank `CR/UNN`  
- verification decides which claim becomes the published truth

### 4\. What Lives Where

#### *4.1 Business Identity*

This is the shared entity multiple businesses can point to.

It should own:

- `CR/UNN`  
- verification standing  
- badge status  
- the currently published business profile  
- the long-term identity timeline of the business

It should not store relationship-originated submissions as permanent truth.

#### *4.2 Trading Partner Relationship*

This is the business-to-business join between an owner business and a counterparty business.

It should own relationship-scoped data such as:

- owner-business-local email used for sharing payment links  
- owner-business-local phone number  
- relationship notes, labels, tags and active/inactive state  
- any future relationship-scoped commercial preferences

These are things that can differ by business relationship and still all be correct at the same time.

#### *4.3 Data Claims*

These are business-level statements made by sources over time.

Sources include:

- trading partner manual entry  
- invoice import  
- self-registration submission  
- admin verification  
- ops correction

Each claim should carry:

- source  
- submitted fields  
- status  
- timestamp  
- actor or origin

This is how the platform preserves provenance, handles conflict safely and avoids destructive merge logic.

### 5\. Source of Truth Policy

The platform should recognize three different views of truth.

#### *5.1 Published truth for counterparties*

This is the shared profile other businesses see.

Rule:

- if verified data exists, show the verified profile  
- if no verified data exists, show a provisional profile with explicit unverified labeling and provenance  
- never silently replace verified truth with a newer unverified submission

Important distinction:

- `published` does not always mean `verified`  
- before verification, the platform may still publish a provisional profile for usability  
- the platform must label that profile as provisional and preserve its source provenance

#### *5.2 Business-owned working truth*

This is what the business itself sees during onboarding, correction and re-submission.

Rule:

- the business should see its own latest submission immediately  
- this does not mean counterparties see it immediately  
- pending submissions are business-visible before they become platform-visible

#### *5.3 Internal ops truth*

This is the complete audit view.

Rule:

- ops and admins should see all claims, statuses, superseded values, decisions and timestamps  
- this is the evidence layer for dispute handling, duplicate resolution and corrective actions

#### *5.4 Claims as discrepancy signals after verification*

Once a business is platform verified, incoming trading partner claims — whether from manual entry or invoice import — stop being candidates for the published profile. They become an append-only discrepancy log.

This log serves two purposes:

- it allows the platform to detect and surface data quality issues to the submitting business: `The name you entered for this counterparty does not match their verified profile on APEX`  
- it allows the platform to alert the verified business when another business is submitting conflicting data about them

Verified data always supersedes trading partner claims. A trading partner cannot degrade or override a platform-verified identity — not by manual edit, not by invoice import, and not by re-adding the counterparty.

This gives verified businesses a strong guarantee: their published identity is controlled by the verification process and by their own subsequent submissions, not by what their counterparties happen to enter.

### 6\. What Counterparties Should See

This is one of the most important product behaviors to clarify.

#### *6.1 Before the business self-registers*

Counterparties see:

- a provisional unverified profile  
- clear provenance such as `Provided by trading partner` or `Imported from invoice`  
- no implication that the data is verified by the business or by APEX

#### *6.2 While the business is self-registered but pending verification*

Counterparties should not see the business's self-submitted fields as authoritative truth.

Recommended rule:

- keep the published counterparty view on the last published profile  
- if there has never been a verified profile, continue showing the best provisional profile  
- label the business as `Registered on APEX - pending verification`  
- allow the business itself to see and edit its pending submission in its own dashboard

This avoids exposing a business's unverified self-submission as if it were platform truth.

#### *6.3 After admin approval*

Counterparties see:

- the newly published verified profile  
- `Platform Verified` badge  
- old names preserved as aliases where appropriate

#### *6.4 After rejection*

Rule:

- keep the last verified published profile if one exists  
- if there has never been a verified profile, keep the last provisional published profile  
- rejected submission stays internal to the business and ops views  
- badge and tier behavior may change based on product policy, but published data should not blindly flip to rejected values

This resolves the current "badge reverted but data did not" confusion.

#### *6.5 Counterparty Visibility Decision Flow*

```
Start
  |
  v
Does a verified published profile exist?
  |-- Yes --> Show verified profile
  |           Show `Verified by APEX`
  |
  |-- No --> Does a provisional published profile exist?
              |-- Yes --> Show provisional profile
              |           Show provenance label
              |           e.g. `Provided by trading partner`
              |
              |-- No --> No counterparty-visible business profile yet

Separate rule running in parallel:

If the business has a pending self-registration submission:
  - business sees its pending submission in its own dashboard
  - counterparties do not see those pending values as authoritative truth
  - counterparties continue seeing the last safe published profile

If admin rejects fields:
  - keep last safe published profile
  - show `Action required to complete verification` to the business
  - do not switch counterparties to rejected values
```

### 7\. Rethinking "Merge"

It may be clearer to avoid using one word to mean several different things.

There are really four events:

| Event | What it really is |
| :---- | :---- |
| Exact CR match when a business adds a counterparty | identity lookup and relationship attach |
| Business reaches Tier 1 | publish verified profile to existing identity |
| TIN-only possible duplicate | possible identity match, routed to ops |
| Incorrect linkage corrected by ops | identity separation or reassignment |

Recommended terminology:

- use `attach` when a business connects to an existing Business Identity  
- use `publish verified profile` when Tier 1 is reached  
- reserve `merge` for exceptional duplicate correction cases only

This terminology shift could remove a lot of confusion from PRD wording.

### 8\. Product Rules to Lock

These are the rules that would benefit from explicit decision and documentation.

#### *8.1 Identity rules*

- `CR/UNN` is the primary identity anchor  
- exact `CR/UNN` match creates or finds the same Business Identity  
- `TIN` is a secondary signal, not an automatic identity decision

#### *8.2 Visibility rules*

- counterparties see published profile, not raw pending submissions  
- business sees its own pending submission immediately  
- ops sees the full claim history

#### *8.3 Verification rules*

- verification promotes a claim into the published profile  
- rejection rejects the new claim; it does not require deleting history  
- last verified profile remains the safest external truth

#### *8.4 Relationship rules*

- relationship-scoped contact details belong to the relationship, not the shared business identity  
- one business should not silently overwrite another business's relationship-scoped contact details

#### *8.5 Expiry rules*

- expiry should apply to the registration application, not to the Business Identity  
- the business may still exist in other businesses' networks even if a registration attempt expires  
- a future re-registration should attach back to the same identity if the `CR/UNN` matches

### 9\. Proposed User-Facing Labels

To reduce ambiguity for users, the UI should label profile state clearly.

Recommended labels:

| Situation | Recommended label |
| :---- | :---- |
| Data created by trading partner | `Provided by trading partner` |
| Data from invoice import | `Imported from invoice data` |
| Business registered but pending | `Registered on APEX - pending verification` |
| Business correction required | `Action required to complete verification` |
| Verified data | `Verified by APEX` |
| Historical name | `Also known as` |

### 10\. Visual Model

```
                     +---------------------------+
                     |     Business Identity     |
                     | CRN: 1010101010           |
                     | Badge: Unverified/Verified|
                     | Published Profile         |
                     +----+------------------+---+
                          |                  |
           +--------------+              +---+--------------------+
           |                             |
+----------+------------------+       +---------------------------+
| Trading Relationship        |       | Data Claims               |
| Desert Pearl -> Al Noor     |       | relationship claim        |
| local email/phone           |       |   (Desert Pearl)          |
+-----------------------------+       | relationship claim        |
                                      |   (Cedar Horizon)         |
+-----------------------------+       | invoice import claim      |
| Trading Relationship        |       | self-registration claim   |
| Cedar Horizon -> Al Noor    |       | admin verified claim      |
| local email/phone           |       +---------------------------+
+-----------------------------+
                                      Claims are business-level.
                                      Relationships are relationship-scoped.
                                      They are siblings, not a chain.
```

### 11\. Scenarios and Recommended Behavior

#### *11.1 Scenario A \- First business adds a counterparty*

Situation:

- Desert Pearl Retail adds counterparty Al Noor Trading LLC with CRN `1010101010`  
- no existing identity found

Recommended behavior:

- create `Business Identity`  
- create Desert Pearl's `Trading Partner Relationship`  
- create relationship-originated claim containing Desert Pearl's submitted values  
- publish a provisional unverified profile

#### *11.2 Scenario B \- Second business adds same CRN with same data*

Situation:

- Cedar Horizon Foods adds the same CRN and same legal name

Recommended behavior:

- attach Cedar Horizon to the same Business Identity  
- create Cedar Horizon relationship  
- create second relationship-originated claim  
- confidence increases, but no special verification claim is created yet

#### *11.3 Scenario C \- Second business adds same CRN with different name*

Situation:

- Desert Pearl says `Al Noor Corp`  
- Cedar Horizon says `Al-Noor Trading`

Recommended behavior:

- both businesses still point to the same Business Identity  
- both names are stored as claims  
- the published profile remains provisional and clearly unverified  
- no business's relationship-originated value is treated as authoritative truth just because it was entered first

This is the core scenario the current PRDs struggle with.

#### *11.4 Scenario D \- Business self-registers after other businesses already added it*

Situation:

- Al Noor Trading LLC creates an APEX account and submits onboarding

Recommended behavior:

- do not create a second identity if exact `CR/UNN` matches  
- create a self-registration claim on the existing Business Identity  
- business sees its own submitted values in onboarding and dashboard  
- counterparties still see the last published profile until verification completes

#### *11.5 Scenario E \- Business reaches Tier 1*

Situation:

- admin approves core identity fields

Recommended behavior:

- promote verified claim into the published profile  
- badge upgrades to `Platform Verified`  
- counterparties now see verified business data  
- older names can be retained as aliases

#### *11.6 Scenario F \- Business submission is rejected*

Situation:

- admin rejects one or more submitted fields

Recommended behavior:

- if some fields are rejected, the claim remains in history and moves to `action_required`  
- if the submission is rejected in full, the claim remains in history and moves to `rejected`  
- published profile stays on last safe published state  
- business enters `action_required`  
- counterparties are not switched to rejected values

#### *11.7 Scenario G \- Registration expires with no resubmission*

Situation:

- business registered, got rejected, then failed to resubmit

Recommended behavior:

- expire the registration application  
- do not destroy the Business Identity if other business relationships still reference it  
- keep the last safe published profile  
- allow future re-registration against the same identity

This is how Product can avoid the current orphaning ambiguity.

#### *11.8 Scenario H \- TIN-only import exists before CRN is known*

Situation:

- invoice import creates a TIN-only record  
- later the business self-registers with a CRN and same TIN

Recommended behavior:

- do not auto-merge purely on TIN  
- create ops review case if deterministic linkage is not already established  
- once ops confirms the identity, attach the TIN-only history correctly

#### *11.9 Scenario I \- Previously verified business edits core data*

Situation:

- verified business changes legal name, VAT, or core identity field

Recommended behavior:

- create a new pending claim  
- keep last verified profile published until review is complete  
- after approval, publish new verified profile  
- after rejection, keep prior verified profile

#### *11.10 Scenario J \- Previously verified business updates Tier 1 data and temporarily drops badge*

Situation:

- a `Platform Verified` business updates a Tier 1 field such as legal name, CR-linked identity data, TIN, or VAT data  
- admin review later determines the new submission is not yet acceptable and sends it back for correction

Recommended behavior:

- create a new pending claim for the updated Tier 1 data  
- if the updated Tier 1 data is rejected or sent to correction, the business may temporarily lose the `Platform Verified` badge based on product policy  
- counterparties should continue seeing the last safe published verified profile while the correction is in progress  
- the business itself should see `Action Required` and the exact fields that must be corrected  
- the pending or rejected replacement values must not become the new public truth  
- when the corrected Tier 1 data is approved, publish the new verified claim and restore the `Platform Verified` badge

This scenario makes the badge/data separation explicit: temporary loss of badge does not require exposing unverified replacement data to counterparties.

#### *11.11 Scenario K \- Same trading partner provides conflicting data via different workflows*

Situation:

- Desert Pearl Retail manually adds Al Noor Trading LLC with legal name `Al Noor Corp` and no TIN  
- Later, Desert Pearl Retail imports invoices issued by Al Noor Trading LLC; the invoice data shows legal name `Al-Noor Trading Co.` and TIN `1234567891`  
- Both data points originate from Desert Pearl, but through different workflows — manual entry and invoice import

Recommended behavior:

- store both as separate claims on the same Business Identity, with distinct `source_type` values: `trading_partner_manual` for the manual entry, `invoice_import` for the invoice-derived data  
- both claims carry the same `source_relationship_id` pointing to Desert Pearl's relationship row with Al Noor Trading LLC  
- the platform detects the discrepancy between the two claims from the same source  
- surface the discrepancy to Desert Pearl: `The name in your invoice data does not match the name you entered manually for this counterparty`  
- the platform does not resolve the conflict automatically; it asks Desert Pearl to confirm which data is correct  
- neither claim is automatically authoritative — the deterministic provisional publication rule described in this note applies

This is the core benefit of the append-only claims model: the discrepancy is visible, attributable and correctable without destroying either version of the record.

#### *11.12 Scenario L \- Platform verified counterparty receives a conflicting claim*

Situation:

- Al Noor Trading LLC is platform verified with legal name `Al Noor Trading LLC` and TIN `1234567890`  
- Cedar Horizon Foods imports an invoice from Al Noor Trading LLC; the invoice data shows legal name `Al-Noor Co.` and TIN `9876543210`  
- the values in the invoice conflict with Al Noor's verified profile

Recommended behavior:

- store the invoice import claim as `source_type: invoice_import` with status `observed`  
- do not update the published profile; verified data always supersedes trading partner claims once a business is platform verified  
- surface a discrepancy flag to Cedar Horizon: `This counterparty is verified on APEX. The data in your invoice does not match their verified profile`  
- optionally surface a discrepancy notification to Al Noor Trading LLC: `A business has submitted invoice data about you that does not match your verified profile — this may indicate a data error on their side or a document issue worth investigating`  
- the claim is stored as an audit record, not as an identity update

This scenario draws the explicit line: once a business is platform verified, trading partner claims of any kind do not alter the published identity. They become an append-only discrepancy log that the platform can use to flag data quality issues to both parties.

This also protects verified businesses from having their published identity degraded by a counterparty importing outdated or incorrect documents.

#### *11.13 Scenario M \- Incorrect identity linkage or incorrect merge*

Situation:

- an ops team later discovers records were linked incorrectly

Recommended behavior:

- ops should correct identity linkage using claim history and audit trail  
- historical evidence remains available  
- this is an exceptional corrective workflow, not the normal way the model works

### 12\. Product Decision Summary

The following answers are proposed for adoption:

| Question | Proposed answer |
| :---- | :---- |
| What is the canonical entity? | Business Identity keyed by exact `CR/UNN` |
| What is relationship-scoped? | Trading Partner Relationship |
| What is the source of truth for business fields? | Published profile derived from claims |
| What happens on conflict? | Store both claims; verification chooses published truth |
| What happens on Tier 1? | Publish verified core identity profile platform-wide; later sections continue through their own review lifecycle |
| What happens on rejection? | Partial rejection moves the submitted section to action required; full rejection marks the claim rejected; in both cases keep last safe published profile |
| What happens on expiry? | Expire registration application, not Business Identity |
| What happens on TIN-only match? | Never auto-create canonical identity or auto-merge; route to provisional observation plus ops review |
| What should be relationship-scoped? | owner-business-local contact fields, notes, tags, status |
| What happens during admin review? | Admin reviews per field within a submitted section; one field review record per field per round and one section state per section |
| What happens on partial field rejection? | Submitted section moves to action required; business corrects only flagged fields; resubmission creates a new full-snapshot claim with a predecessor link |
| What happens on tier unlock? | Admin confirms explicitly; badge updates platform-wide; tier event recorded |
| What happens on tier drop? | Badge reverts immediately; published profile does not change automatically; both are separate decisions |

### 13\. Admin Review and Ops Flows

This section defines the platform admin and ops team review flows that sit between a business's submitted sections and the published Tier 1 identity profile.

#### *13.1 Why This Track Exists Separately*

A business self-registration submission does not auto-publish. Each submitted section enters a review queue independently. Admin reviews it asynchronously and makes field-level decisions. The outcome — approve, partial reject, or full reject — determines the next section state and what the business and counterparties see.

This track is distinct from the trading-partner/import track because:

- it involves human decisions, not automatic derivations  
- Tier 1 review modifies `businesses.badge_status`, `verification_state` and `published_profile_kind` platform-wide  
- later sections continue through their own review states without rewriting the Tier 1 published identity profile  
- field-level rejection requires the business to correct specific fields, not redo everything  
- tier unlock and tier drop are both ops events that must be auditable

#### *13.2 Field-Level Review*

Admin review does not need to be limited to approving or rejecting an entire submission section. Within a section, some fields may be acceptable and one may have a problem.

Recommended behavior:

- admin reviews each submitted field individually  
- admin can approve or request correction at the field level with a reason  
- if all required fields in a submitted section are approved, that section is marked approved  
- if any required field in a submitted section is rejected, that section moves to `action_required`  
- the business sees exactly which fields were rejected and why — not just which section

This is a key design point. If admin approves 4 of 5 fields but rejects the 5th, asking the business to resubmit all 5 would add unnecessary friction. Field-level review avoids that.

#### *13.3 Admin Review Section CTAs*

The review UI could offer per-section actions such as:

- Approve section  
- Request correction on specific fields (admin must provide reason per field)  
- Escalate to ops team for investigation

Approving a section marks the approved fields with their review record. Tier unlock then follows the PRD's section-level CTA model:

- approving Core Business Identification and clicking its CTA unlocks Tier 1 and may publish a verified core identity profile  
- approving Beneficial Owners and clicking its CTA unlocks Tier 2 without changing the already-published Tier 1 identity profile by default  
- approving Bank Account Details and clicking its CTA unlocks Tier 3 without changing the already-published Tier 1 identity profile by default

This note treats `verified` in the source-of-truth sense as "admin-approved for publication on the business identity surface", which maps to Tier 1 core identity approval. It does not mean every onboarding section across all tiers has been approved.

#### *13.4 Tier Unlock Flow*

Tier 1 unlocks when admin approves the core identity fields required by the tier definition.

One useful framing is to treat tier unlock as a deliberate admin event, rather than as an automatic consequence of any single field approval.

Recommended behavior:

- when threshold fields are all approved, admin confirms the tier unlock explicitly  
- tier unlock promotes the current self-registration core-identity claim into the published verified identity profile  
- `verification_state` updates to `verified` and `badge_status` updates to `platform_verified` platform-wide  
- counterparties now see the verified profile and the badge  
- tier unlock is recorded with a timestamp, actor and reason

Tier unlock is not automatically reversible. Reversal requires an explicit tier drop action.

#### *13.5 Tier Drop Flow*

Admin can revoke tier status if later review or a dispute reveals that previously verified information was incorrect.

Recommended behavior:

- badge reversion is immediate and platform-wide  
- the published profile does not automatically revert to a prior unverified state — the two are separate concerns  
- if the profile should also change, admin must explicitly approve new values or revert to the last safe claim  
- the tier drop is recorded with reason, actor and timestamp

It may be helpful to keep badge drop and profile rollback as two separate admin decisions.

#### *13.5.1 Section State Tracking*

Because the current PRD allows section-by-section submission and section-by-section approval, a single application-level status is not sufficient for operational truth.

Recommended behavior:

- keep `business_registration_applications.status` for the overall application lifecycle only, such as `draft`, `in_progress`, `expired`, or `closed`  
- track each reviewable section separately, for example `core_identity_status`, `beneficial_owners_status`, and `bank_account_status`  
- allow combinations such as `core_identity_status = approved`, `beneficial_owners_status = pending_review`, `bank_account_status = not_submitted`  
- derive dashboard and admin queue views from the section states, not from a single application status alone

This keeps the model aligned with the locked PRD's progressive tier unlock design instead of collapsing multiple review tracks into one status field.

#### *13.6 Ops Case Types*

Platform ops should have explicit queues for the following case types.

| Case type | What triggers it | What ops does |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Pending verification review | Business submits a claim for review | Admin reviews fields, approves or rejects per field |
| TIN-only duplicate candidate | TIN-only record found when CRN business appears | Ops confirms or denies identity linkage |
| Incorrect identity linkage | Ops discovery or business dispute | Ops separates or reassigns Business Identities |
| Field correction re-review | Business resubmits after partial rejection | Admin re-reviews specific rejected fields only |
| Tier drop review | Incorrect verified data discovered | Admin revokes tier, optionally triggers fresh review |
| Ops identity correction | Two identities created for same CRN | Ops merges records, preserves full claim history |

These case types are the only legitimate pathways to destructive or corrective operations on the identity model.

#### *13.7 Admin Claim History View*

Ops and admins must have a single audit timeline per business that shows:

- all claims submitted, with source, status and timestamps  
- field-level approval and rejection decisions within each claim  
- which claim is currently published and why  
- the full tier event log — unlocks, drops and reasons  
- which user or system action triggered each status change

This view must never be hidden or purged. It is the authoritative audit trail for any dispute, correction, or compliance question.

### 14\. Final Recommendation for Product

The concrete direction is:

> One Business Identity per exact CR/UNN, many business-to-business relationships to it and all business data changes represented as claims with provenance and status. Counterparties see a published profile, not raw submissions. Tier 1 publishes verified truth. Expiry affects the registration application, not the existence of the Business Identity.

This direction resolves the major source-of-truth, merge and rollback questions with the least conceptual confusion.

## **Path C \- API import**

What is this API and what is the expected behavior out of it? It sounds like a bulk invoice import, is that correct? \- Atef

**Covered in v2.0 PRD 2 Sections 5.1 through 5.4.:**

Path C is not invoice import although invoice import is Partially Linked to Path C \- API Import section. It is a contact and business record import mechanism. Two modes:

**Creation mode** \- seller supplies buyer business identity and contact data (CR/UNN, Arabic legal name, email, phone) via API payload or bulk CSV upload. The platform creates Trading Partner Records automatically at scale. This exists because Path A is one-by-one manual entry \- impractical for sellers with large buyer bases.

**Enrichment mode** \- seller supplies contact details (email, phone) for businesses that already exist in their network, typically records created via Path B that are missing contact data because ZATCA invoices never carry email or phone. Path C fills that gap.

The key distinction: Path C is about business identity and contact data \- not invoices. Invoice import is Path B. Path B brings in invoice history and Path C enriches those same records with contact details so they can send payment links and financing invitations.

# **PRD 3**

## **Field level review actions**

- If we are doing checksum on IBAN and find it invalid why’d we need admin action on this field? \- Atef

  **Covered in PRD 3 FR-R.12.**

  The checksum tells us the IBAN format is mathematically valid. It does not confirm the account exists, belongs to this business, or matches the declared bank name. A Valid checksum result is advisory. The admin still needs to cross-reference the bank derived from the IBAN against the declared bank name before approving. An Invalid result however is a hard gate \- Approve is disabled and the admin can only reject. So the checksum narrows the admin's decision space but does not replace it entirely.

  Yes we release the lock. Two scenarios:

  **Never submitted for review:** 30-day inactivity warning email sent. If no action taken, registration expires at 60 days. CR/UNN released, email freed, record soft-deleted.

  **Action Required with no resubmission:** 14-day inactivity warning email sent. If no resubmission made within 30 days, registration expires. Same outcome \- CR/UNN released, email freed, record soft-deleted.

## **Counterparty**

What if a business adds a counterparty manually with correct data. This counterparty then tries to register through our platform. Will we pre-populate that data in wizard (most likely not, right)? Regardless, the registering business should be able to overwrite any existing data. So what happens after the user completes step1-4 and his data is pending review. The counterparty info would be the same as ones in pending review (same source) so any future invoices will be using the new data even if some of them got rejected.  \- Atef

Consider multiple scenarios and how they should behave (in terms publicly visible business details):  
a) Business ABC registers first (pending verification) and business XYZ tries to add ABC as a counterparty  
b) Business ABC registers first (verified) and business XYZ tries to add ABC as a counterparty  
c) Business XYZ “manually added” business ABC as a counterparty then ABC tries to register  
d) Business XYZ “zatca imported” business ABC as a counterparty then ABC tries to register  
e) Multiple businesses “manually added” ABC as a counterparty then ABC tries to register  
f ) Multiple business “zatca imported” ABC as a counterparty then ABC tries to register  \- Atef

**Covered in v2.0 \- all six scenarios are defined in PRD 2 Section 8\.**

**On pre-population of onboarding wizard:** No. Data that XYZ entered about ABC is XYZ's seller-supplied data \- it is never used to pre-populate ABC's own onboarding wizard. ABC fills their own data independently.

**On the six scenarios:**

**a) ABC registers first (pending) \- XYZ tries to add ABC:** XYZ sees a message: 'This business is registered on APEX and is pending verification.' CR/UNN and legal name pre-populated from ABC's submitted onboarding data only. Record created with Unverified badge. When ABC reaches Tier 1 the merge fires and upgrades the record.

**b) ABC registers first (verified) \- XYZ tries to add ABC:** Verified data pre-populated immediately on CR/UNN field blur. Record created with Platform Verified badge immediately. No merge event needed.

**c) XYZ manually added ABC \- ABC then registers:** No impact on ABC's registration. When ABC reaches Tier 1 merge fires automatically against XYZ's record and upgrades it with verified data.

**d) XYZ ZATCA-imported ABC \- ABC then registers:** Same as scenario c. Merge fires at Tier 1 and upgrades the Path B record.

**e) Multiple businesses manually added ABC \- ABC registers:** Platform-wide simultaneous merge fires across all matching Trading Partner Records at Tier 1\. Every seller's record upgraded at the same time.

**f) Multiple businesses ZATCA-imported ABC \- ABC registers:** Same as scenario e. Platform-wide simultaneous merge across all Path B records.

- Clean slate with opt-in option at login. What if the user decided later on that they need old transactions shouldn’t there be an option to do that rather than just a one time button on login that might not read carefully and skip. \- Atef

  **Valid. Updated PRD 1 \- FR-D.11** but set to deferred.

- Trading partner paths A, B and C. Did we drop VAT/TIN lookup? \- Atef  
    
  **Covered in v2.0 Document 0 Section 3.2 and PRD 2 Section 4\.** VAT/TIN lookup was not dropped. TIN is the secondary matching key across Path A blur check, Path B extraction, and Path C CSV and API. VAT Registration Number is a separate field and is not used as a matching key \-  TIN is.

- Duplicate CR on registration but status is pending review. The second attempt to register is blocked and routed to Qawafel Ops for manual resolution. Now the issue here is when you’re adding a trading partner you’ll get your business information from the first attempt (even if it’s wrong) \- Atef  
    
  **Covered in v2.0 PRD 1 FR-1.6 and PRD 2 FR-A.3.** When adding a trading partner whose CR/UNN matches a pending registration, the platform pre-populates CR/UNN and legal name from the submitted onboarding data only \- not all fields. The message shown is: 'This business is registered on APEX and is pending verification.' The seller is aware the data is unverified. Once the business reaches Tier 1 the merge fires and replaces all data with verified information.

- Trading Partner got acknowledged as a relation to business entity but again even with this the Merge & Deduplication section still contradicts this acknowledgement. \- Atef

  **Covered in v2.0 Document 0 Section 2\.** No contradiction. The Trading Partner Record is a relational reference to the canonical Business entity \- not a copy. The merge section consolidates Trading Partner Records to point to the verified canonical Business entity. The two concepts are consistent \- merge is the mechanism that enforces the single entity model when a Business self-registers.

- What are aliases and who defines them?

  **Covered in v2.0 PRD 2 FR-D.3 and Document 0 Section 8.2.** Aliases are prior trade names that existed on Trading Partner Records before a merge event. They are platform-defined automatically at merge time \- no one manually defines them. When a Business reaches Tier 1 and the merge fires, any name variations that existed across pre-merge records are stored as aliases on the canonical Business entity. They appear in the profile as 'Also known as' \- read-only and searchable.

- If the owner got sent an invitation but decided to click on sign up and filled his email and password rather than clicking on the link should that also route him to simplified account creation? \- Atef

  **Valid. Updated PRD 1 \- FR-7.5**

- What happens if a business gets added as a trading partner and it tries to register after? Keep in mind we are talking about unverified data \- Atef  
    
  **Covered in v2.0 PRD 2 Section 8 scenarios c, d, e, and f**. All four scenarios are defined. When a business that exists as a trading partner registers and reaches Tier 1, the merge fires automatically. Verified data replaces all seller-supplied unverified data across all matching Trading Partner Records platform-wide simultaneously.

  C-1. Invoice import vs counterparty creation   
  \- Question: If invoice import succeeds but counterparty extraction or enrichment fails, what should the seller see: successful import, partial success, or failed import?

  **Tensions**:

  **Gaps**: 

  1\. Ownership invitation skip behavior   
  \- If an authorized registrant skips the ownership invitation, can it be sent later, and is there any limit or escalation for businesses operating without an Owner? 

  2\. Received payment requests during verification

  3\. Guest payer receipt recovery   
  \- If a guest payer closes the success screen without downloading the receipt, how can they retrieve it later? 

  4\. Unverified invited Owner permissions   
  \- Can an invited Owner perform Owner-only actions, such as account deletion or ownership transfer, before the business completes KYB verification?  
    
  Purpose 

# Archived Catalog and Invoice Modules

**Read me**

*Read this first*

# **Purpose of this document**

This is a short orientation document. It explains what the invoice module is, how a business issues and receives invoices on APEX, and which document in this set covers which part. It is not a specification \- each linked document covers its own area in full detail.

# **What the invoice module does**

The invoice module allows a verified business on APEX to issue invoices to its trading partners, 	have those invoices cleared by ZATCA (the Saudi tax authority). A cleared invoice is also the instrument that can later be used to request financing through Al Rajhi Bank.

Three ways an invoice can enter APEX:

* Created directly inside APEX by a business, one invoice at a time.

* Imported in bulk through a file upload, for businesses bringing in invoices already issued through another system.

* Imported automatically through a system-to-system connection, for businesses whose own software sends invoice data directly to APEX.

Regardless of how an invoice enters APEX, every invoice ends up in the same place \- the same list, the same set of rules, the same compliance standard.

# **The three things every invoice carries**

Every invoice in APEX has three separate pieces of status information that are tracked independently of one another:

| Status type | What it tracks | Possible values |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Lifecycle status | Where the invoice is in the process of being created and cleared by ZATCA. | Draft, Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, Rejected, Importing, Import Failed |
| Payment status | Whether the buyer has paid. Only tracked once an invoice is Cleared. | Unpaid, Partially Paid, Paid (plus Overdue, shown when a due date has passed) |
| Financing status | Whether the invoice has been put forward for financing with Al Rajhi. Covered in a separate financing module, not in this document set. | Out of scope here but as an fyi  |

# **What this document Assumes**

* Zatca phase 2 integration is already in place

# **What this document set covers**

The full set is broken into small, focused documents so that each can be read and built  independently. They are ordered the way a business would naturally encounter them \- catalog setup first, since it's required before an invoice can be created, then invoice creation, then the different ways invoices and credit notes can enter or be reviewed in APEX.

| \# | Document | Covers |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Catalog \- Item Setup | Creating and editing the products/services a business sells |
| 2 | Catalog \- List View & Lifecycle | Managing the catalog day to day; activating/deactivating items |
| 3 | Catalog \- Bulk Import | Setting up a catalog in one step via file upload |
| 4 | Invoice Creation \- Drafting | Building an invoice manually, before it is sent for clearance |
| 5 | Invoice Creation \- Submission & ZATCA Clearance | What happens when a business sends an invoice for clearance |
| 6 | Invoice Import \- Bulk CSV (Invoices) | Bringing in invoices already issued elsewhere, via file upload |
| 7 | Invoice Import \- Bulk CSV (Credit Notes) | Bringing in credit notes alongside imported invoices |
| 8 | Invoice Import \- API (Invoices) | Business requirements for a system-to-system invoice connection |
| 9 | Invoice Import \- API (Credit Notes) | Business requirements for a system-to-system credit note connection |
| 10 | Invoice List View | How a business browses, searches, and filters its invoices |
| 11 | Invoice Detail View & Status Lifecycle | What a business sees on a single invoice, and what actions are available at each stage |
| 12 | Credit Note Creation | Correcting or reversing part or all of a cleared invoice |
| 13 | Credit Note Submission & Lifecycle | What happens when a credit note is sent for clearance |
| 14 | Credit Note List View | How a business browses its credit notes |
| 15 | Credit Note Detail View & Status Lifecycle | What a business sees on a single Credit Note, and what actions are available at each stage |

# **What this document set does not cover**

These are deliberately out of scope for the invoice module and are covered elsewhere or later:

* Recording and allocating payments \- will be covered in the payment module.

* Requesting, approving, and disbursing financing applications with Al Rajhi \- will be covered in the financing module.

* Who within a business is allowed to create invoices, manage the catalog, or issue credit notes \- will be covered in the roles and permissions module.

# **Ground rules that apply across every document in this set**

* Saudi domestic trade only. No foreign currency, no cross-border invoices.

* Every invoice is denominated in Saudi Riyals.

* Every invoice must be cleared by ZATCA before it is considered valid. A cleared invoice can never be edited or deleted \- only corrected through a credit note.

# 1 \- Catalog Management \- Item Setup

**Catalog Management \- Item Setup**

| Related documents: Document 2 (Catalog List View & Lifecycle), Document 3 (Catalog Bulk Import), Document 4 (Invoice Creation \- Drafting). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes how a business sets up the catalog of products and services it sells. The catalog is required before a business can create an invoice manually inside APEX \- every line item on a manually created invoice must come from the catalog.

# **Why a catalog is required**

We do not want to encounter data quality problems caused by free-text line items on invoices. Therefore to keep invoice data consistent and reliable, a manually created invoice can only use line items that exist in the business's catalog. 

# **What a catalog item is**

A catalog item represents a single product or service that a business sells. It is a template. When a business adds it to an invoice, its details are copied onto that invoice line. Changing a catalog item afterward does not change any invoice that already used it.

# **Fields on a catalog item**

| Field | Required? | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Name | Yes | The name of the product or service. Appears on the invoice line. Must be unique within the business's own catalog. Maximum 100 characters so it does not break the invoice layout. |
| Description | No | Optional additional detail shown below the name on the invoice line. Maximum 500 characters. |
| Unit of measure | No | How the item is counted or measured \- for example Hour, Kilogram, or Box. Selected from a fixed list, grouped by category. Free typing is not allowed, to keep invoices consistent. |
| Default price | Yes | The standard selling price in Saudi Riyals. Can be changed by the business on any individual invoice line without affecting the catalog item itself. |
| Default VAT treatment | Yes | Either Standard (15%) or Exempt (0%). Can be changed by the business user on any individual invoice line without affecting the catalog item itself. |
| Status | Yes | Active or Inactive. New items are Active by default. Covered fully in Document 2\. |

# **Unit of measure \- the full list**

The list below is grouped into categories. A business user first picks a category, then picks the specific unit within it.

| Category | Units |
| :---- | :---- |
| Time | Minute, Hour, Day, Week, Month, Year |
| Count | Unit, Piece, Pair, Set, Pack, Bundle, Roll, Sheet, Plate, Tablet, Capsule, Vial, Ampule, Dose |
| Weight | Gram, Kilogram, Ton, Metric Ton, Pound, Ounce |
| Volume | Milliliter, Liter, Gallon, Barrel, Cubic Meter |
| Length | Millimeter, Centimeter, Meter, Kilometer, Foot, Inch |
| Area | Square Meter, Square Foot, Square Kilometer |
| Packaging | Box, Carton, Bag, Pallet, Container, Drum, Can, Bottle, Jar, Crate, Sack |
| Construction | Beam, Block, Tile |
| Digital / Service | License, Subscription, Transaction, Request, Session |

# **VAT treatment \- why only two options**

APEX supports two VAT treatments: Standard (15%) and Exempt (0%). This reflects the fact that Qawafel APEX serves domestic trade between businesses inside Saudi Arabia only. Categories that exist under Saudi tax law for other situations \- such as exports or out-of-scope supplies \- are not relevant to this business and are not offered.

# **How a catalog item behaves once created**

* A catalog item is a starting point, not a binding rule. A business user can change the price or VAT treatment for a single invoice line without changing the catalog item.

* Editing a catalog item only affects invoices created after the edit. Invoices that already used the item, including drafts, are not changed.

* A catalog item cannot be permanently deleted. It can only be made Inactive. See Document 2 for full detail.

# **Creating a catalog item from within invoice creation**

While building an invoice, if a business user cannot find the item they need in the catalog, they can create a new catalog item without leaving the invoice they are working on. This uses the same fields described in this document. Once saved, the new item is immediately available to add to the invoice.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-1.1 | A business can create a new catalog item by providing Name, Default price, and Default VAT treatment. | Item is created and appears in the catalog list with Status set to Active. |
| FR-1.2 | Name is a required field and must be unique within the business's own catalog. | Saving is blocked with a clear message if Name is left blank or matches an existing item's name for the same business. |
| FR-1.3 | Name cannot exceed 100 characters so it does not break the invoice layout. | Saving is blocked with a clear message if Name exceeds the limit. |
| FR-1.4 | Description is optional and cannot exceed 500 characters. | Saving is blocked with a clear message only if the limit is exceeded; the field can otherwise be left blank. |
| FR-1.5 | Unit of measure is optional and, if provided, must be selected from the defined category/unit list. | Saving succeeds with no unit selected, or with one valid unit selected. Free-text entry is not possible. |
| FR-1.6 | Default price is required and must be a positive number, in Saudi Riyals. | Saving is blocked with a clear message if the field is blank, zero or negative, or not a number. |
| FR-1.7 | Default VAT treatment is required and must be either Standard or Exempt. | Saving is blocked with a clear message if no VAT treatment is selected. |
| FR-1.8 | A new catalog item defaults to Active status without the business user having to set it. | After creation, the item's Status field reads Active. |
| FR-1.9 | Editing a catalog item's price or VAT treatment does not change any invoice line that already used that item. | An invoice created before the edit, including a Draft, shows the original price and VAT treatment unchanged after the catalog item is edited. |
| FR-1.10 | A business can create a new catalog item from within the invoice creation flow without losing their place in the invoice. | After saving the new item, the business user returns to the invoice they were building, with the new item available for selection. |

**Stories Pack (3)**

**CAT-1-US01 — Create a Catalogue Item**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to create a Catalogue Item so that it can be selected when creating future invoices.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Name, Default Price, and Default VAT Treatment are required.  
* Description and Unit of Measure are optional.  
* Name cannot exceed 100 characters.  
* Description cannot exceed 500 characters.  
* Price must be a positive SAR amount.  
* VAT Treatment must be Standard or Exempt.  
* Unit of Measure must come from the approved list.  
* The new item is Active by default.  
* The item Name must be unique within the Business catalogue.

---

## **CAT-1-US02 — Select a Unit of Measure by Category**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to select a Unit of Measure from a category so that Catalogue Items use consistent measurement values.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Unit of Measure is optional.  
* The user first selects a category, then selects a unit within that category.  
* The available categories are Time, Count, Weight, Volume, Length, Area, Packaging, Construction, and Digital / Service.  
* Only the units defined under the selected category are available.  
* Free-text Unit of Measure entry is not allowed.  
* The selected Unit of Measure is saved with the Catalogue Item.

---

## **CAT-1-US03 — Edit an Active Catalogue Item**

**User Story**

As an authorised Business User, I want to edit an Active Catalogue Item so that future invoices use its latest default values.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The user can update Name, Description, Unit of Measure, Default Price, and Default VAT Treatment.  
* The same validation rules used during creation also apply during editing.  
* The updated Name must remain unique within the Business catalogue.  
* Existing invoice lines, including Draft invoice lines, remain unchanged.  
* The Catalogue Item keeps the same identity after editing.

---

## **CAT-1-US04 — Create a Catalogue Item During Invoice Drafting**

**User Story**  
As a Business User drafting an invoice, I want to create a missing Catalogue Item without leaving the invoice so that I can continue preparing the invoice.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The same Catalogue Item fields and validation rules are used.  
* The current Invoice Draft context is preserved.  
* After creation, the user returns to the same Invoice Draft.  
* The new item becomes available in the invoice item picker.  
* Creating the item does not automatically create or modify an invoice line.
