# 2 \- Catalog Management \- List View & Lifecycle

**Catalog Management \- List View & Lifecycle**

| Related documents: Document 1 (Catalog \- Item Setup), Document 4 (Invoice Creation \- Drafting). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes how a business views and manages its catalog day to day, and how an item moves between Active and Inactive.

# **Active and Inactive \- what they mean**

Every catalog item is either Active or Inactive. This is the only lifecycle a catalog item has \- there is no approval process and no draft state. An item is Active the moment it is created.

| Status | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| Active | Visible and selectable when a business is adding a line item to an invoice. |
| Inactive | No longer selectable for new invoice lines. The item itself, and every invoice that previously used it, is unaffected. |

# **Deactivating instead of deleting**

A catalog item can never be permanently deleted. A business can only deactivate it. This protects against accidentally losing a frequently used item, and keeps a business's catalog history intact. A deactivated item can be reactivated at any time, restoring it to the invoice creation picker.

# **Catalog list view**

This is the screen a business lands on when managing their catalog.

# **Columns**

| Column | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Name | The catalog item name. Selecting it opens the item for editing. |
| Description | Shown as a short preview, truncated if long. |
| Unit of measure | The selected unit, shown for quick reference. |
| Default price | Shown in Saudi Riyals. |
| Default VAT treatment | Standard or Exempt. |
| Status | Active or Inactive. |

# **Default view, search, and sorting**

* By default, only Active items are shown. A business can switch a filter to see inactive or all items, including Active and Inactive ones.

* Search works by item name only.

* Items are sorted alphabetically by name by default.

# **Actions available per item**

| If item is Active | If item is Inactive | Always available |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Edit, Deactivate | Reactivate | View item details |

# **Empty states**

* No catalog items at all: the business is prompted to create their first item, or to use the bulk import option (Document 3).

* No items match the current filter or search: a message indicates no matches were found, with an option to clear the filter or search.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-2.1 | A business can deactivate an Active catalog item. | Item's Status changes to Inactive. Item no longer appears in the invoice creation line item picker. |
| FR-2.2 | A business can reactivate an Inactive catalog item. | Item's Status changes to Active. Item reappears in the invoice creation line item picker. |
| FR-2.3 | A catalog item cannot be permanently deleted by any business user. | No delete option is available anywhere in the catalog management screens. |
| FR-2.4 | Deactivating a catalog item does not affect any invoice that already used it. | An invoice created before deactivation, on any status, still displays the line item exactly as it was at the time it was added. |
| FR-2.5 | The catalog list view shows only Active items by default. | On first load, no Inactive items are shown unless the business changes the filter. |
| FR-2.6 | A business can switch the catalog list filter to view inactive or all items, including Active and Inactive ones. | Selecting the filter shows All, Active and Inactive items, with Status visible per row. |
| FR-2.7 | Search on the catalog list works by item name only. | Entering a search term returns items whose name contains the term. Searching by price, description, or other fields returns no special matching. |
| FR-2.8 | The catalog list is sorted alphabetically by name by default. | On first load, items appear in A-to-Z order by name. |
| FR-2.9 | An empty catalog shows a prompt to create the first item or use bulk import. | A business with zero catalog items sees this prompt instead of an empty table. |
| FR-2.10 | A filtered or searched view with no matches shows a clear no-results message. | When a filter or search returns zero items, a message indicates no matches were found, with an option to clear the filter or search. |

**Stories Pack (6)**

**CAT-2-US01 — View the Catalogue List**

**User Story**

As an authorised Business User, I want to view my Business catalogue so that I can manage its products and services.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The list shows Name, Description preview, Unit of Measure, Default Price, VAT Treatment, and Status.  
* Active items are shown by default.  
* Items are sorted alphabetically by Name by default.  
* Only items belonging to the Current Business are shown.  
* Selecting an item opens its details.

---

**CAT-2-US02 — Search and Filter Catalogue Items**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to search and filter Catalogue Items so that I can find the item I need quickly.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Search works by item Name only.  
* The user can filter by Active, Inactive, or All.  
* Status is visible for every item.  
* A no-results message appears when no items match.  
* The user can clear the current search or filter.

---

**CAT-2-US03 — View Catalogue Empty States**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want clear empty-state guidance so that I know what to do when no Catalogue Items are available.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A Business with no Catalogue Items sees an option to create its first item.  
* The empty state also offers the Bulk Import option.  
* A search or filter with no matches shows a different no-results message.  
* The no-results message provides an option to clear the search or filter.

---

**CAT-2-US04 — Deactivate a Catalogue Item**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to deactivate a Catalogue Item so that it can no longer be selected for new invoice lines.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Only an Active item can be deactivated.  
* The item Status changes to Inactive.  
* The item is removed from the default Active catalogue list.  
* The item is removed from the invoice item picker.  
* Existing invoice lines remain unchanged.  
* The item is not permanently deleted.

---

**CAT-2-US05 — Reactivate a Catalogue Item**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to reactivate an Inactive Catalogue Item so that it can be used again in new invoices.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Only an Inactive item can be reactivated.  
* The item Status changes to Active.  
* The same Catalogue Item identity is retained.  
* The item reappears in the default Active list.  
* The item becomes selectable in the invoice item picker again.

---

**CAT-2-US06 — Prevent Catalogue Item Deletion**

**User Story**  
As a Business, I want Catalogue Items to be deactivated instead of deleted so that catalogue and invoice history remain intact.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* No Delete action is available in Catalogue Management.  
* A Business User cannot permanently delete a Catalogue Item.  
* Inactive items remain available through the Inactive or All filters.  
* Existing invoices remain unaffected by item lifecycle changes.

# 3 \- Catalog Management \- Bulk Import

**Catalog Management \- Bulk Import**

| Related documents: Document 1 (Catalog \- Item Setup). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes how a business can set up its entire catalog in one step, by uploading a file, instead of creating items one at a time.

# **Who this is for**

A business with a large number of products or services \- for example a wholesale distributor with hundreds of items \- can use this to populate their catalog quickly rather than entering each item manually through Document 1's creation flow.

# **How it works**

* The business downloads a file template provided by APEX.

* The business fills in the template with their products and services.

* The business uploads the completed file.

* APEX checks every row in the file and shows the business a preview of what will be created, along with any rows that have a problem.

* The business confirms, and the valid rows are created as catalog items. Rows with problems are not created.

# **Template columns**

The uploaded file must use the same fields described in Document 1:

| Column | Notes |
| :---- | :---- |
| Name | Required. Must be unique within the business's catalog. |
| Description | Optional. |
| Unit of measure | Optional. Must exactly match one of the units defined in Document 1\. Values outside that list are rejected. |
| Default price | Required. Must be a positive number, in Saudi Riyals. |
| Default VAT treatment | Required. Must be either Standard or Exempt. |
| Status | Optional. Defaults to Active if left blank. |

# **Validation rules**

* A row is rejected if the name is missing, or duplicates a name already used elsewhere in the file or already existing in the business's catalog.

* A row is rejected if the unit of measure does not exactly match one of the defined options.

* A row is rejected if the default price is missing, not a number, or not a positive value.

* A row is rejected if the VAT treatment is missing or is not Standard or Exempt.

* One bad row does not block the rest of the file. Every other valid row is still created.

# **Result screen**

After the business confirms the import, they see a summary: how many items were created successfully, and a list of any rows that were rejected along with the specific reason for each, so they can correct and re-upload only those rows if needed.

# **Not covered here**

There is no system-to-system (API) option for bringing items into the catalog. The catalog is set up and maintained directly by the business, either one item at a time (Document 1\) or through this bulk upload.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-3.1 | A business can download a file template with the correct column headers for catalog import. | Template file downloads and contains the columns: Name, Description, Unit of measure, Default price, Default VAT treatment, Status. |
| FR-3.2 | A business can upload a completed file to bring multiple catalog items in at once. | Upload accepts a file in the supported format and proceeds to a preview step. |
| FR-3.3 | Each row's Name is validated as required and unique against both the file and the business's existing catalog. | A row is flagged as an error if its Name is blank, or duplicates another row in the file, or duplicates an existing catalog item's name. |
| FR-3.4 | Each row's Unit of measure, if provided, is validated against the defined list. | A row is flagged as an error if Unit of measure is provided but does not exactly match a defined option. |
| FR-3.5 | Each row's Default price is validated as required and a positive number. | A row is flagged as an error if Default price is missing, not a number, zero, or negative. |
| FR-3.6 | Each row's Default VAT treatment is validated as required and either Standard or Exempt. | A row is flagged as an error if Default VAT treatment is missing or does not equal Standard or Exempt. |
| FR-3.7 | Rows with errors do not block valid rows in the same file from being imported. | After confirming the import, every row without an error is created as a catalog item, regardless of other rows having errors. |
| FR-3.8 | After import, the business sees a summary of how many items were created and which rows failed, with a specific reason per failed row. | The result screen lists a success count and, separately, every failed row with its row number and the exact validation reason. |

As an authorised Business User, I want to download a Catalogue Import template so that I can prepare multiple Catalogue Items for upload.

* It contains these columns:  
  * Name  
  * Description  
  * Unit of Measure  
  * Default Price  
  * Default VAT Treatment

* Every row is validated independently.

* Description follows the Catalogue Item length limit.

* Invalid rows are not created.  
* One invalid row does not block other valid rows.

* Every failed row shows its original row number.  
* Every failed row shows a specific failure reason.

# 4 \- Invoice Creation \-  Drafting

**Invoice Creation \-  Drafting**

| Related documents: Document 1 (Catalog \-  Item Setup), Document 2 (Catalog \-  List View & Lifecycle), Document 5 (Invoice Creation \-  Submission & ZATCA Clearance), Document 11 (Invoice Detail View & Status Lifecycle), Document 12 (Credit Note Creation). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes how a business manually builds an invoice inside APEX, from starting a new invoice through to having a complete Draft ready to send for ZATCA clearance. It does not cover what happens after the business user submits the invoice \-  that is covered in Document 5\.

# **What a Draft is**

A Draft is an invoice that exists only inside APEX and has not yet been sent anywhere. It has no legal standing. It can be freely edited or deleted. No identifiers have been assigned to it yet, and ZATCA has no knowledge of it.

# **Starting a new invoice**

A business starts a new invoice from the invoice section of APEX. An empty Draft is created and the business user begins filling it in. The Draft can be saved at any point and returned to later, or deleted if no longer needed.

# **Selecting the trading partner**

A business selects the buying Business from their existing list of trading partners. There is no option to type in a new buyer directly on the invoice \-  the buyer must already exist as a trading partner. If the buyer is not yet in the trading partner list, the business adds them there first, following the same pattern used for adding a trading partner elsewhere on the platform.

* Once a trading partner is selected, their legal name, VAT number, and UNN are pulled automatically from their verified profile.

* The business cannot manually edit the buying Business legal name, VAT number, or UNN on the invoice. These always reflect the trading partner's profile.

# **Selling Business information**

The selling Business legal name, VAT number, UNN, and logo (if uploaded) are pulled automatically from the business's own verified profile. None of these are editable on the invoice.

# **Dates**

| Field | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Invoice date | Shown as a placeholder while the invoice is a Draft and can be changed freely for planning purposes. It is not the final date. The actual invoice date is set automatically at the moment the invoice is submitted for ZATCA clearance (see Document 5\) and cannot be set manually at that point. |
| Due date | Set manually by the business. Required before the invoice can be submitted. There is no automatic calculation from payment terms. |

# **Adding line items**

Every line item on a manually created invoice must come from the business's catalog (Document 1). There is no free-text line item entry. If the item a business needs does not exist in the catalog, they can create it without leaving the invoice, as described in Document 1\.

When a catalog item is added to an invoice, the following are copied onto the line and can each be adjusted for that specific line without changing the catalog item itself:

* Name

* Description if any

* Unit of measure if any

* Unit price

* VAT treatment (Standard or Exempt)

Quantity is entered by the business user for every line. It is required, and the minimum value is 1\. There is no maximum quantity restriction.

# **Discounts**

A discount can be applied to an individual line item. It is not possible to apply a discount to the invoice as a whole \-  every discount must be entered at the line level. This keeps the calculation clear when an invoice has lines at different VAT treatments.

* A discount can be entered as either a fixed Saudi Riyal amount or a percentage.

* The discount is applied before VAT is calculated. VAT is calculated on the amount remaining after the discount.

* The discount amount is shown explicitly on the line, alongside the original price and the resulting taxable amount.

# **Line and invoice totals**

Each line shows: quantity, unit price, discount (if any), the taxable amount after discount, the VAT rate applied, the VAT amount, and the line total.

The invoice summary, shown below the line items, displays:

* Subtotal \-  the sum of all line taxable amounts, after discounts, before VAT.

* VAT breakdown \-  one line per VAT rate present on the invoice. For example, if the invoice has both Standard and Exempt lines, both are shown separately, not combined.

* Total VAT \-  the sum of VAT across all rates.

* Invoice total \-  subtotal plus total VAT. This is the amount the buyer owes.

# **Notes Section**

An optional free-text field is available for the business user to add any additional information \-  for example a reference number or delivery instruction. There is no language restriction. The field has no hard character limit, though a soft guidance count is shown to help keep the invoice document well formatted. Notes appear on the invoice document the buyer eventually receives.

# **Currency**

Every invoice is in Saudi Riyals. There is no currency selection on the invoice.

# **Saving and returning to a Draft**

A Draft can be saved at any point, even if incomplete, and returned to later. A Draft can also be deleted entirely. Once an invoice leaves the Draft state, it can no longer be edited or deleted \-  see Document 5 for what happens at that point.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-4.1 | A business can start a new Draft invoice from the invoice section of APEX. | An empty Draft invoice is created and the business user is taken into the invoice creation screen. |
| FR-4.2 | A business can only select a buying business from their existing trading partner list. There is no free-text buyer entry. | The buying business field only accepts a selection from the trading partner list. No text field is available to type a new buyer name directly. |
| FR-4.3 | Selecting a trading partner automatically populates the buying Business legal name, VAT number (if present), and UNN on the invoice from their verified profile. | After selection, these fields display the trading partner's profile data and are not editable by the business. |
| FR-4.4 | If the selected trading partner has no VAT number, the invoice proceeds with UNN as the buying Business identifier only. | Invoice can be saved as a Draft and later submitted with the VAT number field blank for that buying Business. |
| FR-4.5 | Selling Business details (legal name, VAT number, UNN, logo) are pulled automatically from the business's own profile and are not editable on the invoice. | These fields display the business's profile data with no input control available to change them on the invoice. |
| FR-4.6 | The invoice date shown during Draft is a placeholder only and can be freely changed while in Draft. | Changing the invoice date field while in Draft status is allowed and does not trigger any validation against ZATCA. |
| FR-4.7 | Due date is a required manual field before an invoice can be submitted. | Attempting to submit an invoice with no due date set is blocked with a clear message. |
| FR-4.8 | Every line item must be added from the business's catalog. There is no free-text line item entry. | The line item field only accepts a selection from the catalog or the quick-add catalog creation flow. No plain text line entry is available. |
| FR-4.9 | Adding a catalog item to a line copies its Name, description, unit of measure, price, and VAT treatment onto that line, each independently editable for that line only. | Changing the price or VAT treatment on one invoice line does not change the value on the underlying catalog item, nor on any other invoice line using the same item. |
| FR-4.10 | Quantity is required on every line item with a minimum value of 1\. | Saving a line with quantity blank, zero, or negative is blocked with a clear message. |
| FR-4.11 | A discount can be applied at the line level only, as either a fixed amount or a percentage. | No discount control exists at the invoice-total level. Each line independently supports a fixed amount or percentage discount entry. |
| FR-4.12 | VAT is calculated on the line amount after the discount is applied, not before. | For a line with a discount, the displayed VAT amount reflects the post-discount taxable amount, and this is verifiable against the displayed taxable amount and VAT rate. |
| FR-4.13 | The invoice summary shows a separate VAT amount for each distinct VAT rate present on the invoice, not a single combined VAT figure. | An invoice with both Standard and Exempt lines displays two separate VAT rows in the summary, each with its own amount. |
| FR-4.14 | Notes is an optional free-text field with no hard character limit and no language restriction. | A business can save a Draft with the Notes field empty, or containing Arabic text, English text, or both, of any reasonable length. |
| FR-4.15 | A Draft invoice can be saved in an incomplete state and returned to later. | A business can leave the invoice creation screen with required fields incomplete and the invoice remains accessible afterward with the same partial data. |
| FR-4.16 | A Draft invoice can be permanently deleted. | Deleting a Draft removes it from the business's invoice list with no remaining record. |

**Stories Pack**

## **INV-4-US01 \- Create and Manage a Draft Invoice**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to create and manage a Draft invoice so that I can prepare it over time before submitting it for clearance.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Starting a new invoice creates an empty invoice with lifecycle status Draft.  
* The user is taken directly to the invoice creation screen.  
* A Draft has no official invoice reference number or legally binding identifiers.  
* A Draft is not sent to ZATCA and has no legal standing.  
* The user can save a Draft at any point, including when required fields are incomplete.  
* Returning to the Draft restores all previously saved data.  
* The user can edit any Draft field that is defined as editable.  
* The user can permanently delete a Draft.  
* Deleting a Draft removes it from the Business invoice list.  
* Once the invoice leaves Draft, it cannot be edited or deleted.

---

## **INV-4-US02 \- Select the Buyer and Populate Business Details**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to select an existing Trading Partner as the buyer so that verified buyer and seller information is used on the invoice.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The buyer can only be selected from the Current Business's existing Trading Partners.  
* Free-text buyer entry is not available.  
* A buyer is not created automatically from the invoice flow.  
* Selecting a Trading Partner copies its legal name, VAT number when present, and UNN from its verified profile.  
* Buyer legal name, VAT number, and UNN are read-only on the invoice.  
* A Trading Partner without a VAT number can still be selected and the invoice can proceed using its UNN.  
* The selling Business legal name, VAT number, UNN, and uploaded logo are populated from its verified profile.  
* Selling Business details are read-only on the invoice.  
* Changing either Business profile later does not silently rewrite the saved invoice without an explicit product-defined refresh action.

---

## **INV-4-US03 \- Set Draft Invoice and Due Dates**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to set planning and due dates on a Draft so that the invoice is ready for submission at the correct time.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The invoice date shown in Draft is a planning placeholder.  
* The user can freely change the placeholder invoice date while the invoice remains Draft.  
* Changing the Draft invoice date does not trigger ZATCA validation.  
* The due date is entered manually by the user.  
* The due date is required before submission.  
* No due date is calculated automatically from payment terms.  
* A missing due date does not prevent saving an incomplete Draft.  
* A missing due date blocks submission with a clear validation message.

---

## **INV-4-US04 \- Add Catalogue Items to an Invoice**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to add items from the Business Catalogue so that every manually created invoice line is based on a controlled item.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Every manually created invoice line must originate from a Catalogue Item.  
* Free-text invoice line creation is not available.  
* Only Catalogue Items eligible for invoice selection can be selected.  
* The item picker only exposes items belonging to the Current Business.  
* When the needed item does not exist, the user can open the Catalogue quick-create flow without losing the current Draft context.  
* After quick creation, the new Catalogue Item becomes available for selection in the same Draft.  
* Creating a Catalogue Item does not automatically create an invoice line.  
* Selecting an item more than once creates separate invoice lines when the user explicitly adds it more than once.

---

## **INV-4-US05 \- Override the Catalogue Snapshot on an Invoice Line**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to adjust the copied values on an invoice line so that the line reflects the specific transaction without changing the Catalogue Item.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Adding a Catalogue Item copies its Name, Description when present, Unit of Measure when present, Unit Price, and VAT Treatment onto the invoice line.  
* Each copied value can be changed independently for that invoice line.  
* Changing an invoice line does not modify the underlying Catalogue Item.  
* Changing one invoice line does not modify another line created from the same Catalogue Item.  
* Later Catalogue Item edits or lifecycle changes do not rewrite an existing invoice line, including a line in a saved Draft.  
* The invoice line retains the copied and adjusted values used for the transaction.

---

## **INV-4-US06 \- Enter Quantity and Line-Level Discounts**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to enter quantities and line-level discounts so that each invoice line reflects the agreed commercial terms.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Quantity is required for every invoice line.  
* Quantity must be at least 1.  
* Blank, zero, and negative quantities are rejected with a clear message.  
* No maximum quantity is imposed by this PRD.  
* A discount can only be applied to an individual line.  
* No invoice-level discount control is available.  
* A line discount can be entered as a fixed Saudi Riyal amount or a percentage.  
* The line shows the original amount, the discount amount, and the resulting taxable amount.  
* Updating a quantity or discount recalculates the affected line and invoice summary.

---

## **INV-4-US07 \- Calculate Line and Invoice Totals**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want invoice calculations to update automatically so that I can verify the amount the buyer will owe.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A line's taxable amount is calculated after applying its discount.  
* VAT is calculated on the post-discount taxable amount.  
* Each line displays quantity, unit price, discount when present, taxable amount, VAT rate, VAT amount, and line total.  
* The invoice subtotal equals the sum of all line taxable amounts after discounts and before VAT.  
* The invoice summary displays a separate VAT row for every distinct VAT treatment or rate present.  
* Standard and Exempt amounts are not combined into one VAT row.  
* Total VAT equals the sum of VAT across all invoice lines.  
* Invoice total equals subtotal plus total VAT.  
* Repeated recalculation produces the same totals for the same saved inputs.

---

## **INV-4-US08 \- Add Notes and Use Saudi Riyal Currency**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to add optional notes to a Saudi Riyal invoice so that supporting information appears on the final document.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Notes are optional.  
* Notes accept Arabic, English, or a combination of both.  
* Notes have no hard character limit defined by this PRD.  
* A soft guidance count is displayed to help the user keep the document well formatted.  
* Notes are preserved when the Draft is saved and reopened.  
* Notes appear on the invoice document produced after clearance.  
* Every invoice is denominated in Saudi Riyals.  
* No currency selector is available.

---

# 5 \- Invoice Creation \- Submission & ZATCA

**Invoice Creation \- Submission & ZATCA Clearance**

| Related documents: Document 4 (Invoice Creation \- Drafting), Document 10 (Invoice List View), Document 11 (Invoice Detail View & Status Lifecycle), Document 12 (Credit Note Creation). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes what happens when a business submits a completed Draft invoice \- from the moment they confirm submission through to the invoice being cleared by ZATCA or rejected. This is the point at which an invoice becomes a real, legally binding document.

# **Submission is a single action**

A business submits an invoice for clearance with one submission action. The moment a business submits, two things happen together: the invoice's identifiers are locked, and the invoice is sent to ZATCA for clearance. There is no in-between state where identifiers are locked but the invoice has not yet been sent.

# **What locks at submission**

* The invoice date locks to the actual date of submission, replacing whatever placeholder date was shown during Draft. The business cannot set this manually.

* The invoice's official reference number is assigned. This number follows a prefix the business has set up, with APEX automatically continuing the sequence \- the business does not type this number.

* Every line item, amount, and detail on the invoice is locked. No further editing is possible from this point forward, on this invoice, by anyone.

# **What the business sees while awaiting clearance**

After submission, the invoice shows the status Sent to ZATCA. This means APEX has sent the invoice to ZATCA and is waiting for a response. A timestamp tooltip is shown indicating how long the invoice has been in this state.

The invoice remains in Sent to ZATCA for as long as it takes to receive a response from ZATCA. There is no automatic escalation, alert, or change in business experience based on how long this takes \- the invoice simply remains in this status until ZATCA responds.

# **Outcome: Cleared**

If ZATCA accepts the invoice, it becomes Cleared. This is now a complete, legally valid invoice. From this point:

* The invoice can never be edited or deleted by anyone, under any circumstance.

* The only way to correct a Cleared invoice is through a credit note, described in Document 12\.

* The business can now download the invoice document, and the trading partner record reflects this transaction.

# **Outcome: Rejected**

If ZATCA rejects the invoice, it becomes Rejected. The reference number and identifiers already assigned to this invoice can never be reused on any other invoice.

* A Rejected invoice is never deleted. It remains permanently visible in the business's invoice records.

* The business only path forward is to create a brand new invoice. There is no edit-and-resubmit action on a Rejected invoice \- the new invoice is a separate Draft, built from scratch.

# **If submission cannot be completed**

If APEX is unable to confirm whether ZATCA received the submission \- for example due to a connectivity issue \- the invoice remains in Sent to ZATCA. APEX continues checking for ZATCA's response. The business is not shown a Draft state again, since the invoice's identifiers are already locked and cannot be reassigned. Once a response is confirmed, the invoice moves to either Cleared or Rejected as normal.

# **Status labels**

The following labels are shown to the business throughout APEX \- on the invoice itself, in the invoice list, and in filters. These same labels apply consistently everywhere.

| Label shown to business  | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| Draft | Being built. Not yet submitted. Covered in Document 4\. |
| Sent to ZATCA | Submitted. Awaiting a response from ZATCA. |
| Cleared | Accepted by ZATCA. Final, legally valid, cannot be changed. |
| Rejected | Not accepted by ZATCA. Permanent record, cannot be resubmitted \- a new invoice must be created. |

# **What a business can do at each status**

| Status | Available actions |
| :---- | :---- |
| Draft | Edit, delete, submit for clearance. |
| Sent to ZATCA | View only. No action available \- the business waits for the outcome. |
| Cleared | Download the invoice document, issue a credit note. (Recording a payment and requesting financing are covered in separate modules later.) |
| Rejected | View only. The business creates a new invoice separately if needed. |

# **Record keeping**

Every invoice, regardless of outcome, is retained permanently and is never deleted once it leaves Draft status. This includes Rejected invoices. This reflects the Saudi requirement to keep invoice records for a minimum of six years.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-5.1 | Submitting a Draft invoice locks its identifiers and sends it for ZATCA clearance as one single action. | There is no intermediate state visible to the business where identifiers are locked but the invoice has not yet been sent to ZATCA. |
| FR-5.2 | The invoice date locks to the actual date of submission and overrides any placeholder date set during Draft. | After submission, the invoice date displayed matches the date the submission occurred, regardless of what date was shown while in Draft. |
| FR-5.3 | The business cannot manually set or edit the invoice date at or after submission. | No date input control is available for invoice date once the invoice has left Draft status. |
| FR-5.4 | The official invoice reference number is assigned automatically at submission, following the business's configured prefix and continuing sequence. | The assigned reference number is unique, follows the business's prefix, and is not editable by the business. |
| FR-5.5 | Once submitted, no field on the invoice can be edited by any business, regardless of outcome. | No edit control is available on an invoice in Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, or Rejected status. |
| FR-5.6 | An invoice in Sent to ZATCA displays a tooltip timestamp showing how long it has been awaiting a response. | The tooltip timestamp is visible on the invoice status and updates to reflect elapsed time. |
| FR-5.7 | An invoice remains in Sent to ZATCA indefinitely until a clearance response is received, with no automatic escalation or alert shown to the business. | No status change, alert, or notification occurs based solely on elapsed time in Sent to ZATCA. |
| FR-5.8 | When ZATCA accepts the invoice, its status changes to Cleared and it becomes permanently uneditable and undeletable. | No edit or delete control is available on a Cleared invoice under any circumstance. |
| FR-5.9 | When ZATCA rejects the invoice, its status changes to Rejected and its identifiers are never reused on any future invoice. | A new invoice created afterward is assigned a different reference number and different underlying identifiers from the rejected one. |
| FR-5.10 | A Rejected invoice is retained permanently and is never deleted. | A Rejected invoice remains visible in the business's invoice list and detail views indefinitely. |
| FR-5.11 | There is no resubmit action on a Rejected invoice. A business must create a separate new invoice. | No submit or resubmit control is available on an invoice in Rejected status. |
| FR-5.12 | If APEX cannot confirm ZATCA's response due to a connectivity issue, the invoice remains in Sent to ZATCA rather than reverting to Draft. | An invoice that has been submitted never returns to Draft status under any circumstance. |
| FR-5.13 | A Cleared invoice can be downloaded by the business as a document. | A download control is available on a Cleared invoice and produces the invoice document. |
| FR-5.14 | A Cleared invoice can have a credit note issued against it. | An issue credit note control is available on a Cleared invoice, opening the credit note creation flow described in Document 12\. |

**Stories Pack**

## **INV-5-US01 \- Submit a Draft Invoice for Clearance**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to submit a completed Draft invoice once so that it becomes locked and is sent to ZATCA for clearance as one action.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Submission is available only for an invoice in Draft status.  
* Submission is blocked when required invoice data is missing.  
* Confirming submission locks the invoice identifiers and sends the invoice to ZATCA as one logical action.  
* No user-visible state exists where identifiers are locked but the invoice has not been sent.  
* After the submission request is accepted, the lifecycle status becomes Sent to ZATCA.  
* All invoice lines, amounts, parties, dates, notes, and other details become read-only.  
* Repeating the same submission action does not assign another reference number or create another logical ZATCA submission.  
* A submitted invoice never returns to Draft.

---

## **INV-5-US02 \- Assign and Lock Invoice Identifiers**

**User Story**  
As a Business, I want invoice identifiers assigned automatically at submission so that official numbering remains controlled and unique.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The official invoice date is set to the actual submission date.  
* The submission date replaces any placeholder date used in Draft.  
* The user cannot manually set or edit the invoice date after submission.  
* The official invoice reference number is assigned automatically at submission.  
* The reference number uses the Business's configured invoice prefix.  
* The numbering sequence continues automatically and cannot be typed or edited by the user.  
* Every submitted invoice receives a unique reference number within the Business.  
* Concurrent submissions cannot receive the same reference number.  
* An assigned reference number is never released for reuse, regardless of the clearance outcome.

---

## **INV-5-US03 \- View an Invoice Awaiting ZATCA Response**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to see that an invoice is awaiting ZATCA so that I understand why no further action is currently available.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A submitted invoice displays lifecycle status Sent to ZATCA.  
* The status is view-only and no edit, delete, cancel, or resubmit action is available.  
* A timestamp or tooltip shows how long the invoice has been awaiting a response.  
* The elapsed-time display updates as time passes.  
* The invoice remains in this status until a confirmed ZATCA outcome is received.  
* Elapsed time alone does not trigger a status change, escalation, alert, or automatic user action.  
* The same status label is used consistently in invoice lists, filters, and detail views.

---

## **INV-5-US04 \- Handle an Unconfirmed ZATCA Submission**

**User Story**  
As a Business, I want an uncertain ZATCA submission to remain safely pending so that locked identifiers are not reused or exposed through a false Draft state.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* If APEX cannot confirm whether ZATCA received the invoice, the invoice remains Sent to ZATCA.  
* The invoice does not revert to Draft.  
* The assigned date, reference number, and identifiers remain locked.  
* APEX continues checking for a confirmed ZATCA response.  
* The user cannot create another submission for the same invoice while the outcome is unknown.  
* When a confirmed response is received, the invoice transitions once to either Cleared or Rejected.  
* Repeated delivery of the same confirmed response does not apply the outcome more than once.

---

## **INV-5-US05 \- Complete a Cleared Invoice**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want an accepted invoice to become Cleared so that I can use the legally valid document and correct it only through a credit note.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A ZATCA acceptance changes the lifecycle status to `Cleared`.  
* A Cleared invoice is legally valid and permanently read-only.  
* No edit, delete, void, cancel, or revert-to-Draft action is available.  
* The Business can download the cleared invoice document.  
* The downloaded document contains the final locked invoice data and identifiers.  
* The Business can start the credit note flow from the Cleared invoice.  
* The related Trading Partner record reflects the transaction.  
* Reprocessing the same clearance response does not create duplicate records or duplicate transaction effects.

---

## **INV-5-US06 \- Retain a Rejected Invoice**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want a rejected invoice retained as a permanent record so that its identifiers and ZATCA outcome remain traceable.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A ZATCA rejection changes the lifecycle status to `Rejected`.  
* A Rejected invoice remains permanently visible in invoice records.  
* Its official reference number and underlying identifiers are never reused.  
* The invoice is view-only and cannot be edited, deleted, voided, cancelled, or returned to Draft.  
* No submit or resubmit action is available.  
* The user must create a separate new Draft when another invoice is needed.  
* The new Draft receives different identifiers when it is submitted.

---

## **INV-5-US07 \- Enforce Invoice Status Actions and Retention**

**User Story**  
As a Business, I want invoice actions controlled by lifecycle status so that legally significant records cannot be altered improperly.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Draft allows Edit, Delete, and Submit for clearance.  
* Sent to ZATCA is view-only.  
* Cleared allows Download and Issue Credit Note.  
* Rejected is view-only.  
* No invoice can be voided or cancelled outright.  
* No invoice that has left Draft can be permanently deleted by a Business User.  
* Every invoice that leaves Draft is retained as a permanent Business record.  
* Status and action rules are enforced consistently from list and detail screens and cannot be bypassed through direct requests.

---

# 6 \- Invoice Import \- Bulk CSV (Invoices)

**Invoice Import \- Bulk CSV (Invoices)**

| Related documents: Document 7 (Invoice Import \- Bulk CSV, Credit Notes), Document 10 (Invoice List View), Document 11 (Invoice Detail View & Status Lifecycle). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes how a business brings invoices that were already issued and cleared by ZATCA outside of APEX into the platform, by uploading a file. This is for businesses that have been invoicing through another system and want their invoice history and ongoing invoices visible and usable inside APEX for financing applications.

# **How this is different from creating an invoice in APEX**

An invoice brought in through this path was already issued and cleared by ZATCA before it reached APEX. APEX is not creating a new invoice or submitting anything to ZATCA \- it is registering an already-existing, already-legal invoice into the business's records. This means the rules are different from Document 4 and Document 5 in several important ways, covered below.

# **The catalog does not apply here**

Line items on an imported invoice come directly from the file the business uploads, exactly as they appear in the business's original system. There is no requirement for these line items to match anything in the business's APEX catalog, and importing invoices does not create or change any catalog items.

# **How the import works**

* The business downloads a file template provided by APEX.

* The business fills the template with their invoice data, or exports it from their existing system into that shape.

* The business uploads the file.

* APEX checks every row and shows the business a preview of what will be imported, along with any rows that have a problem.

* The business confirms, and the valid rows are registered as invoices. Rows with problems are not imported.

# **Template \- what every invoice row must include**

Every field that ZATCA requires on a Standard Tax Invoice must be present in the uploaded data. A ready-to-use template file (Invoice Bulk Import Template) is provided alongside this document, with one example invoice filled in for reference. The template requires, at minimum:

* The official invoice reference number, exactly as it appears on the original cleared invoice.

* The original invoice date, exactly as it appears on the original cleared invoice.

* Buying Business details matching an existing trading partner in the business's APEX account.

* Due date.

* Line item details \- description, quantity, unit price, VAT treatment, and line total.

* The invoice's subtotal, VAT amount, and total.

# **Reference number is taken exactly as provided**

Unlike invoices created inside APEX, the invoice reference number on an imported invoice is not generated by APEX \- it is accepted exactly as it appears in the uploaded file, because it was already assigned and cleared by ZATCA through the business's original system. APEX only checks that this reference number has not already been used elsewhere in the business's APEX records.

# **Matching the Trading Partner**

The trading partner named in the file must match an existing trading partner already on the business's APEX account. If no match is found, that row is rejected. The business cannot create a new trading partner automatically through this import \- the trading partner must already exist.

# **VAT treatment on imported lines**

Each line's VAT treatment is taken from the file exactly as provided and must be either Standard or Exempt, matching APEX's two supported VAT categories.

# **Validation rules**

| Check | Result if it fails |
| :---- | :---- |
| Reference number missing or duplicates an existing invoice in this business's APEX records | Row rejected |
| Buying Business does not match an existing trading partner | Row rejected |
| A required ZATCA field is missing | Row rejected |
| VAT treatment on a line is not Standard or Exempt | Row rejected |
| One row in the file has a problem | Only that row is rejected \- every other valid row in the same file is still imported |

# **What status an imported invoice receives**

An invoice that passes all checks is registered with the status Importing while APEX completes registering it, and then moves to Cleared \- the same status a successfully cleared invoice created inside APEX would have. It is not registered as a Draft, because it was never a draft \- it is a fact that has already happened.

If a row fails validation, it is not imported at all, and is reported to the business as a failed row with the specific reason.

# **Possible credit notes against imported invoices**

An invoice being imported may already have a credit note issued against it in the business's original system, which APEX has no way of knowing about unless the business provides it. To prevent an inaccurate outstanding balance, the business can upload a second file, alongside the invoice file, containing any credit notes that exist against the invoices being imported. This is described fully in Document 7\. If a business does not have any credit notes to bring in, they simply do not upload a second file.

# **After import**

Imported invoices appear in the same invoice list as invoices created directly in APEX, alongside a small indicator showing they arrived through file import rather than being created manually. See Document 10 for the full list view.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-6.1 | A business can download a file template containing the columns required for invoice import. | Template downloads and contains all fields listed in this document as required, including reference number, dates, trading partner details, line items, and totals. |
| FR-6.2 | A business can upload a completed file to import multiple invoices at once. | Upload accepts a file in the supported format and proceeds to a preview step before anything is created. |
| FR-6.3 | Each row's invoice reference number is validated as present and not already used in the business's APEX invoice records. | A row is rejected if the reference number is blank or matches an existing invoice already in this business's account. |
| FR-6.4 | Each row's trading partner must match an existing trading partner on the business's account. | A row is rejected if the trading partner information in the file does not match any existing trading partner. |
| FR-6.5 | Each row must contain every ZATCA-required field for a Standard Tax Invoice. | A row is rejected if any required field \- including dates, line item details, and totals \- is missing. |
| FR-6.6 | Each line's VAT treatment must be either Standard or Exempt. | A row is rejected if any line's VAT treatment value is anything other than Standard or Exempt. |
| FR-6.7 | A row that fails validation does not block other valid rows in the same file from being imported. | After confirming the import, every row without an error is registered as an invoice, regardless of other rows having errors. |
| FR-6.8 | A successfully imported invoice is registered with Cleared status, not Draft. | After import completes, the invoice's status reads Cleared and not Draft. |
| FR-6.9 | An imported invoice's reference number is stored exactly as provided in the file, without being reformatted or reassigned by APEX. | The reference number displayed on the imported invoice matches the value in the uploaded file character for character. |
| FR-6.10 | After import, the business sees a summary of how many invoices were imported successfully and which rows failed, with a specific reason per failed row. | The result screen lists a success count and, separately, every failed row with its row number and the exact validation reason. |
| FR-6.11 | Importing invoices does not create, modify, or reference the business's catalog in any way. | After import, no new catalog items exist as a result of the import, and existing catalog items are unchanged. |

**Stories Pack**

## **INV-6-US01 \- Download the Invoice Import Template**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to download the approved invoice import template so that I can prepare externally cleared invoices in the format APEX accepts.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The template downloads in the supported file format.  
* The template includes all fields required for a Standard Tax Invoice.  
* It includes the original invoice reference number and original invoice date.  
* It includes Buying Business details used to match an existing Trading Partner.  
* It includes due date, line descriptions, quantities, unit prices, VAT treatments, line totals, subtotal, VAT amount, and invoice total.  
* The template includes an example invoice for reference when provided by the approved product asset.  
* Downloading a template does not create an invoice or an import record.

---

## **INV-6-US02 \- Upload and Preview an Invoice Import**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to upload an invoice file and preview its validation results so that I can review problems before invoices are registered.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A completed file in the supported format can be uploaded.  
* APEX validates every invoice row independently.  
* No invoice is registered before the user confirms the preview.  
* The preview distinguishes valid rows from invalid rows.  
* Every invalid row shows its source row number and a specific reason.  
* The preview uses the values from the uploaded file without applying Catalogue rules.  
* Uploading the same file for preview more than once does not itself create duplicate invoices.

---

## **INV-6-US03 \- Validate Imported Invoice Data**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want imported invoice rows validated against the invoice import rules so that incomplete or unsupported invoices are not registered.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The original invoice reference number is required.  
* A row is invalid when its reference number duplicates an invoice already registered for the Current Business.  
* Every ZATCA-required Standard Tax Invoice field must be present.  
* Required dates, line-item details, and totals must be present.  
* Every line's VAT Treatment must be exactly Standard or Exempt.  
* Unsupported VAT Treatment values invalidate the affected invoice row.  
* Validation errors are deterministic and identify the failed rule clearly.  
* An invalid row does not create an invoice record during preview or confirmation.

---

## **INV-6-US04 \- Match an Imported Invoice to a Trading Partner**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want each imported invoice matched to an existing Trading Partner so that the buyer is linked to a verified Business record.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Buyer data in the file is matched only against Trading Partners belonging to the Current Business.  
* A matching Trading Partner must already exist before import confirmation.  
* The import does not create a new Trading Partner automatically.  
* A row with no matching Trading Partner is rejected with a clear reason.  
* A matching result is stable for the previewed data unless the Trading Partner record changes before confirmation.  
* Confirmation revalidates the match before registering the invoice.

---

## **INV-6-US05 \- Confirm a Partial Invoice Import**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to confirm an invoice import so that valid invoices are registered even when other rows contain errors.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Only rows that pass all validation checks are registered.  
* Invalid rows are not registered.  
* One invalid row does not block any other valid row in the same file.  
* Confirmation rechecks uniqueness and Trading Partner matching against current data.  
* A row that becomes invalid after preview fails without blocking other valid rows.  
* Repeating confirmation for the same import result does not create duplicate invoices.  
* Each accepted invoice is registered once with the exact uploaded business data.

---

## **INV-6-US06 \- Register an Imported Invoice as Cleared**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want a valid externally issued invoice registered as Cleared so that it is available in APEX without being submitted to ZATCA again.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* An accepted invoice may display Importing while APEX completes registration.  
* After successful registration, its lifecycle status becomes Cleared, not Draft.  
* APEX does not submit the imported invoice to ZATCA.  
* The original invoice reference number is stored and displayed character for character as provided.  
* APEX does not apply the Business's generated invoice prefix or sequence to the imported reference.  
* The original invoice date and imported line data are preserved as provided.  
* The invoice is immutable after registration under the same Cleared invoice rules.  
* The invoice is marked as originating from file import.

---

## **INV-6-US07 \- View the Invoice Import Result**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to view the final import result so that I know which invoices succeeded and which rows require correction.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The result shows the number of invoices registered successfully.  
* Every failed row is listed separately.  
* Each failed row shows its original row number.  
* Each failed row shows the exact validation reason.  
* Successfully imported invoices appear in the unified invoice list.  
* Failed rows can be corrected and submitted through a new import.  
* The result remains consistent when the confirmation response is refreshed or retried.

---

## **INV-6-US08 \- Keep Invoice Import Independent from the Catalogue**

**User Story**  
As a Business, I want imported invoice lines kept independent from the Catalogue so that external invoice history is preserved exactly as issued.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Imported line items do not need to match Catalogue Items.  
* Importing an invoice does not create Catalogue Items.  
* Importing an invoice does not update or deactivate existing Catalogue Items.  
* Imported invoice lines store the descriptions, quantities, prices, VAT treatments, and totals provided in the file.  
* Catalogue validation is not applied as an additional condition for invoice import.  
* File-imported invoices are distinguishable from manually created and API-imported invoices by their origin indicator.

# 7 \- Credit Notes Import \- Bulk CSV (Credit Notes)

**Credit Notes Import \- Bulk CSV (Credit Notes)**

| Related documents: Document 6 (Invoice Import \- Bulk CSV, Invoices), Document 12 (Credit Note Creation), Document 13 (Credit Note Submission & Lifecycle), Document 14 (Credit Note List View). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes how a business brings in credit notes that already exist against invoices being imported through Document 6\. This ensures the outstanding balance on an imported invoice is accurate from the moment it appears in APEX, rather than showing the full original amount when part of it was already credited outside the platform.

# **Why this matters**

When a business imports invoices that were issued through another system, that system may have already issued credit notes against some of those invoices \- for example because goods were returned, or a price was corrected. APEX has no way of knowing this unless the business provides it. Without this information, an imported invoice would show an incorrect outstanding balance, which creates risk both for the business's own records and for any future financing request made against that invoice.

# **This file is optional**

A business only uses this import if they have credit notes to bring in. A business with no existing credit notes against their imported invoices simply imports their invoice file from Document 6 and does not upload anything here.

# **How it works**

* The business uploads their invoice file, as described in Document 6\.

* In the same import session, the business can optionally upload a second file containing credit notes.

* APEX matches each credit note in the file to its original invoice, using the original invoice's reference number.

* APEX checks every row and shows the business a preview, along with any rows that have a problem.

* The business confirms, and the valid credit notes are registered, linked to their original invoices, with the outstanding balance recalculated automatically.

# **Matching a credit note to its original invoice**

Every credit note in the file must reference the original invoice it corrects, using that invoice's reference number. This is the same reference number described in Document 6\.

* If the original invoice is included in the same import \- in the invoice file uploaded alongside this one \- the match succeeds and both are registered together.

* If the original invoice already exists in APEX from an earlier import, the match also succeeds.

* If no matching invoice can be found at all \- neither in this import nor already in APEX \- the credit note row is rejected. A credit note can never exist in APEX without its original invoice already present.

# **Template \- what every credit note row must include**

A ready-to-use template file (Credit Note Bulk Import Template) is provided alongside this document, with one example credit note filled in for reference. The template requires:

* The reference number of the original invoice being corrected.

* The credit note's own reference number, exactly as it appears in the original system.

* The reason for the credit note.

* Which line items, or which amounts, are being credited.

* The credit note's date.

* The resulting subtotal, VAT amount, and total being credited.

# **Validation rules**

| Check | Result if it fails |
| :---- | :---- |
| Original invoice reference number does not match any invoice in this import or already in APEX | Row rejected, with a message that the original invoice could not be found |
| Credit note reference number missing or duplicates one already in APEX | Row rejected |
| Required field missing | Row rejected |
| One row in the file has a problem | Only that row is rejected \- every other valid row is still imported |

# **What happens to the original invoice once a credit note is imported**

Once a credit note is successfully imported and linked to its original invoice, that invoice's outstanding balance is recalculated automatically to reflect the credited amount. The business does not need to do anything further.

# **Status of an imported credit note**

A successfully imported credit note is registered with the same Cleared status as its original invoice, since it was already legally issued outside APEX before being brought in.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-7.1 | A business can optionally upload a credit note file alongside an invoice import, without it being required. | An invoice import can be completed successfully with no credit note file uploaded at all. |
| FR-7.2 | Each credit note row must reference an original invoice that exists either in the same import or already in APEX, using that invoice's reference number. | A credit note row is rejected if its referenced invoice reference number cannot be matched to any invoice in the current import or already in the business's APEX records. |
| FR-7.3 | A credit note cannot be imported on its own without its original invoice present. | There is no path for a credit note row to be accepted if its original invoice cannot be found. |
| FR-7.4 | Each credit note row's own reference number is validated as present and not already used in the business's APEX credit note records. | A row is rejected if the credit note reference number is blank or duplicates an existing one. |
| FR-7.5 | A row that fails validation does not block other valid rows in the same file from being imported. | After confirming the import, every row without an error is registered, regardless of other rows having errors. |
| FR-7.6 | A successfully imported credit note is automatically linked to its original invoice. | Viewing the original invoice shows the imported credit note linked to it, and viewing the credit note shows a link back to the original invoice. |
| FR-7.7 | Importing a credit note automatically recalculates the outstanding balance of its original invoice. | After import, the original invoice's displayed outstanding balance reflects the credited amount without further action by the business. |
| FR-7.8 | A successfully imported credit note is registered with Cleared status. | After import completes, the credit note's status reads Cleared. |
| FR-7.9 | After import, the business sees a summary of how many credit notes were imported successfully and which rows failed, with a specific reason per failed row. | The result screen lists a success count and, separately, every failed row with its row number and the exact validation reason. |

# [**Bulk Import Template File**](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1jNwysK-P3ML8UbAJnUUYlW6PnWIE3jH78U9ewAnhmbA/edit?gid=296466017#gid=296466017)

**Stories pack**

## **CN-7-US01 \- Optionally Add Credit Notes to an Invoice Import**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to optionally upload a credit note file with an invoice import so that existing external credits are reflected in APEX from the start.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The invoice import can be completed without a credit note file.  
* A credit note file can be uploaded as a second file in the same import session.  
* The approved credit note template can be downloaded in the supported format.  
* The template includes original invoice reference, credit note reference, reason, credited lines or amounts, credit note date, subtotal, VAT amount, and total credited.  
* Uploading the optional file does not prevent previewing the invoice file.  
* No credit note is registered before confirmation.

---

## **CN-7-US02 \- Match an Imported Credit Note to Its Original Invoice**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want each imported credit note matched to its original invoice so that a credit note cannot exist without the document it corrects.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Every credit note row must contain the original invoice reference number.  
* The referenced invoice may be a valid invoice in the same import session.  
* The referenced invoice may already exist in the Current Business's APEX records.  
* A credit note row is rejected when no matching invoice exists in either location.  
* A credit note is never registered without its original invoice.  
* If the referenced invoice row in the same session fails registration, the dependent credit note is not registered.  
* Cross-Business invoice references are not treated as a match.

---

## **CN-7-US03 \- Validate Imported Credit Note Data**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want credit note rows validated before import so that incomplete or duplicate credit notes are not registered.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The credit note's own reference number is required.  
* A credit note reference number must not duplicate one already registered for the Current Business.  
* The reason is required.  
* Credited line items or credited amounts are required.  
* The credit note date, subtotal, VAT amount, and total credited are required.  
* The credit note reference number is preserved exactly as provided by the external system.  
* Every invalid row is identified with its row number and a specific failure reason.  
* Validation does not create or update the original invoice.

---

## **CN-7-US04 \- Preview and Confirm a Partial Credit Note Import**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to preview and confirm credit note rows independently so that valid credits are registered even when other rows fail.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The preview shows valid and invalid credit note rows before registration.  
* No credit note is registered during preview.  
* Confirmation registers every row that still passes validation.  
* One invalid row does not block another valid row.  
* Confirmation revalidates invoice matching and reference-number uniqueness.  
* A row that becomes invalid after preview fails without blocking other rows.  
* Repeating confirmation does not register the same credit note more than once.

---

## **CN-7-US05 \- Register and Link an Imported Credit Note**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want a valid external credit note registered and linked so that both documents show their relationship.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A successfully imported credit note is registered with lifecycle status `Cleared`.  
* It is not registered as a Draft and is not submitted to ZATCA by APEX.  
* The credit note is automatically linked to exactly one original invoice.  
* The original invoice detail shows the related credit note.  
* The credit note detail shows a link back to the original invoice.  
* The credit note's reference number and original externally issued data are preserved.  
* Registering the same accepted row again does not create another link or credit note.

---

## **CN-7-US06 \- Recalculate the Imported Invoice Balance**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want an imported credit note to update the original invoice balance automatically so that the outstanding amount is accurate.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* After a credit note is successfully registered, the original invoice outstanding balance is recalculated.  
* The credited amount is reflected without further user action.  
* A failed credit note row does not change the original invoice.  
* Multiple successfully imported credit notes are each reflected once in the invoice balance.  
* Replaying the same import result does not reduce the balance more than once.  
* The updated balance is visible from the invoice detail view.

---

## **CN-7-US07 \- View the Credit Note Import Result**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to view the credit note import result so that I can correct failed rows and verify successful credits.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The result shows the number of credit notes registered successfully.  
* Every failed row is listed separately with its source row number.  
* Every failed row shows the exact validation reason.  
* Successful credit notes appear in the Credit Note list.  
* Related invoice balances reflect only successfully registered credit notes.  
* Failed rows can be corrected and submitted through a new import.

---
