# 8 \- Invoice Import \- API (Invoices)

**Invoice Import \- API (Invoices)**

| Related documents: Document 6 (Invoice Import \- Bulk CSV, Invoices) \- this document follows the same business rules through a different channel. Document 9 (Invoice Import \- API, Credit Notes), Document 10 (Invoice List View), Document 11 (Invoice Detail View & Status Lifecycle). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes the business requirements for a business to connect its own system directly to APEX, so that invoices it issues and clears through its own software are automatically brought into APEX without anyone manually uploading a file.

This document deliberately does not describe the technical design of this connection \- authentication methods, data formats, or message structures. Those decisions belong to the engineering team building this capability, who may also choose to use a third-party connector or middleware provider. This document sets out what the business needs the result to be, so that whoever designs the technical solution is building toward the right outcome.

# **Who this is for**

A business whose own software \- an ERP system, an accounting platform, or a custom-built system \- already issues and clears invoices with ZATCA, and who wants those invoices to appear in APEX automatically rather than through manual file upload.

# **One connection method for everyone**

APEX publishes a single, standard way for any business's system to connect and send invoice data. APEX does not build a custom connection for each individual business. If a business's own system cannot produce data in the shape APEX requires, it is the responsibility of that business, their ERP vendor, or their technical team to bridge that gap \- including through a third-party connector if needed. This is the only approach that allows APEX to support many different businesses, each using different software, without engineering having to build a new integration for every new business that joins.

# **Same business rules as file import**

An invoice brought in through this connection follows exactly the same business rules as an invoice brought in through file upload, described in Document 6:

* The invoice was already issued and cleared by ZATCA before it reaches APEX. APEX is registering it, not creating or submitting it.

* The invoice's line items do not need to relate to the business's APEX catalog in any way.

* The invoice's reference number is accepted exactly as provided, not generated by APEX.

* The business partner must already exist as a trading partner in the business's APEX account.

* Every ZATCA-required field must be present for the invoice to be accepted.

* VAT treatment on each line must be either Standard or Exempt.

* A successfully received invoice is registered with Cleared status.

* An invoice that does not meet these requirements is not registered, and the business's system receives a clear indication of why.

# **Access requires approval first**

A verified business on APEX is eligible to request access to this connection. However, access is not automatic the moment a business is verified \- it goes through an approval and testing step first.

* A verified business requests API access.

* The business is granted access to a test environment, where they can confirm their system correctly sends invoice data that meets APEX's requirements, without those invoices being treated as real.

* Once the business's connection is confirmed to be working correctly in the test environment, they are granted access to send real, live invoices.

This testing step exists because a malformed invoice reaching ZATCA in real conditions still has real consequences \- including the invoice being permanently rejected and its identifiers being unusable again. Testing first reduces the chance of this happening once a business is live.

# **What happens when something is wrong with an incoming invoice**

If an invoice sent through this connection does not meet APEX's requirements \- a missing field, an unmatched business partner, an invalid VAT treatment, or a duplicate reference number \- it is not registered. The business's own system receives a clear indication that the invoice was not accepted and why, so their technical team or software can correct it and resend.

# **Possible credit notes against API-imported invoices**

As with file import, an invoice arriving through this connection may already have a credit note issued against it in the business's original system. The business's system is expected to send any such credit notes through this same connection, alongside or shortly after their original invoice. This is described in Document 9\. An invoice connection that never sends credit note data for invoices that actually have them creates the same outstanding balance risk described in Document 6 and Document 7 \- this is the responsibility of the business and their technical integration, not something APEX can detect on its own.

# **After import**

Invoices that arrive through this connection appear in the same invoice list as those created manually or brought in through file upload, with an indicator showing they arrived through this connection. See Document 10\.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-8.1 | Any verified business on APEX can request access to connect their own system for invoice import. | A request access option is available to any business with a verified status, and not to unverified businesses. |
| FR-8.2 | A business is granted test access before being granted live access. | After requesting access, a business is first able to send invoices to a test environment, and is not yet able to send invoices that are registered as real, live invoices. |
| FR-8.3 | A business is only granted live access after their test connection is confirmed to meet APEX's requirements. | Live access is not available to a business until their test environment usage has been reviewed and approved. |
| FR-8.4 | An invoice received through this connection follows the same business rules as Document 6 \- already cleared, catalog-independent, reference number accepted as-is, business partner must be an existing trading partner, all ZATCA-required fields present, VAT treatment must be Standard or Exempt. | An invoice sent through this connection that fails any of these checks is not registered as an invoice in APEX. |
| FR-8.5 | A successfully received invoice is registered with Cleared status. | After being received and accepted, the invoice's status reads Cleared, not Draft or any other status. |
| FR-8.6 | An invoice that fails validation is not registered, and the business's own system receives an indication that it failed and why. | The business's connected system receives a response indicating rejection and the specific reason, rather than no response or a silent failure. |
| FR-8.7 | Invoices received through this connection do not create, modify, or reference the business's catalog in any way. | After receiving invoices through this connection, no new catalog items exist as a result, and existing catalog items are unchanged. |
| FR-8.8 | Invoices received through this connection appear in the same invoice list as invoices from every other channel, with an indicator of how they arrived. | The invoice list shows invoices from manual creation, file import, and this connection together, each distinguishable by an origin indicator. |

**Stories Pack**

## **INV-8-US01 \- Request Invoice API Access**

**User Story**  
As a verified Business, I want to request access to the invoice import connection so that my external system can send already-cleared invoices to APEX.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The request-access option is available to verified Businesses.  
* The option is not available to an unverified Business.  
* Requesting access does not immediately grant live access.  
* The request is associated with the Current Business.  
* A Business cannot use another Business's connection or access state.  
* The user can see the current access stage: not requested, test access, or live access.

---

## **INV-8-US02 \- Use a Test Invoice Connection**

**User Story**  
As a verified Business with approved test access, I want to send invoice data to a test environment so that I can validate my integration before sending live invoices.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Test access is granted before live access.  
* Test submissions use the same business validation rules intended for live invoices.  
* Test invoices are not registered as real Business invoices.  
* Test invoices do not appear in the live invoice list or become available for financing.  
* The connected system receives validation outcomes for test submissions.  
* Test access does not permit live invoice registration.  
* Repeated test submissions do not affect live numbering, balances, or records.

---

## **INV-8-US03 \- Approve Live Invoice API Access**

**User Story**  
As an authorised APEX reviewer, I want to approve a tested Business connection so that only integrations confirmed to meet APEX requirements can send live invoices.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Live access is unavailable until test usage has been reviewed and approved.  
* Approval applies to the specific Business connection.  
* A rejected or incomplete review keeps the Business in test-only access.  
* Once approved, the Business can send live invoices through the same standard connection.  
* Live approval does not alter invoice data already registered during any earlier approved live operation.

---

## **INV-8-US04 \- Send Invoices Through One Standard Connection**

**User Story**  
As a connected Business System, I want to send invoice data through one standard APEX contract so that the same integration can support Businesses using different external systems.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* APEX exposes one standard invoice-import method rather than a custom contract per Business.  
* The same required business fields and validation rules apply to every connected Business.  
* A Business, ERP vendor, technical team, or connector is responsible for mapping external data into the required APEX shape.  
* APEX does not add Business-specific validation exceptions silently.  
* The technical authentication, transport, and message design can be chosen by Engineering without changing these business outcomes.  
* An invoice arriving through this connection is treated as already issued and cleared externally.  
* APEX does not submit the received invoice to ZATCA.

---

## **INV-8-US05 \- Validate and Register an API Invoice**

**User Story**  
As a connected Business System, I want a valid externally cleared invoice registered in APEX so that it becomes available without manual file upload.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The invoice reference number is required, unique within the Business, and preserved exactly as received.  
* The Buying Business must match an existing Trading Partner in the Current Business.  
* Every ZATCA-required Standard Tax Invoice field must be present.  
* Every line's VAT Treatment must be Standard or Exempt.  
* Accepted line items do not need to match Catalogue Items.  
* A valid live invoice is registered with lifecycle status Cleared.  
* It is marked as originating from the direct system connection.  
* Registration does not create, update, or reference Catalogue Items.  
* Repeating the same accepted request does not register a duplicate invoice.

---

## **INV-8-US06 \- Return an API Invoice Rejection Reason**

**User Story**  
As a connected Business System, I want a clear response when an invoice is rejected so that I can correct the source data and resend it.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* An invoice that fails any required validation is not registered.  
* Failure reasons include missing required data, duplicate reference number, unmatched Trading Partner, and unsupported VAT Treatment when applicable.  
* The response clearly identifies that the invoice was not accepted.  
* The response includes a specific validation reason rather than a silent failure.  
* A rejected API request does not create a Cleared invoice or alter an existing invoice.  
* Corrected data can be sent again as a new request.  
* Technical retries of the same failed request do not create partial invoice records.

---

## **INV-8-US07 \- Show API-Imported Invoices in the Unified List**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want API-imported invoices shown with all other invoices so that I can manage one complete invoice record.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Accepted API invoices appear in the unified Invoice list.  
* They appear alongside manually created and file-imported invoices.  
* Each API-imported invoice displays the direct-connection origin indicator.  
* Selecting the invoice opens the standard Invoice detail view.  
* The same Cleared invoice actions and immutability rules apply regardless of origin.  
* Search, sort, and applicable filters include API-imported invoices.

---

# 9 \- Credit Notes Import \- API (Credit Notes)

**Credit Notes Import \- API (Credit Notes)**

| Related documents: Document 8 (Invoice Import \- API, Invoices), Document 7 (Invoice Import \- Bulk CSV, Credit Notes) \- same business rules through a different channel. Document 12 (Credit Note Creation), Document 13 (Credit Note Submission & Lifecycle), Document 14 (Credit Note List View). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes the business requirements for a business's own system to send credit notes into APEX through the same direct connection described in Document 8, for credit notes that exist against invoices arriving through that connection.

As with Document 8, this document describes what the business needs the result to be, not the technical design of the connection itself.

# **Same business rules as file import**

A credit note received through this connection follows exactly the same business rules as a credit note brought in through file upload, described in Document 7:

* A credit note must reference the original invoice it corrects, using that invoice's reference number.

* A credit note can never be registered in APEX without its original invoice already present \- either received earlier through this same connection, through file import, or created directly in APEX.

* A successfully received credit note is registered with Cleared status, and automatically recalculates the outstanding balance of its original invoice.

* A credit note that does not meet these requirements is not registered, and the business's system receives a clear indication of why.

# **Uses the same connection and access as invoices**

This is not a separate connection or a separate access request from Document 8\. A business that has been granted access to send invoices through the API uses that same connection to also send credit notes. There is no additional approval step specific to credit notes.

# **Sending credit notes alongside their original invoice**

A business's system is expected to send any credit note that exists against an invoice at the same time as, or shortly after, sending that invoice through this connection. This is the responsibility of the business's own system and its technical integration \- APEX has no way of independently knowing that an external credit note exists unless the business's system sends it.

# **What happens when something is wrong with an incoming credit note**

If a credit note sent through this connection does not meet APEX's requirements \- for example its original invoice cannot be found, or a required field is missing \- it is not registered. The business's own system receives a clear indication that the credit note was not accepted and why.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-9.1 | A credit note received through this connection must reference an original invoice that already exists in APEX, using that invoice's reference number. | A credit note is rejected if its referenced original invoice reference number does not match any invoice already registered in the business's APEX account. |
| FR-9.2 | A credit note cannot be registered without its original invoice already present in APEX. | There is no path for a credit note received through this connection to be accepted if its original invoice cannot be found. |
| FR-9.3 | A business uses the same access granted for invoice import (Document 8\) to also send credit notes \- no separate request or approval is required. | A business with live invoice API access can send credit notes through the same connection without going through a separate access request. |
| FR-9.4 | A successfully received credit note is registered with Cleared status. | After being received and accepted, the credit note's status reads Cleared. |
| FR-9.5 | A successfully received credit note automatically recalculates the outstanding balance of its original invoice. | After the credit note is registered, the original invoice's displayed outstanding balance reflects the credited amount without further action by the business. |
| FR-9.6 | A credit note that fails validation is not registered, and the business's own system receives an indication that it failed and why. | The business's connected system receives a response indicating rejection and the specific reason, rather than no response or a silent failure. |
| FR-9.7 | A successfully received credit note is automatically linked to its original invoice. | Viewing the original invoice shows the received credit note linked to it, and viewing the credit note shows a link back to the original invoice. |

## 

## **Story Pack**

## **CN-9-US01 \- Use Existing Invoice API Access for Credit Notes**

**User Story**  
As a Business with live invoice API access, I want to send credit notes through the same connection so that I do not need a separate integration or approval process.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* No separate credit note API access request is required.  
* No additional approval step is required after live invoice API access is granted.  
* Credit notes use the same Business connection and access state as invoices.  
* A Business without live invoice API access cannot register live credit notes through the connection.  
* Credit note access is revoked or restricted when the associated invoice API access is revoked or restricted.  
* Test access can validate credit note data without creating live credit notes.

---

## **CN-9-US02 \- Validate the Original Invoice for an API Credit Note**

**User Story**  
As a connected Business System, I want each credit note matched to an invoice already in APEX so that a credit note cannot be registered without its original invoice.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Every credit note must contain the original invoice reference number.  
* The original invoice must already exist in the Current Business's APEX records.  
* The invoice may have originated from manual creation, file import, or the direct connection.  
* A credit note is rejected when the referenced invoice cannot be found.  
* A cross-Business invoice reference is not accepted.  
* A credit note is not registered ahead of an invoice that has not yet completed registration.  
* The credit note is linked to exactly one matching original invoice.

---

## **CN-9-US03 \- Reject Invalid API Credit Notes Clearly**

**User Story**  
As a connected Business System, I want a clear rejection response for invalid credit notes so that I can correct and resend them.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Required credit note fields must be present.  
* The credit note's own reference number must be present and unique within the Business.  
* The original invoice must be found before the credit note is accepted.  
* An invalid credit note is not registered.  
* The response states that the credit note was rejected.  
* The response includes the specific validation reason.  
* The failure is not silent and does not change the original invoice balance or payment status.  
* Corrected data can be sent again safely.

---

## **CN-9-US04 \- Register and Apply an API Credit Note**

**User Story**  
As a connected Business System, I want a valid external credit note registered and applied so that the original invoice reflects the externally issued correction.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A valid credit note is registered with lifecycle status `Cleared`.  
* The external credit note reference and supplied legal data are preserved.  
* The credit note is linked automatically to its original invoice.  
* The original invoice detail links to the credit note.  
* The credit note detail links back to the original invoice.  
* The original invoice outstanding balance is recalculated automatically.  
* The updated balance requires no additional Business User action.  
* Repeating the same accepted credit note request does not register or apply it more than once.

# 10 \- Invoice List View

**Invoice List View**

| Related documents: Document 5 (Invoice Creation \- Submission & ZATCA Clearance) \- status labels used here. Document 11 (Invoice Detail View & Status Lifecycle), Document 13 (Credit Note Submission & Lifecycle) \- credit note indicator. Document 14 (Credit Note List View). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes the screen a business lands on to view, search, filter, and act on their invoices. Every invoice, regardless of which of the three channels brought it into APEX \- created manually, imported through file upload, or imported through a direct system connection \- appears together in this single list.

# **Columns**

| Column | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Invoice reference number | The invoice's official reference number. Selecting it opens the invoice detail view (Document 11). |
| Date | The invoice date. |
| Due date | Shown in red with a warning indicator if the invoice is overdue \- meaning it is Cleared, not yet fully paid, and the due date has passed. |
| Business Partner | The trading partner the invoice was issued to. |
| Channel | A small icon showing how the invoice entered APEX \- created manually, file import, or API. |
| Amount | The invoice total, including VAT, in Saudi Riyals. |
| Status | The invoice's lifecycle status \- Draft, Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, Rejected, Importing, or Import Failed. |
| Payment status | Unpaid, Partially Paid, or Paid. Only shown once implemented and an invoice is Cleared \- blank for any other status. |
| Credit note | An icon shown only if a credit note exists against this invoice. Selecting it goes to that credit note. Blank if none exists. |

# **Search**

Search covers the invoice reference number and the Trading Partner name. 

# **Default sort order**

Invoices are sorted by invoice date, most recent first. A business user can re-sort by selecting any column heading \- date, due date, or amount.

# **Filters**

A business can filter the list to one of the following at a time:

| All  ·  Draft  ·  Sent to ZATCA  ·  Cleared  ·  Rejected  ·  Import Failed  ·  Unpaid  ·  Partially Paid  ·  Paid  ·  Overdue |
| :---- |

These same labels are used consistently across the invoice detail view and anywhere else invoice status is shown.

# **Actions available directly from the list**

A business can act on an individual invoice directly from the list, without opening it, depending on its status:

| Status | Available actions |
| :---- | :---- |
| Draft | Edit, Delete. |
| Sent to ZATCA | None. |
| Cleared | Download, Issue credit note. Later record a payment.  |
| Rejected | None \- a new invoice is created separately. |
| Import Failed | None \- the business corrects the source file or system data and re-imports. |

There are no actions that can be applied to multiple invoices at once on this screen.

# **Empty states**

* No invoices at all: the business is shown a prompt to create their first invoice, or to import invoices, covering all three channels.

* A filter is applied with no matching invoices: a message indicates no matches were found, with an option to clear the filter.

* A search returns no matching invoices: a message indicates no matches were found for the search term, with an option to clear the search.

# **Not shown on this screen**

Financing status is not shown on the invoice list for now. This is covered later separately in the financing module. Recording a payment is also not an action available from this screen \- it will be covered in the payment module later.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-10.1 | Every invoice, regardless of which of the three channels created it, appears in this single list. | An invoice created manually, an invoice imported by file, and an invoice imported through a direct connection are all visible together in the same list. |
| FR-10.2 | Each row displays a channel indicator showing how that invoice entered APEX. | A business user can visually distinguish a manually created invoice from a file-imported one and from one received through a direct connection, without opening the invoice. |
| FR-10.3 | Search matches against invoice reference number and buyer name. | Entering a search term returns invoices where the term appears in either field. |
| FR-10.4 | The list is sorted by invoice date, most recent first, by default. | On first load, the most recently dated invoice appears at the top of the list. |
| FR-10.5 | A business can re-sort the list by date, due date, or amount. | Selecting any of these column headings reorders the list accordingly. |
| FR-10.6 | A business can filter the list to exactly one of the defined filter values at a time. | Selecting a filter shows only invoices matching that single status or payment state. |
| FR-10.7 | Payment status is only displayed for invoices with a Cleared lifecycle status. | An invoice in Draft, Sent to ZATCA, Rejected, or Import Failed status shows no payment status value. |
| FR-10.8 | An overdue invoice's due date is visually highlighted on the list without requiring the business user to apply a filter. | An invoice that is Cleared, not fully paid, and past its due date shows its due date in red with a warning indicator, visible in the default unfiltered list. |
| FR-10.9 | A credit note indicator is shown only on invoices that have at least one credit note issued against them. | An invoice with no credit notes shows a blank credit note column. An invoice with one or more credit notes shows an indicator that links to the related credit note(s). |
| FR-10.10 | Row-level actions shown match exactly the action set defined for that invoice's status. | A Draft invoice's row offers only Edit and Delete. A Cleared invoice's row offers only Download and Issue credit note. No other action appears for either. |
| FR-10.11 | An empty invoice list, a filtered list with no results, and a search with no results each display a distinct, clear message. | Each of these three scenarios shows wording specific to that scenario, not a single generic empty message. |

**Story Pack**

## **INV-10-US01 \- View the Unified Invoice List**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to view all Business invoices in one list so that I can review invoices regardless of how they entered APEX.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Manually created, file-imported, and API-imported invoices appear in the same list.  
* Each row displays invoice reference number, invoice date, due date, Business Partner, channel, amount, lifecycle status, payment status when applicable, and credit note indicator when applicable.  
* Selecting the invoice reference opens the Invoice detail view.  
* Amount is displayed as the invoice total including VAT in Saudi Riyals.  
* Channel visually distinguishes manual creation, file import, and direct system connection.  
* Lifecycle status can display Draft, Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, Rejected, Importing, or Import Failed as applicable.  
* Only invoices belonging to the Current Business are shown.

---

## **INV-10-US02 \- Search Invoices**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to search invoices so that I can find a document by reference number or buyer.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Search matches invoice reference number.  
* Search matches Trading Partner or buyer name.  
* A matching invoice is returned when the term appears in either supported field.  
* Search includes invoices from all origin channels and lifecycle statuses.  
* A no-results message identifies that no invoices match the search term.  
* The user can clear the search and return to the unsearched list.

---

## **INV-10-US03 \- Sort Invoices**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to sort invoices so that I can review them in the order most useful to me.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The default sort is invoice date, most recent first.  
* The user can sort by invoice date.  
* The user can sort by due date.  
* The user can sort by amount.  
* Selecting a supported column heading changes the order accordingly.  
* Sorting preserves the current search and filter where applicable.  
* Equal values use a stable deterministic secondary order.

---

## **INV-10-US04 \- Filter Invoices**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to filter invoices by one defined state at a time so that I can focus on the invoices requiring attention.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The available filters are All, Draft, Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, Rejected, Import Failed, Unpaid, Partially Paid, Paid, and Overdue.  
* Only one filter can be active at a time.  
* A lifecycle filter returns invoices with that lifecycle status.  
* A payment filter returns eligible Cleared invoices with that payment state.  
* Overdue returns Cleared invoices that are not Paid and whose due date has passed.  
* The user can clear the active filter.  
* A filter with no matches displays a filter-specific no-results message.

---

## **INV-10-US05 \- Display Payment and Overdue Information**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want payment and overdue information shown on eligible invoices so that I can identify unpaid obligations quickly.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Payment status is shown only when the invoice lifecycle status is Cleared.  
* Supported payment values are Unpaid, Partially Paid, and Paid.  
* Draft, Sent to ZATCA, Rejected, Importing, and Import Failed invoices show no payment status.  
* An invoice is visually overdue when it is Cleared, not fully Paid, and its due date has passed.  
* The overdue due date is shown in red with a warning indicator in the default list.  
* Overdue is derived automatically and is not stored as a manually selected lifecycle status.  
* A fully Paid invoice is not shown as overdue.

---

## **INV-10-US06 \- Navigate to Related Credit Notes**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want an indicator on invoices with credit notes so that I can open the related corrections directly.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The credit note column is blank when an invoice has no related credit notes.  
* An indicator is shown when an invoice has one or more related credit notes.  
* Selecting the indicator opens the Credit Note list filtered to that invoice.  
* The filtered list includes all credit notes related to the selected invoice.  
* The indicator updates when the first credit note becomes related to the invoice.  
* A failed or unregistered credit note does not create a false related-credit indicator.

---

## **INV-10-US07 \- Use Status-Specific Invoice Row Actions**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want row actions limited by invoice status so that I only see actions that are legally and operationally valid.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Draft rows offer Edit and Delete only.  
* Sent to ZATCA rows offer no action.  
* Cleared rows offer Download and Issue Credit Note only within this PRD's scope.  
* Rejected rows offer no action.  
* Importing rows offer no action.  
* Import Failed rows offer no action; source data must be corrected and imported again.  
* Recording a payment and financing actions are not introduced by this list PRD.  
* No action can be applied to multiple invoices at once.  
* Direct requests cannot perform an action that is hidden for the current status.

---

## **INV-10-US08 \- View Invoice List Empty States**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want clear invoice-list empty states so that I know how to proceed when no records are visible.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A Business with no invoices sees a prompt to create or import its first invoices.  
* The initial empty state covers manual creation, file import, and direct connection options.  
* A filter with no matches shows a message specific to the selected filter.  
* A search with no matches shows a message specific to the search term.  
* Filter and search no-results states provide a way to clear the active condition.  
* The initial empty state is not shown when invoices exist but are hidden by search or filter.

---

# 11 \- Invoice Detail View & Status Lifecycle

**Invoice Detail View & Status Lifecycle**

| Related documents: This document is the single source of truth for invoice status and the full action matrix across all channels. Document 4 (Invoice Creation \- Draft), Document 5 (Invoice Creation \- Submission & ZATCA Clearance), Document 6 and Document 8 (Import \- Invoices), Document 10 (Invoice List View), Document 12 and Document 13 (Credit Notes). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes what a business sees when they open a single invoice, regardless of which of the three channels brought that invoice into APEX, and brings together every status an invoice can carry and every action available at each one. Where this document and any other document in this set differ on a status or action, this document is the authoritative source.

# **What appears on every invoice, regardless of channel**

The invoice detail view shows the complete invoice \- selling business details, buying business details, dates, line items, discounts, the VAT breakdown, the summary totals, and notes \- exactly as described in Document 4 for manually created invoices, and as received for imported invoices. Alongside this, the detail view shows:

* The invoice's current lifecycle status.

* The invoice's current payment status, once Cleared.

* Which channel brought the invoice into APEX \- created manually, file import, or direct system connection.

* A link to any credit note issued against this invoice, if one exists.

* A full history of what has happened to this invoice \- when it was created, submitted, cleared or rejected, and by whom, where applicable.

# **The three things tracked on every invoice**

Every invoice carries three separate pieces of status, tracked independently:

| Status type | What it tracks | Where it's covered |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Lifecycle status | Where the invoice is in being created or imported and cleared by ZATCA. | Fully defined in this document. |
| Payment status | Whether the buying business has paid. | Fully defined in this document. Payment recording itself is a separate module. |
| Financing status | Whether the invoice has been put forward for financing. | Out of scope \- covered in the financing module. |

# **Lifecycle statuses \- full definition**

| Status | Meaning | Applies to |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Draft | Being built inside APEX. Not yet submitted to ZATCA. No legal standing. | Manually created invoices only. |
| Sent to ZATCA | Submitted. Identifiers locked. Awaiting a response from ZATCA. | Manually created invoices only. |
| Cleared | Accepted by ZATCA, or already cleared externally and successfully registered in APEX. Final and legally valid. Can never be edited or deleted. | All three channels. |
| Rejected | Not accepted by ZATCA. Permanent record. Identifiers can never be reused. No resubmission \- a new invoice must be created. | Manually created invoices only. |
| Importing | APEX is in the process of registering an invoice received through file import or direct system connection. | Imported invoices only (file or direct connection). |
| Import Failed | APEX could not register the invoice \- a required field was missing, the buyer could not be matched, or another validation rule failed. | Imported invoices only (file or direct connection). |

# **Payment statuses \- full definition**

| Status | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| Unpaid | No payment has been recorded against this invoice. |
| Partially Paid | Some, but not all, of the invoice total has been paid. |
| Paid | The full invoice total has been paid. |
| Overdue | Not a separate stored status \- shown automatically whenever an invoice is Cleared, not yet Paid, and its due date has passed. |

* Payment status is only ever shown once an invoice is Cleared. It has no meaning before that.

* Payment status is always calculated from recorded payments. 

* If a credit note is cleared against an invoice, that invoice's payment status is automatically recalculated to reflect the new, reduced amount owed.

# **Full action matrix \- every status, every available action**

| Status | Available actions |
| :---- | :---- |
| Draft | Edit, Delete, Submit for ZATCA clearance. |
| Sent to ZATCA | None \- view only. |
| Cleared | Download the invoice document, Issue a credit note. (Recording a payment and requesting financing are available here too, but are defined in their own separate modules later, not in this document.) |
| Rejected | None \- view only. A new invoice is created separately. |
| Importing | None \- view only, transient state. |
| Import Failed | None \- view only. The business corrects the source data and re-imports. |

# **What is never possible, on any invoice, at any status**

* Editing a Cleared invoice.

* Deleting a Cleared, Sent to ZATCA, Rejected, or Import Failed invoice.

* Voiding or cancelling an invoice outright. The only correction mechanism for a Cleared invoice is a credit note.

* Reverting a Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, or Rejected invoice back to Draft.

* Resubmitting a Rejected invoice \- a new invoice must always be created instead.

# **Record keeping**

Every invoice, regardless of its final status, is retained permanently once it leaves Draft. This includes Rejected and Import Failed invoices. No business user, regardless of permissions, can permanently delete an invoice once it has left Draft status. This reflects the Saudi requirement to retain invoice records for a minimum of six years.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-11.1 | The invoice detail view displays lifecycle status, payment status (when applicable), originating channel, and a link to any related credit note. | Opening any invoice, regardless of channel, shows all four of these elements in the detail view. |
| FR-11.2 | The invoice detail view shows a complete history of status changes for that invoice, including timestamps. | A business user can view when the invoice was created, submitted, and cleared or rejected, in chronological order. |
| FR-11.3 | Payment status is displayed only when lifecycle status is Cleared. | An invoice in any lifecycle status other than Cleared shows no payment status value on its detail view. |
| FR-11.4 | Payment status can be manually set or derived from recorded payments. | Input control for payment status exists on the invoice detail view. |
| FR-11.5 | When a credit note clears against an invoice, that invoice's payment status is automatically recalculated. | After a related credit note reaches Cleared status, the original invoice's payment status reflects the reduced amount owed without manual action. |
| FR-11.6 | An invoice displays Overdue automatically when it is Cleared, not Paid, and its due date has passed \- without this being a status the business user sets. | An eligible invoice shows an Overdue indicator the day after its due date passes, with no manual action taken by anyone. |
| FR-11.7 | The available actions shown on an invoice detail view exactly match the action matrix defined in this document for that invoice's current status. | A Draft invoice's detail view offers Edit, Delete, and Submit only. A Cleared invoice's detail view offers Download and Issue credit note, with no edit or delete option present anywhere on the screen. |
| FR-11.8 | There is no edit option available on any invoice with lifecycle status Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, Rejected, Importing, or Import Failed. | Attempting to access an edit function on an invoice in any of these statuses is not possible through any control on the screen. |
| FR-11.9 | There is no delete option available on any invoice with lifecycle status Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, Rejected, Importing, or Import Failed. | Attempting to access a delete function on an invoice in any of these statuses is not possible through any control on the screen. |
| FR-11.10 | There is no void, cancel, or revert-to-draft action available on any invoice at any status. | No control with this function exists anywhere in the invoice detail view, regardless of status. |
| FR-11.11 | A Rejected invoice has no resubmit action; only the option to create a new, separate invoice is available elsewhere in APEX. | No resubmit control exists on a Rejected invoice's detail view. |
| FR-11.12 | An invoice is never permanently deleted once it has left Draft status, regardless of its final outcome. | A Rejected or Import Failed invoice remains permanently accessible and is never removed from the business's records. |

**Story Pack**

## 

## **INV-11-US01 \- View Complete Invoice Details Across All Channels**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to open any invoice in a consistent detail view so that I can review the complete legal and commercial record.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The detail view supports manually created, file-imported, and API-imported invoices.  
* It displays selling Business details and buying Business details.  
* It displays invoice and due dates, line items, discounts, VAT breakdown, summary totals, and notes.  
* Manually created invoice values are shown as finally saved and cleared.  
* Imported invoice values are shown as received and registered.  
* It displays the current lifecycle status.  
* It displays payment status when applicable.  
* It displays the originating channel.  
* It displays a link to related credit notes when any exist.  
* The detail view is scoped to the Current Business.

---

## **INV-11-US02 \- Track the Invoice Lifecycle by Origin**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want invoice lifecycle statuses applied consistently so that I understand the state of any invoice regardless of origin.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Draft applies only to manually created invoices being built in APEX.  
* Sent to ZATCA applies only to submitted manually created invoices awaiting ZATCA.  
* Cleared applies to all channels after ZATCA acceptance or successful registration of an externally cleared invoice.  
* Rejected applies to manually created invoices rejected by ZATCA.  
* Importing applies only while a file or API invoice is being registered.  
* Import Failed applies only when an imported invoice cannot be registered.  
* A Cleared invoice is final and cannot be edited or deleted.  
* Status labels are consistent in list, detail, filters, and related navigation.  
* A status transition cannot move a submitted or final invoice back to Draft.

---

## **INV-11-US03 \- View Invoice Status History**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to view an invoice's chronological history so that I can trace how and when its status changed.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The detail view shows when the invoice record was created or first received.  
* For manually created invoices, it shows when the invoice was submitted.  
* It shows when the invoice was Cleared, Rejected, or failed import as applicable.  
* Every history entry includes a timestamp.  
* The responsible actor is shown where the action was performed by a Business User and actor data is applicable.  
* System-originated transitions are distinguishable from user actions.  
* History entries are ordered chronologically.  
* Repeated processing of the same event does not create duplicate history entries.

---

## **INV-11-US04 \- Display and Maintain Payment Status**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want payment status shown on Cleared invoices so that I can understand whether the buyer's obligation is unpaid, partially paid, or paid.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Payment status is displayed only when lifecycle status is Cleared.  
* Supported values are Unpaid, Partially Paid, and Paid.  
* Payment status can be manually set from the Invoice detail view or derived from recorded payments, as stated in this PRD.  
* When payment records are available, the displayed status reflects the recorded amounts.  
* Payment status is not displayed for Draft, Sent to ZATCA, Rejected, Importing, or Import Failed invoices.  
* Overdue is shown automatically when the invoice is Cleared, not Paid, and the due date has passed.  
* Overdue appears from the day after the due date without manual action.  
* Overdue is an indicator, not a separately stored payment or lifecycle status.

---

## **INV-11-US05 \- Recalculate Invoice Status After a Credit Note**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want a Cleared credit note reflected on the original invoice so that its balance and payment state remain accurate.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The invoice detail view links to each related registered credit note.  
* When a related credit note becomes Cleared, the outstanding balance is reduced by the credited amount.  
* The invoice payment status is recalculated against the reduced amount owed.  
* A rejected credit note does not change the invoice balance or payment status.  
* The recalculation occurs automatically without a manual refresh action beyond normal view loading.  
* A repeated clearance event for the same credit note does not reduce the balance twice.  
* The invoice history records the credit-note effect where applicable.

---

## **INV-11-US06 \- Enforce the Invoice Detail Action Matrix**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want available actions to match the invoice lifecycle so that I cannot perform an invalid operation.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Draft offers Edit, Delete, and Submit for ZATCA clearance.  
* Sent to ZATCA is view-only.  
* Cleared offers Download and Issue Credit Note within this PRD's scope.  
* Rejected is view-only and requires a separate new invoice when needed.  
* Importing is view-only.  
* Import Failed is view-only and requires corrected source data to be imported again.  
* No edit option is available for Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, Rejected, Importing, or Import Failed.  
* No delete option is available for Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, Rejected, Importing, or Import Failed.  
* Action restrictions are enforced beyond the visible controls.

---

## **INV-11-US07 \- Prevent Invalid Invoice Reversal and Preserve Records**

**User Story**  
As a Business, I want non-Draft invoices preserved and irreversible so that legal records and identifiers remain trustworthy.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* No invoice can be voided or cancelled outright.  
* No Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, or Rejected invoice can be reverted to Draft.  
* A Rejected invoice has no resubmit action.  
* A Cleared invoice can only be corrected through a credit note.  
* An invoice that has left Draft is never permanently deleted by a Business User.  
* Rejected and Import Failed invoices remain accessible indefinitely as Business records.  
* No permission level available to a Business User bypasses these restrictions.  
* The same restrictions apply whether the operation is attempted from the UI or directly through an application endpoint.

# 12 \- Credit Note Creation

**Credit Note Creation**

| Related documents: Document 11 (Invoice Detail View & Status Lifecycle) \- a credit note can only be created against a Cleared invoice. Document 13 (Credit Note Submission & Lifecycle), Document 14 (Credit Note List View). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes how a business corrects or reverses part or all of a Cleared invoice by issuing a credit note. A credit note is the only way to correct a Cleared invoice \- a Cleared invoice itself can never be edited or deleted.

# **When a credit note is used**

A business issues a credit note when something about an already-Cleared invoice needs to change \- for example, goods were returned, a price was incorrect, part or all of the supply was cancelled, or the supply itself changed. A credit note always corrects exactly one original invoice.

# **Starting a credit note**

A business starts a credit note from the Cleared invoice it relates to. There is no way to start a credit note independently of an invoice \- the originating invoice must be selected first, and it must already be Cleared.

# **Reason**

Every credit note must have a reason, selected from a fixed list. This is not a free-text field.

| Cancellation of the invoice or part of the invoice |
| :---- |
| Discount or reduction of price after supply |
| Return of goods |
| Correction of an error in the original invoice |
| Change in supply |

# **What is inherited automatically from the original invoice**

* Selling business details

* Buying business details

* The original invoice's reference number and identifiers, shown on the credit note as a reference.

* The original invoice's line items, presented for the business user to select from.

None of these can be changed by the business user on the credit note. A credit note always addresses the same buying business as its original invoice.

# **What the business specifies**

* Which original line items are being credited, and at what quantity or value. A business does not need to credit every line, or the full quantity on a line \- partial credit notes are fully supported.

* A discount adjustment, if the credit relates to a discount.

* VAT treatment per credited line \- inherited from the original line by default, but can be changed if the reason for the credit requires it.

* The reason, selected from the fixed list above.

* Optional notes.

# **What a credit note cannot do**

* It cannot introduce a new line item that was not on the original invoice.

* It cannot change who the credit note is addressed to.

* It cannot set a due date \- a credit note reduces an existing obligation, it does not create a new one.

* It cannot select line items from the catalog \- only from the original invoice's own lines.

# **How much can be credited**

A business can credit any amount up to the full original invoice total, regardless of how much of that invoice has already been paid. A credit note corrects the underlying commercial transaction, not the current payment position. If a credit note would result in the selling business owing the buying business money \- for example because the buying business already paid in full before the credit note is issued \- that refund is handled outside of APEX.

# **Partial and full credit notes**

A partial credit note credits some, but not all, of the original invoice's value. A full credit note credits the entire original invoice. Both are built the same way \- a full credit note is simply a partial credit note where every original line is credited in full.

# **Identifiers**

A credit note receives its own reference number, separate from but related to the invoice numbering described in Document 5\. Credit note reference numbers use a distinct prefix so they are immediately recognizable as credit notes, while still continuing the same underlying sequence as the business's invoices, to preserve an unbroken numbering chain.

# **Timing**

A credit note should be issued within 15 calendar days from the end of the month in which the adjustment being corrected occurred, in line with Saudi tax regulation. If a business user attempts to create a credit note outside this window, APEX shows a clear warning explaining the regulatory timing requirement, but does not block the business user from proceeding \- responsibility for timely issuance rests with the business.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-12.1 | A credit note can only be started from a Cleared invoice. | There is no option to start a credit note from an invoice in any status other than Cleared, and no option to create a credit note without first selecting an originating invoice. |
| FR-12.2 | A reason is required on every credit note and must be one of the five defined values according to Zatca. | Saving or submitting a credit note is blocked if no reason is selected, and only the five defined reasons are selectable. |
| FR-12.3 | Selling and buying business details on a credit note are inherited automatically from the original invoice and cannot be edited. | No input control exists for changing the selling or buying business details on a credit note. |
| FR-12.4 | Line items available to credit are limited to the lines that exist on the original invoice. | The line item selection on a credit note only offers items that appear on the original invoice; no catalog picker or free-text line entry is available. |
| FR-12.5 | A business can credit any subset of original invoice lines, at any quantity up to the original quantity. | A credit note can be created referencing only one of several original lines, and at a partial quantity of that line. |
| FR-12.6 | A credit note has no due date field. | No due date input exists anywhere on the credit note creation screen. |
| FR-12.7 | The total amount credited across a credit note cannot exceed the original invoice's total. | Attempting to credit an amount greater than the original invoice total is blocked with a clear message. |
| FR-12.8 | Credit notes can be created for a partial amount or the full original invoice amount. | A business user can successfully create a credit note crediting only some original lines, or all original lines in full. |
| FR-12.9 | A credit note's reference number uses a distinct prefix from regular invoices, while continuing the same overall sequence. | A newly created credit note's reference number is visually distinguishable from an invoice reference number, and its underlying sequence position continues from the business's most recent document. |
| FR-12.10 | Attempting to create a credit note more than 15 calendar days after the end of the month in which the adjustment occurred shows a warning but does not block creation. | A credit note created outside this window displays a clear warning message and can still be saved and submitted by the business user. |

**Story Pack**

## **CN-12-US01 \- Start a Credit Note from a Cleared Invoice**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to start a credit note from a Cleared invoice so that I can correct that specific legal invoice.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The credit note flow can only be started from an invoice with lifecycle status `Cleared`.  
* No credit note creation action is available from Draft, Sent to ZATCA, Rejected, Importing, or Import Failed invoices.  
* A credit note cannot be created independently without selecting an original invoice.  
* Each credit note is associated with exactly one original invoice.  
* Starting the flow creates a Draft credit note that can be saved, edited, deleted, or submitted while it remains Draft.  
* The original invoice remains unchanged while the credit note is Draft.  
* Starting the flow more than once creates separate Drafts only when the user explicitly starts separate credit notes.

---

## **CN-12-US02 \- Select a Required Credit Note Reason**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to select a standard reason for the credit note so that the correction uses an approved ZATCA reason.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A reason is required before the credit note can be saved or submitted.  
* The reason is selected from a fixed list and is not free text.  
* The selectable reasons are:  
  * Cancellation of the invoice or part of the invoice  
  * Discount or reduction of price after supply  
  * Return of goods  
  * Correction of an error in the original invoice  
  * Change in supply  
* No additional reason value can be entered by the user.  
* A missing reason blocks saving and submission with a clear validation message.  
* The selected reason is shown on the Credit Note detail view and document.

---

## **CN-12-US03 \- Inherit Original Invoice Information**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want the credit note to inherit immutable information from the original invoice so that it always corrects the same transaction and buyer.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Selling Business details are copied from the original invoice.  
* Buying Business details are copied from the original invoice.  
* Selling and buying Business details are read-only on the credit note.  
* The original invoice reference number and identifiers are displayed as the credit note's source reference.  
* The original invoice's line items are presented as the only lines available to credit.  
* The user cannot change the Trading Partner addressed by the credit note.  
* The user cannot select lines from the Catalogue.  
* The user cannot add a free-text or new line that did not exist on the original invoice.

---

## **CN-12-US04 \- Create a Partial or Full Credit Note**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to credit selected invoice lines partially or fully so that the correction matches the actual commercial adjustment.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The user can select any subset of lines from the original invoice.  
* The user can credit a partial quantity of an original line.  
* The credited quantity cannot exceed the original quantity of that line within this credit note.  
* The user can credit a specific value when the product-defined line supports value-based crediting.  
* A partial credit note may contain only some lines or part of a line.  
* A full credit note may credit every original line in full.  
* Both partial and full credit notes use the same creation flow.  
* Unselected original lines remain unaffected.

---

## **CN-12-US05 \- Adjust Credit Values and Calculate Totals**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to adjust permitted credit values and see automatic calculations so that the credit note accurately represents the correction.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* The user can enter a discount adjustment when the credit relates to a discount.  
* VAT Treatment defaults from each original invoice line.  
* VAT Treatment can be changed for a credited line when the correction reason requires it.  
* Credit note taxable amounts and VAT are recalculated from the credited lines and adjustments.  
* The credit note displays subtotal, VAT breakdown, total VAT, and total credited.  
* Optional notes can be added and saved.  
* The calculation is repeatable for the same entered values.  
* Adjusting the credit note does not alter the original invoice while the credit note is Draft.

---

## **CN-12-US06 \- Enforce Credit Note Amount and Field Restrictions**

**User Story**  
As a Business, I want credit note limits enforced so that a correction cannot introduce a new obligation or exceed the original invoice.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A credit note has no due date field.  
* A credit note has no separate buyer selection.  
* A credit note cannot add new Catalogue or free-text lines.  
* The credit note total cannot exceed the original invoice total.  
* An attempt to exceed the original invoice total is blocked with a clear validation message.  
* The Business may create a credit note up to the original invoice total regardless of how much has already been paid.  
* The credit note corrects the commercial transaction, not the recorded payment itself.  
* Any refund owed because the invoice was already paid is handled outside APEX.

---

## **CN-12-US07 \- Use Credit Note Numbering**

**User Story**  
As a Business, I want credit notes to use a distinct but continuous document sequence so that they are recognisable without breaking the Business's numbering chain.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* A credit note receives its own reference number separate from the original invoice reference.  
* The credit note reference uses a prefix distinct from the invoice prefix.  
* The prefix makes the document visually recognisable as a credit note.  
* The credit note continues the Business's overall underlying document sequence.  
* The reference is assigned automatically at submission, not typed by the user.  
* Concurrent invoice and credit note submissions cannot reuse the same sequence position.  
* Once assigned, a credit note reference cannot be edited or reused.

---

## **CN-12-US08 \- Warn About Late Credit Note Issuance**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want a warning when a credit note may be issued late so that I understand the Saudi regulatory timing requirement before proceeding.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* APEX evaluates whether creation occurs more than 15 calendar days after the end of the month in which the corrected adjustment occurred.  
* When outside that window, a clear regulatory timing warning is displayed.  
* The warning explains that the credit note should be issued within the stated window.  
* The warning does not block saving or submission.  
* The user can proceed after seeing the warning.  
* The warning is not shown when the credit note is within the window.  
* Displaying or acknowledging the warning does not alter the original invoice.

---

# 13 \- Credit Note Submission & Lifecycle

**Credit Note Submission & Lifecycle**

| Related documents: Document 12 (Credit Note Creation), Document 11 (Invoice Detail View & Status Lifecycle) \- payment status recalculation on the original invoice. Document 14 (Credit Note List View). |
| :---- |

# **Purpose**

This document describes what happens when a business submits a credit note \- from the moment they confirm submission through to the credit note being cleared by ZATCA or rejected, and what that means for the original invoice it corrects.

# **Submission is a single action, same as an invoice**

A business submits a credit note for clearance with one action. The moment a business user submits, the credit note's identifiers are locked and it is sent to ZATCA for clearance, together, as one step. This follows exactly the same pattern as invoice submission, described in Document 5\.

# **What locks at submission**

* The credit note's date locks to the actual date of submission.

* The credit note's own reference number is assigned, using the distinct prefix described in Document 12, continuing the business's overall document sequence.

* Every credited line, amount, and detail on the credit note is locked. No further editing is possible from this point forward.

# **Awaiting clearance**

After submission, the credit note shows the status Sent to ZATCA, the same status label used for invoices. It remains in this status for as long as it takes ZATCA to respond, with no automatic escalation, exactly as described for invoices in Document 5\.

# **Outcome: Cleared**

If ZATCA accepts the credit note, it becomes Cleared and is now legally effective. From this point, the credit note itself can never be edited or deleted.

Once Cleared, two things happen automatically on the original invoice:

* The original invoice's outstanding balance is recalculated to reflect the credited amount.

* The original invoice's payment status is recalculated based on the new balance. For example, an invoice that was Partially Paid may become fully accounted for if the credit note covers the remaining unpaid amount.

The business user does not need to take any further action for these updates to happen.

# **Outcome: Rejected**

If ZATCA rejects the credit note, it becomes Rejected. As with invoices, its identifiers can never be reused, it is never deleted, and there is no resubmit action \- a business user creates a new credit note from the original invoice if the correction is still needed.

The original invoice is entirely unaffected by a Rejected credit note. Its balance and payment status remain exactly as they were before the credit note was attempted.

# **If submission cannot be completed**

As with invoices, if APEX cannot confirm whether ZATCA received the submission, the credit note remains in Sent to ZATCA. It does not revert to Draft, since its identifiers are already locked.

# **Status labels**

Credit notes use the same status labels as invoices, applied consistently:

| Label shown to business user | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| Draft | Being built. Not yet submitted. Covered in Document 12\. |
| Sent to ZATCA | Submitted. Awaiting a response from ZATCA. |
| Cleared | Accepted by ZATCA. Final, legally effective, cannot be changed. Original invoice automatically updated. |
| Rejected | Not accepted by ZATCA. Permanent record, cannot be resubmitted. Original invoice unaffected. |

# **What a business user can do at each status**

| Status | Available actions |
| :---- | :---- |
| Draft | Edit, delete, submit for clearance. |
| Sent to ZATCA | View only. |
| Cleared | Download the credit note document. |
| Rejected | View only. A new credit note is created separately, from the original invoice, if still needed. |

A credit note does not generate any of its own payment or financing actions. It is not a financing instrument and never has its own due date or payment record.

# **There is no import path for credit notes created this way**

This document covers only credit notes created directly inside APEX against a Cleared invoice. Credit notes that already existed against imported invoices, brought in from another system, are covered separately in Document 7 (file import) and Document 9 (direct connection).

# **Record keeping**

Every credit note, regardless of outcome, is retained permanently and is never deleted once it leaves Draft status. This includes Rejected credit notes, in line with the same six-year retention requirement that applies to invoices.

# **Functional Requirements**

Each requirement below is independently testable and maps to a single piece of buildable work.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-13.1 | Submitting a Draft credit note locks its identifiers and sends it for ZATCA clearance as one single action. | There is no intermediate state visible to the business user where identifiers are locked but the credit note has not yet been sent to ZATCA. |
| FR-13.2 | The credit note's reference number is assigned automatically at submission, using the distinct credit note prefix and continuing the business's overall document sequence. | The assigned reference number uses the credit note prefix and is not editable by the business user. |
| FR-13.3 | Once submitted, no field on the credit note can be edited by any business user, regardless of outcome. | No edit control is available on a credit note in Sent to ZATCA, Cleared, or Rejected status. |
| FR-13.4 | When a credit note reaches Cleared status, the original invoice's outstanding balance is automatically recalculated. | Viewing the original invoice immediately after the credit note clears shows an outstanding balance reduced by the credited amount, with no manual action taken. |
| FR-13.5 | When a credit note reaches Cleared status, the original invoice's payment status is automatically recalculated based on the new balance. | An invoice whose remaining unpaid balance is fully covered by a cleared credit note shows an updated payment status reflecting that, without manual action. |
| FR-13.6 | When a credit note is Rejected, the original invoice's balance and payment status remain completely unchanged. | After a credit note is rejected, the original invoice's outstanding balance and payment status are identical to their values before the credit note was created. |
| FR-13.7 | A Rejected credit note is retained permanently and is never deleted. | A Rejected credit note remains visible in the business's records indefinitely. |
| FR-13.8 | There is no resubmit action on a Rejected credit note. | No submit or resubmit control is available on a credit note in Rejected status. |
| FR-13.9 | If APEX cannot confirm ZATCA's response due to a connectivity issue, the credit note remains in Sent to ZATCA rather than reverting to Draft. | A credit note that has been submitted never returns to Draft status under any circumstance. |
| FR-13.10 | A Cleared credit note can be downloaded by the business user as a document. | A download control is available on a Cleared credit note and produces the credit note document. |

## **Story Pack**

## **CN-13-US01 \- Submit and Lock a Draft Credit Note**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want to submit a completed Draft credit note once so that its identifiers are locked and it is sent to ZATCA for clearance as one action.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Submission is available only for a Draft credit note.  
* Required credit note data is validated before submission.  
* Confirming submission assigns identifiers and sends the credit note to ZATCA as one logical action.  
* No user-visible intermediate state exists where identifiers are locked but the credit note has not been sent.  
* The credit note date locks to the actual submission date.  
* The credit note reference number is assigned using the distinct prefix and overall Business sequence.  
* Credited lines, quantities, values, VAT, reason, notes, and all other details become read-only.  
* Repeating the same submission action does not create a second reference or logical submission.  
* A submitted credit note never returns to Draft.

---

## **CN-13-US02 \- View a Credit Note Awaiting ZATCA**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want a submitted credit note shown as awaiting ZATCA so that I know the correction is pending and cannot be changed.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* After submission, lifecycle status becomes Sent to ZATCA.  
* The status is view-only.  
* No edit, delete, cancel, revert, or resubmit action is available.  
* The credit note remains Sent to ZATCA until a confirmed response is received.  
* Elapsed time alone does not trigger escalation, alert, or status change.  
* The same Sent to ZATCA label is used consistently across credit note list and detail views.  
* The original invoice is not changed while the credit note is awaiting clearance.

---

## **CN-13-US03 \- Handle an Unconfirmed Credit Note Submission**

**User Story**  
As a Business, I want an uncertain credit note submission to remain safely pending so that locked identifiers are never reused or exposed through a false Draft state.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* If APEX cannot confirm whether ZATCA received the credit note, it remains Sent to ZATCA.  
* The credit note does not revert to Draft.  
* Its date, reference number, and identifiers remain locked.  
* The user cannot submit the same credit note again while the outcome is unknown.  
* APEX continues checking for a confirmed outcome.  
* Once confirmed, the credit note transitions once to Cleared or Rejected.  
* Repeated delivery of the same outcome does not apply it more than once.

---

## **CN-13-US04 \- Apply a Cleared Credit Note to the Original Invoice**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want an accepted credit note applied automatically so that the original invoice balance and payment status reflect the legal correction.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* ZATCA acceptance changes the credit note lifecycle status to Cleared.  
* A Cleared credit note is legally effective and permanently read-only.  
* The original invoice outstanding balance is reduced by the credited amount.  
* The original invoice payment status is recalculated against the new balance.  
* An invoice whose remaining unpaid balance is fully covered reflects the resulting accounted-for payment state.  
* The update occurs automatically without a separate user action.  
* Reprocessing the same clearance response does not reduce the balance or recalculate the effect twice.  
* The original invoice and credit note remain linked in both directions.

---

## **CN-13-US05 \- Retain a Rejected Credit Note Without Changing the Invoice**

**User Story**  
As an authorised Business User, I want a rejected credit note retained without affecting the original invoice so that the failed correction remains traceable.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* ZATCA rejection changes the credit note lifecycle status to Rejected.  
* The Rejected credit note remains permanently visible.  
* Its reference number and identifiers are never reused.  
* It is view-only and cannot be edited, deleted, or reverted to Draft.  
* No submit or resubmit action is available.  
* The user must create a separate new credit note from the original invoice when correction is still required.  
* The original invoice outstanding balance remains exactly unchanged.  
* The original invoice payment status remains exactly unchanged.

---

## **CN-13-US06 \- Enforce Credit Note Actions, Download, and Retention**

**User Story**  
As a Business, I want credit note actions governed by lifecycle status so that correction records remain legally reliable.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* Draft allows Edit, Delete, and Submit for clearance.  
* Sent to ZATCA is view-only.  
* Cleared allows Download of the credit note document.  
* Rejected is view-only.  
* A Cleared credit note document can be downloaded with its final locked data.  
* No credit note has its own payment-recording or financing actions.  
* A credit note has no due date or independent payment status.  
* Any credit note that leaves Draft is retained permanently and cannot be deleted by a Business User.  
* Status restrictions cannot be bypassed through direct requests.

---
